Airwindows.description: Universal Airwindows plugin host. Select any plugin from the airwin2rack registry (~340 effects — Chris Johnson's suite, MIT-licensed) and TonePi binds it into the chain via the shared libtp_airwin.so. One block hosts any mono or stereo Airwindows effect; per-plugin controls (1..9 normalised floats labelled A..I in Chris's original naming) are exposed as sliders at chain-build time.
Airwindows.name: Airwindows

params.desc: Airwindows plugin name from the registry.
params.label: Plugin

params.desc: 0 = active, 1 = bypass
params.label: Bypass

Airwindows.usage: Select Plugin: Pick a name from the registry (auto-built at first chain compile from /var/lib/tonepi/airwin_plugins.json). Sliders: The chain compiler emits one slider per plugin parameter, with the plugin's own labels. Latency: 0 samples — per-sample bridge calls the airwin processor with n=1. Mono/Stereo: Stereo plugins receive separate L/R; mono plugins see L only (R mirrored on output). Mix mono/stereo freely in any chain.

params.label: Plugin

params.desc: 0 = active, 1 = bypass
params.label: Bypass

Airwindows / Brightness.usage:
Plugin: Slew
Category: Brightness
I/O: mono (usable in either chain type)
Params: 1

Airwindows / Brightness.description: Universal Airwindows plugin host. Select any plugin from the airwin2rack registry (~340 effects — Chris Johnson's suite, MIT-licensed) and TonePi binds it into the chain via the shared libtp_airwin.so. One block hosts any mono or stereo Airwindows effect; per-plugin controls (1..9 normalised floats labelled A..I in Chris's original naming) are exposed as sliders at chain-build time.

One block hosts any mono or stereo Airwindows effect; per-plugin controls (1..9 normalised floats labelled A..I in Chris's original naming) are exposed as sliders at chain-build time.

Amp.description: American clean amp, classic blackface (Fender Twin Reverb) voicing.  85 W all-tube circuit with 3×12AX7 preamp, passive TMB tonestack, spring reverb, tremolo, 12AT7 LTP phase inverter, push-pull 6L6 power with dynamic sag.  HX41 widened to expose Drive, ChVol, and Presence independently for Helix HD2_AmpUSDoubleNrm A/B parity.
Amp.name: Fender Twin Reverb

params.desc: 0=Normal channel, 1=Vibrato channel.  Maps to Helix HD2_AmpUSDoubleNrm / HD2_AmpUSDoubleVib.  The two channels share the same power section but differ in preamp voicing / spectral balance.
params.label: Channel

params.desc: Preamp gain (V2 plate drive).  0=clean / low headroom, 3.5=Helix-stored Twin default, 7+=push into breakup.
params.label: Drive

params.desc: Channel volume (post-tonestack pot).  ID kept as `volume` for backward-compat with pre-HX41 chains.  8.5=Helix-stored Twin default.
params.label: ChVol

params.desc: TMB tonestack high-shelf.  Highly interactive with Bass (passive Fender topology).
params.label: Treble

params.desc: TMB tonestack midrange.  Twin defaults sit around 5 — low values deepen the iconic mid scoop.
params.label: Mid

params.desc: TMB tonestack low-shelf.  Interactive with Treble — raising Bass softens the Treble slope.
params.label: Bass

params.desc: Power-stage NFB high-shelf at 3.5 kHz, ±5 dB across the range.  Twin defaults sit low (~1).  Independent of Treble.
params.label: Presence

params.desc: Built-in spring reverb.  0=dry, 3=subtle, 10=dripping wet.  Not in Helix HD2_AmpUSDoubleNrm — Helix puts reverb in a separate FX block.
params.label: Reverb

params.desc: Tremolo intensity.  Not in Helix amp model (separate FX).
params.label: Trem Depth

params.desc: Tremolo rate.  Not in Helix amp model.
params.label: Trem Speed

params.desc: 0=normal, 1=bright cap engaged.  Capacitance bypass across ChVol — strongest at low ChVol, vanishes at high ChVol.
params.label: Bright (0/1)

params.desc: Final output trim.  -30=silent, 0=unity, +6=boost.
params.label: Master

Amp.usage: Helix Twin Normal default: Drive=3.5, ChVol=8.5, Treble=5.7, Mid=5.2, Bass=4.4, Presence=1.0. Matches Helix HD2_AmpUSDoubleNrm stored voicing. Clean sparkle: Drive=2, ChVol=4, Treble=7, Mid=5, Bass=4, Presence=3. The Twin's signature. Edge of breakup: Drive=7, ChVol=6, Treble=6, Mid=6, Bass=5. Starts to push. Cranked: Drive=10, ChVol=10, Master=-3dB. Power section compresses. Add a mid-hump OD in front for SRV. Surf: Drive=4, ChVol=4, Reverb=6, Trem Depth=5, Trem Speed=4. Dick Dale territory. Bright switch: Use at low ChVol to restore treble lost by the volume taper. Presence vs Treble: Treble is a passive tonestack shelf around 2-5 kHz; Presence is a power-stage NFB shelf at 3.5 kHz. Use Presence to add edge / cut without changing the tonestack curve.

Amp.description: British hi-fi amp. British hi-fi amp with 4×12AX7 preamp, Baxandall tone stack, EL34 push-pull power, Partridge OT. Gain channel + half-power switch.
Amp.name: Hiwatt T40/20

params.desc: 0=clean, 5=crunch, 10=full overdrive
params.label: Gain

params.desc: Preamp gain. Higher=more tube saturation
params.label: Volume

params.desc: Low frequency shelf. 0=thin, 5=neutral, 10=boomy
params.label: Bass

params.desc: Midrange presence. 0=scooped, 5=flat, 10=forward
params.label: Mid

params.desc: High frequency shelf. 0=dark, 5=neutral, 10=bright
params.label: Treble

params.desc: Power amp HF emphasis. 0=warm, 5=neutral, 10=cutting
params.label: Presence

params.desc: Final output trim. -30=silent, 0=unity, +6=boost
params.label: Master

params.desc: 0=normal, 1=bright cap engaged (more presence at low volume)
params.label: Bright (0/1)

params.desc: 0=full power (tighter), 1=half power (more sag/compression)
params.label: Half Power (0/1)

Amp.usage: Clean headroom: Gain=0, Vol=5. Crystal clean with massive headroom — classic rock guitarist's platform. Mild crunch: Gain=5, Vol=5. Responsive to pick dynamics. classic rock guitarist power chords. Full overdrive: Gain=10, Vol=7. Compressed, harmonically rich. Reduce Master to tame. Half power: Engages more sag and compression at lower volumes. Bedroom cranked tone. Presence: Boost for cutting through a mix, cut for smoother lead tones.

Amp.description: British non-master-volume amp (variant B). Uses circuit-derived JTM45 tonestack (tonestacks.lib) and cubic OT saturation (ef.cubicnl) for more accurate iron-core transformer harmonics. Same preamp triodes and EL34 push-pull power section as variant A.
Amp.name: British NMV Stack B

Brown sound: Jumped=on, Vol I=8, Vol II=6, Treble=7, Mid=5, Bass=4, Presence=6. Clean: Vol I=3, Treble=6, Mid=5, Bass=5. AC/DC: Vol I=6, Treble=7, Mid=5, Bass=3, Presence=7.

Amp.description: British non-master-volume amp 100W NMV stack (v1.9). Dual-channel (Bright I + Normal II) with jumpable inputs. Passive coupled TMB tone stack with bass-treble interaction. ECC83 preamp with cathode bypass shelves (M2/M3), 106Hz input HPF (M1), EL34 push-pull power amp with adjustable sag, 4th-order 7kHz OT rolloff (M5), LF iron core saturation, and presence feedback. Noise gate built in.
Amp.name: Marshall 1959 Super Lead

params.desc: Bright channel volume. Includes bright cap at low settings
params.label: Volume I

params.desc: Normal channel volume. Only active when Jumped=on
params.label: Volume II

params.desc: High shelf. Coupled: bass loading compresses treble gain
params.label: Treble

params.desc: Mid peak/scoop. Depth increases with bass+treble interaction
params.label: Middle

params.desc: Low shelf. Coupled: treble loading shifts bass corner up
params.label: Bass

params.desc: Power amp negative feedback shelf. 0=dark, 5=neutral, 10=cutting

params.label: Jumped (0/1)

params.desc: Output trim. NMV stack has no master volume — this is post-power-amp
params.label: Master

params.desc: Gate threshold. -96=off, -70=light cleanup, -50=aggressive
params.label: Noise Gate

params.desc: 0=tight (modern), 0.3=vintage feel, 0.7=spongy, 1.0=max droop
params.label: Sag

Amp.usage: NMV stack crunch: Vol I=5, Vol II=0, Treble=7, Mid=5, Bass=4, Presence=5. Classic rock crunch. Jumped (Hendrix): Jumped=on, Vol I=7, Vol II=5. Both channels mixed — fat, harmonically rich. Brown sound (EVH): Jumped=on, Vol I=8, Vol II=6, Treble=7, Mid=5, Bass=4, Presence=6. Hot-rodded NMV stack. Classic clean: Vol I=3, Treble=6, Mid=5, Bass=5. Low volume — bright channel sparkle. AC/DC rhythm: Vol I=6, Treble=7, Mid=5, Bass=3, Presence=7. Angus Young territory. Sag: 0=tight, 0.3=vintage feel, 0.7=spongy compression. Models power supply droop under load.

Amp.description: modern pedal amp. 100W pedalboard amp with 3 voices (USA/UK/Flat), 6 power tube responses (KT88–EL84–Linear), 3 power levels (100W/20W/1W).
Amp.name: Blackstar AMPED 1

params.desc: 0=clean, 5=crunch, 10=full overdrive
params.label: Gain

params.desc: Low frequency shelf. 0=thin, 5=neutral, 10=boomy
params.label: Bass

params.desc: Midrange presence. 0=scooped, 5=flat, 10=forward
params.label: Mid

params.desc: High frequency shelf. 0=dark, 5=neutral, 10=bright
params.label: Treble

params.desc: Built-in reverb. 0=dry, 3=subtle, 10=dripping wet
params.label: Reverb

params.desc: Final output trim. -30=silent, 0=unity, +6=boost
params.label: Master

params.desc: 0=American (scooped), 1=British (punchy), 2=transparent
params.label: Voice (0=USA 1=UK 2=Flat)

params.desc: Power tube: 0=KT88(stiff), 1=6L6(full), 2=EL34(middy), 3=6V6(spongy), 4=EL84(chimey), 5=linear
params.label: Response (0=KT88..5=Linear)

params.desc: 0=full power, 1=20W (more sag), 2=1W (bedroom cranked)
params.label: Power (0=100W 1=20W 2=1W)

Amp.usage: USA Clean: Voice=USA, Gain=2, Vol=5. American-style scooped clean. UK Crunch: Voice=UK, Gain=6. British-style punchy midrange drive. Flat + pedals: Voice=Flat, Gain=0. Transparent platform — let your pedals do the work. 6V6 sag: Response=6V6. Warm, spongy, bedroom-cranked feel. Great with single coils. EL84 chime: Response=EL84. Vox-like top-end sparkle and early breakup. 1W mode: Maximum sag and compression at whisper volume. Every note sustains.

Amp.description: Unified neural amp/effect engine — loads NAM .nam profiles and GuitarML .json models with selectable architecture (Auto, LSTM, WaveNet). Reproduces the exact nonlinear response of captured hardware using machine learning inference. Supports up to 8 simultaneous contexts per chain.
Amp.name: Neural Model

params.desc: Model index. Use the model dropdown to select by name.
params.label: Model

params.desc: Inference architecture: 0=Auto (detect from file), 1=LSTM, 2=WaveNet
params.label: Architecture

params.desc: Input gain trim before neural processing
params.label: Input

params.desc: Output gain trim after neural processing
params.label: Output

params.desc: Default=Inline. NAM Process() runs on the audio thread; bit-identical to Worker mode at half the latency (1.33 ms vs 2.67 ms). After the Internal backend + Pi-5 NeuralAudio rebuild (114fe7a) and the slim-Lite split (67c3f8e), a Full WaveNet is ~17% of one core and a Lite is ~3% — leaves plenty of headroom on a single chain. Switch to Worker only when stacking 4+ neural blocks or running alongside a heavy reverb that needs the audio thread.
params.label: Worker Offload

params.desc: Inference is bypassed when the model input falls below this level, with a 5 dB open hysteresis. Default -70 dB matches the captured-amp noise-floor region and saves ~25-30% of one core per slot in inline mode. Raise toward -50 for aggressive silencing of low-level noise; lower toward -120 to effectively disable silence detection (no musical signal ever reaches that floor, so NN runs continuously — useful when A/B-ing the model's own silent-input character).
params.label: Silence Thresh

params.desc: SlimmableContainer A2 files only. Default=Full (1.0 quality scale). Lite picks the 0.5 submodel — smaller WaveNet, ~5x lower CPU, slightly reduced fidelity. Non-Slimmable models ignore this. Set at compile time — change requires recompile.
params.label: Quality

params.desc: High-pass corner after the model — trim sub-bass rumble. 20 Hz = off.
params.label: Low Cut

params.desc: Low-pass corner after the model — tame fizz / harshness. 20 kHz = off.
params.label: High Cut

params.desc: Low shelf at 100 Hz, post-NN. 0 dB = flat.
params.label: Bass

params.desc: Parametric peak at 800 Hz (B=200), post-NN. 0 dB = flat.
params.label: Mid

params.desc: High shelf at 4 kHz, post-NN. 0 dB = flat.
params.label: Treble

params.desc: Wet/dry blend AROUND the entire neural block (input gain + NN + EQ + output gain). 1.0 = fully wet (current behaviour). 0.0 = bypass the model entirely while keeping the block compiled.
params.label: Mix

Amp.usage: Basic use: Select a model from the dropdown. Supports both NAM (.nam) and GuitarML (.json) formats. Architecture: Auto detects the correct engine from the model file. Force LSTM or WaveNet if needed. Input gain: Adjust if the model is too quiet or too hot. Models expect instrument-level input. Output gain: Level-match with the rest of your chain. In a chain: Gate → Drive → Neural Model → IR Cab → Delay → Reverb. Replaces a traditional amp block. Stacking: You can use multiple Neural Model blocks (up to 8 per chain) for creative layering.

Amp.description: Physics-informed high-gain amp + power section with ADAA tube saturation, Marshall WDF tone stack, asymmetric sag, and resonant presence/depth shelves. Three tube types (6L6/EL34/KT88), three channels (Crunch 3-stage / Lead 4-stage / Ultra 5-stage). Transient-driven tightness preserves pick attack at extreme drive.
Amp.name: TonePi HiGain

params.desc: 0=6L6 (American glassy), 1=EL34 (British grunt), 2=KT88 (hi-fi tight)
params.label: Tube

params.desc: 0=Crunch (3 stages), 1=Lead (4 stages), 2=Ultra (5 stages), 3=Insane (6 stages — extra cascade for screaming high-gain leads)
params.label: Channel

params.desc: Per-stage input gain (1× to 2× per stage). Cascades through 3-5 stages — small per-stage drive compounds dramatically
params.label: Drive

params.desc: Transient-driven headroom expansion. Pick attack rides above the saturation knee, sustain stays compressed
params.label: Tightness

params.desc: WDF tone stack bass (audio taper). Interacts with mid + treble exactly like real Marshall
params.label: Bass

params.desc: WDF tone stack mid (linear taper). Strong scoop at center; push to 8+ for forward leads
params.label: Mid

params.desc: WDF tone stack treble (audio taper). High shelf with bass-load interaction
params.label: Treble

params.desc: Power amp HF feedback shelf. 0=dark, 5=neutral, 10=cutting. Resonant peak at the corner (Q=0.85)
params.label: Presence

params.desc: Output transformer resonant shelf. Q>1 produces a peak at fc — the "thump" character not an EQ flat boost
params.label: Depth

params.desc: 0=tight (modern), 5=vintage feel, 10=spongy. Asymmetric: 50ms attack, 300ms release; transients pass untouched
params.label: Sag

params.desc: Post-power-amp output level. Power tube saturation already happened — master is clean trim
params.label: Master

params.desc: 0=fixed (Phase A): manual sliders only. 1=adaptive: tightness tracks playing speed (onset rate), presence tracks input centroid (dark→up, bright→down), and stage-3 h2 coefficient slews to maintain the tube-type harmonic ratio target (3:1 for 6L6/KT88, 2:1 for EL34). All three controls are slew-limited (500 ms / 3 s / 2 s) so they shape feel rather than chase individual notes.
params.label: AutoAdapt

params.desc: Inter-stage pink-noise texture (Phase C). Off = denormal-prevention only (Phase A bit-exact). On = ≈ −66 dBFS pink noise per stage with per-tube spectral shape (EL34 boosts ~1 kHz "air", KT88 cuts for hi-fi smoothness, 6L6 flat); adds tactile "tube life" during sustained notes. Inaudible in isolation, perceptual aliveness in the mix.
params.label: Texture

params.desc: Power-amp broadband hiss floor (Phase C). Off = clean digital silence. On = ≈ −63/−65/−67 dBFS (EL34/6L6/KT88) shaped by the presence biquad so brighter presence → brighter hiss. Gated by an internal env-follower so it collapses with input level — pairs cleanly with a noise_gate2 placed before HiGain.
params.label: AmpHiss

params.desc: Clean post-master output trim, applied after master + HP. The preamp cascade + 2× makeup + presence/depth shelves run the chain ~10 dB hot above dry input even at master=5 (linear 0.5× = −6 dB) — leaving 0 dB of headroom for downstream AG / FX / interface, which forces aggressive limiting and audible pumping. Default −6 dB hands that headroom back without touching any saturation stage; pull lower if you stack heavy post-amp processing, push to 0 dB for the legacy hot output.
params.label: Output

params.desc: Master multiplier across every coupling-cap + cathode-bypass HP. Log-mapped: each unit ≈ 0.2 octave. 5 = unity (use the per-stage CoupSX / CathSX values as-is), 0 = ½× all corners (more bass), 10 = 2× all corners (tighter). Per-stage sliders below let you sculpt by stage; LowCut is the quick global ride.
params.label: LowCut

params.desc: Master multiplier across every Miller-LP corner. Log-mapped: each unit ≈ 0.2 octave. 5 = unity (per-stage Miller defaults from tube_stage.h), 0 = ½× (darker), 10 = 2× (more air). Channel-to-channel darkening (Crunch < Lead < Ultra) is preserved at every slider position.
params.label: Air

params.desc: Dynamic bass tightening — sidechain envelope on the chain input drives the per-stage coupling-HP corner UP during loud playing, RELAXES it during quiet/sustained passages. Models the "corrective NFB / tight switch" found on modern high-gain heads (Mesa Mark V, Diezel Herbert, EVH 5150 III, ENGL Powerball II). 0 = OFF (no dynamic shift, default), 10 = aggressive (+400 Hz HP shift at full envelope). Eliminates cascade-mud during chunking without sacrificing palm-mute weight or sustain bloom.
params.label: BassTight

params.desc: Stage-0 coupling-cap HP corner. Lower = more bass into stage 1 (richer chunk, can muddy at heavy drive); higher = tighter, leaves stage 1 saturating cleaner higher-frequency content. Below 50 Hz the cascade can accumulate sub-audio DC and produce a sub-50 Hz gargle on bass-heavy chords.
params.label: CoupS0

params.desc: Stage-1 coupling-cap HP corner. By this stage the signal is already partially saturated; tightening here reduces inter-stage bass bloom.
params.label: CoupS1

params.desc: Stage-2 coupling-cap HP corner. This is the Crunch tap output; it controls bass extension of the Crunch channel and the bass entering the Lead/Ultra cascade.
params.label: CoupS2

params.desc: Stage-3 coupling-cap HP corner. First gain stage past the WDF tonestack. Higher here = the "modern tight" mod many high-gain heads do via bright caps + tight bass switches.
params.label: CoupS3

params.desc: Stage-4 (Ultra-tap) coupling-cap HP corner. Final stage before Insane; raise to remove residual sub-100 Hz flub from the cascade before it hits stage 5 / the power section.
params.label: CoupS4

params.desc: Stage-5 (Insane-tap) coupling-cap HP corner. Only audible when Channel=Insane. Higher = tighter "no-flub" lead voice.
params.label: CoupS5

params.desc: Stage-0 cathode-bypass HP corner. Companion to CoupS0. Pair them at the same value for a more "symmetrical" stage; spread them for slightly different shelf character.
params.label: CathS0

params.desc: Stage-1 cathode-bypass HP corner.
params.label: CathS1

params.desc: Stage-2 cathode-bypass HP corner.
params.label: CathS2

params.desc: Stage-3 cathode-bypass HP corner.
params.label: CathS3

params.desc: Stage-4 cathode-bypass HP corner.
params.label: CathS4

params.desc: Stage-5 (Insane-tap) cathode-bypass HP corner.
params.label: CathS5

params.desc: Stage-0 Miller-LP corner. Highest in the cascade so the early signal has full top end before the saturator chain darkens it.
params.label: MillerS0

params.desc: Stage-1 Miller-LP corner.
params.label: MillerS1

params.desc: Stage-2 (Crunch-tap) Miller-LP corner. Sets the brightness of the Crunch channel and the brightness of the signal entering the Lead/Ultra/Insane cascade.
params.label: MillerS2

params.desc: Stage-3 (Lead-tap) Miller-LP corner. The post-WDF stage; commonly darker than stage 2 to model real cascaded preamp plate-loading darkness.
params.label: MillerS3

params.desc: Stage-4 (Ultra-tap) Miller-LP corner. Default 9.5 kHz preserves modern high-gain string definition while damping the upper-octave fizz.
params.label: MillerS4

params.desc: Stage-5 (Insane-tap) Miller-LP corner. Default 7.5 kHz — dark singing-lead voice. Only audible when Channel=Insane.
params.label: MillerS5

Amp.usage: Crunch rhythm: Tube=EL34, Channel=Crunch, Drive=5, Tight=4, Mid=6. Vintage British growl. Lead solo: Tube=EL34, Channel=Lead, Drive=7, Tight=6, Mid=7, Pres=6. Sustain-rich singing lead. Cab.description: Two cabinet IRs fed the same signal and panned apart, with NO delay between them. Widens a single mono guitar the way a doubler cannot: the two sides differ in timbre rather than in time, so pick attacks stay coincident and the image survives a mono sum without comb filtering. Built for fast palm-muted rhythm, where any time-based widener smears the chug.

Cab.usage: Start here: two DIFFERENT cabs — one darker, one brighter — Width 1.0, Balance 0. Choosing the pair: difference is the effect. Two 4x12s with the same mic in the same spot give almost no width; a V30 against a Greenback, or a close mic against a room mic, give a lot. MATCH THE ONSET. Captures bake in their own pre-delay, and pairing two that differ puts a time offset back in — the one thing this block exists to avoid. Measured on this rig: V30 Edgy + Mesa 57 are almost uncorrelated (0.02, so very wide) but their impulses arrive 6 samples apart, which combs from about 4 kHz up. A pair whose impulses land on the same sample is worth more than a pair that measures wider. Too wide / hollow in the room: lower Width toward 0.6. It never comb-filters, but a very wide pair can leave the centre thin on a small PA. Going out mono? Width costs nothing — the mono sum is just the two cabs blended. Use Balance to pick which one dominates. One cab too dominant: Balance, not Level — Level moves both.

Cab.usage:
Grid: the cab (Twin 2x12, Princeton 1x10, Creamback 2x12, AC30 Alnico Blue, V30 / Greenback / Mesa 4x12, Deluxe 1x12).
Mic: an index into the grid's mic list (shown by the picker).
Position: 0 = dust cap, 1 = cone edge -- brighter at the cap, darker and fuller toward the edge.
Two mics: their combination is a real comb filter; it is exact at captured positions (0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 on the Twin / Princeton grids) and approximate between them. Align lines up the mics' arrivals.
(derived) mics: not captured on this cab -- built from its own SM57 and the mic's measured character (within the spread between two speakers of one cab).
Speaker Dynamics: off by default. Push sets how hard the amp drives the speaker; Motor adds excursion distortion / IMD on low notes; Thermal is the slow power compression of a hot voice coil.

Tape echo: Mode=Tape, Mod=5. Wow + flutter with saturation (one transport: the mono sum stays whole). Aged tape echo: Mode=Worn Tape, Repeats=6, Filter=4. Darker every pass. Shimmer: Mode=Ice, Pattern=Octave up, Mod=4, Repeats=6. Each repeat climbs another octave in the blend. Reverse swell: Mode=Reverse, Pattern=One head, Time=500ms, Mix=7. Each half-second comes back backwards. Volume-pedal swell: Mode=Swell, Smear=3 (rise ~0.7 s), Mix=8. Every pick's echo fades in from silence. Synced tremolo echo: Mode=Trem, Sync=on, SyncDiv=4, Pattern=Square. Filter sweep echo: Mode=Filter, Repeats=6, Mod=6. A resonant low-pass sweeps the echoes. AM radio echo: Mode=Lo-Fi, Filter=3, Pattern=AM Radio. Mix arithmetic: the wet is Mix/10 of the first echo, linear: Mix 10 = 0 dB, 5 = -6 dB, 2.5 = -12 dB, 1 = -20 dB under the dry.

Note: Slapback caps at ~200 ms; Tape time glides (vd~).

Delay.description: Physical delays: each mode models a real mechanism or place that delays sound -- tape, its heads and its transport; a canyon, its rock, air and ground; the Moon; bucket-brigade chips; a bouncing ball; a garden hose; a can of oil; the sea's tide; sand; a chaotic attractor; Doppler shifts; a space that follows your pitch; a forgetful memory; a ghost that answers your phrase -- so the repeats darken, saturate, smear and wobble from the physics, not from filters and LFOs. Every mode syncs to the TonePi tempo.
Delay.name: TonePi Physical Delay

params.desc: The delaying mechanism. Echoplex EP-3: a loop of oxide tape, a record head on a slide and a fixed playback head, from their physics -- the oxide's particles recorded with a real AC bias (they saturate, and the bias trades highs against distortion as on a real machine), read back through the playback gap (the gap, the head-to-tape spacing and the coating cost the highs: every repeat darkens because it is recorded and read again), the capstan and pinch wheel making the flutter. Moving Time slides the record head along the tape: the pitch swoops as it moves. The EP-3's FET preamp is its input, so it colours the dry too. Mountain Canyon: you and your amp on a grassy valley floor facing a granite cliff -- the echo from its physics: the image of the cliff, its rock scattering by its roughness (each square metre of the face sending back its share, so the echo smears), the air taking the highs over the distance, the grass making distant sound thin in the low mids, and the air's turbulence making the echo fade in and out and wander, as distant sound does on a windy day. A second wall behind you (Repeats) bounces it back and forth. Moonbounce: your guitar on single sideband to the Moon and back, as radio amateurs bounce signals off it: the echo returns 2.4-2.7 s later (the Moon's real distance), from a rough, rocking Moon -- its regions beat against each other as it librates (the echo's flutter, faster on the higher bands), in the hiss your station can dig it out of (the radar equation), on two crossed dipoles that the ionosphere's Faraday rotation pans it between. Deluxe Memory Man: two MN3005 bucket-brigade chips (8192 stages) between their filters, an NE570 compander around them, from the chips' physics -- they sample at their clock (long delays, slow clocks: darker, with aliasing grit), lose a little charge at every transfer, gather noise the longer it waits, leak their clock (a faint whine at the longest delays); the compander keeps the hiss down and makes the repeats breathe. Kinetic: the repeats as a ball dropped on a steel floor -- every landing an echo, each sooner than the last as the ball loses height (its restitution), fading and darkening as the landings soften (the impact's sound and contact time), until it chatters to rest and rolls. Cooper Time Cube: the 1970s studio delay that sent sound down coiled garden hoses to a microphone -- the air dragging on the hose's wall darkens it (and holds the lows back a touch), a soft rubber wall slows and softens it, the ends reflect a little back for faint later repeats; two hoses, left and right (14 and 16 ms on the original). Tel-Ray Oil Can: the echo stored as electric charge on a disc turning in a can of oil, written and read by brushes -- the oil drains the charge and lets it spread (darker, softer repeats), the brushes' contact flickers (grit), the disc runs a little off-centre (the can's watery wobble), and the wiper never quite clears it (a ghost of each echo a turn later). Its medium's values are estimates: none were found measured. Tidal: the echo's time and feedback rise and fall with the sea -- the real tide's five main constituents at their true periods (so it never repeats, and swells between spring and neap tides), run faster, with surf on top. Spectral Erosion: the repeats keep their loudness but lose their frequency density -- each pass drops a random share of the spectrum in grains, so the later repeats thin out and dissolve like sand, and the grains that are left can drift. Entropy: the repeats degrade by real chaos -- a Lorenz attractor runs live and sets the loop's timing wobble, its tone and its grit, deterministic but never repeating; below a threshold it settles (steady, predictable decay), above it, chaos. Doppler: the repeats' pitch follows how you play -- busy, staccato picking makes them approach (higher, blue-shifted), slow legato lets them recede (lower); each repeat shifts again, so they climb or sink. Resonant Mirror: the space the echoes ring in follows your pitch -- low notes stretch it into a huge, slow, booming tube 30 m long, high notes shrink it to a small ringing glass tube; it glides as you move up and down the neck, and old echoes keep the space they were played in. Amnesia: the repeats forget stretches of what you played and fill the holes with guesses -- the last moment they remember, carried on as a blur, drifting in pitch and fading; every repeat can forget again, so old echoes turn into dreams of themselves. Negative Space: silent while you play; when you stop, a ghost answers in the spaces you left -- on the beats your phrase did not use, off-beats first -- either with your own notes re-timed and moved to your phrase's other pitches, or with notes it predicts from your phrase (its key, a counter-melody) on a plucked string (Voice).
params.label: Mode

params.desc: Dry/wet (equal power).
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Delay time. EP-3: the record head's place on its slide, 60-600 ms at the tape's 8 ips; moving it while playing swoops the pitch, as sliding the real head does. Canyon: the cliff's echo, 30 ms - 3 s (5 - 515 m away); the echoes follow it at once (sweeping it moves the cliff: the repeats bend in pitch), the rock's scattered tail a moment later, the echoes already in the air ringing on. Moonbounce: the Moon's distance, 2378 ms (perigee) to 2713 ms (apogee). Memory Man: the clock, 41 ms (100 kHz) to 550 ms (7.4 kHz, below the chip's spec, as the pedal runs it). Kinetic: the first landing, 30 ms to 1.5 s (dropped from 4 mm to 11 m). Time Cube: the left hose, 5-120 ms (1.7-41 m of hose; 14 ms = the original); the right one is 16/14 of it. Oil Can: the motor, 50-350 ms (the read brush a sixth of a turn on). Tidal: the mean time, 30 ms - 2 s (the tide swings it). Erosion: 30 ms - 2 s. Entropy: 30 ms - 2 s. Doppler: 60 ms - 2 s. Mirror: 30 ms - 2 s. Amnesia: 30 ms - 2 s. Negative Space: the beat its grid of eighths is built on, 100 ms - 1.5 s (Sync: the TonePi tempo's beat).
params.label: Time

params.desc: Feedback. EP-3: Sustain -- the playback fed back into the record amp; past ~0.85 the repeats build and run away, held by the tape's own saturation. Canyon: the wall behind you, 1.5x further than the cliff -- 0 = open valley (one echo), 1 = rock as reflective as the cliff: the sound runs back and forth, each pass darker and more smeared. Moonbounce: Relay -- the received echo sent up again (each trip adds the Moon's flutter and the hiss). Memory Man: Feedback, to the edge of runaway. Kinetic: Bounce -- the restitution at 1 m/s, 0.3 (a dead thud, few bounces) to 0.95 (a lively ball, a long accelerando). Time Cube: Feedback (the console's loop around it). Oil Can: Repeat. Tidal: the mean feedback (the tide swings it). Erosion: Feedback (the level stays; the density goes). Entropy: Feedback. Doppler: Feedback (each repeat shifts again). Mirror: Feedback (the trails keep their space). Amnesia: Feedback (each pass can forget more). Negative Space: how long it answers, 1 (0) to 8 (1) cycles of two bars.
params.label: Repeats

params.desc: High cut on the wet (outside the loop).
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Every mode: Time from the TonePi tempo instead of the Time knob, as a division. One the mode cannot reach is taken an octave at a time (halved or doubled) until it fits, so the echo stays on the beat (EP-3 60-600 ms, Canyon 30 ms - 3 s). Moonbounce's range is narrower: the multiple of the division that falls within 2.38-2.71 s. Memory Man: 41-550 ms. Kinetic: the first landing (30 ms - 1.5 s); the bounces after it accelerate, off the beat by nature. Time Cube: 5-120 ms. Oil Can: 50-350 ms. Tidal: the mean time, 30 ms - 2 s. Erosion: 30 ms - 2 s. Entropy: 30 ms - 2 s. Doppler: 60 ms - 2 s. Mirror: 30 ms - 2 s. Amnesia: 30 ms - 2 s. Negative Space: Sync on uses the TonePi tempo's own beat for its grid.
params.label: Sync

params.desc: Mode-specific. EP-3: Bias -- the record head's AC bias, 0.5 = aligned (0 = half, 1 = double): down = brighter but grittier and more distorted (the deep oxide no longer properly biased), up = cleaner and darker (the bias erases the highs). Canyon: Rock -- the face's roughness, 2 mm (0: a polished slab, a clean ringing echo) to 0.4 m (1: broken blocks, a long smeared echo; the highs scatter first). Moonbounce: Band -- 144 MHz (2 m: slow, deep fades), 432 MHz, 1296 MHz (23 cm), 10 GHz (3 cm: a fast, raspy flutter); higher bands also bring the echo out of the hiss for the same dish. Memory Man: Depth -- the LFO sweeping the clock, 0 to +-30 % (chorus at short times, vibrato and seasick pitch at long). Kinetic: Material -- rubber (0: soft, dark echoes), oak, steel (1: bright clicks of the guitar). Time Cube: Ends -- how much the driver and microphone reflect, 0 (matched: one clean slap) to 0.9 (the faint repeats at 3x and 5x the delay). Oil Can: Oil -- fresh (0) to aged (1): it drains and spreads the charge faster: quieter, darker repeats. Tidal: Tide -- how far the water swings them: time +-25 % and feedback +-0.3 at 1. Erosion: Erosion -- the share of the spectrum each pass loses, 0 to 60 %. Entropy: Entropy -- how far the attractor pushes the loop (time +-2 %, tone 3 octaves, drive x5). Doppler: Depth -- the shift at the extremes of your playing, 0 to 12 semitones. Mirror: Range -- how far the space moves with your pitch (0: a fixed mid-size tube; 1: 30 m to 15 cm across the neck). Amnesia: Forget -- each stretch's chance to be forgotten on a pass, 0 to 80 %. Negative Space: Density -- how many of the empty slots it fills (off-beats twice as often).
params.label: Param 1

params.desc: Mode-specific. EP-3: Wear -- the transport's age: capstan and pinch-wheel run-out and speed drift (0 = a fresh machine, 1 = a tired one: seasick). Canyon: Air -- the humidity, 10 % (0) to 90 % (1) at 15 C: how much of the highs the distance takes (dry air takes more). Moonbounce: Station -- the dish, 2 m (0) to 100 m (1), 1 kW: small = the echo barely out of the noise, big = clean. Memory Man: Rate -- the LFO, 0.1 (0) to 8 Hz (1). Kinetic: Ball Size -- 5 mm (0) to 50 mm (1) radius: bigger = darker. Time Cube: Bore -- the hose, 6 mm (0: thin, dark) to 25 mm (1: wide, brighter). Oil Can: Brushes -- their wear: the contact's flicker and dropouts (grit, crackle). Tidal: Period -- the main (M2) tide, 4 s (0) to 2 minutes (1); spring to neap is 28.5 of them. Erosion: Grain -- the size of what goes, 4 (0: fine sand) to 128 bins (1: chunks, 190 Hz to 6 kHz wide). Entropy: Rate -- the attractor's speed (slow drifts to restless flicker). Doppler: Sensitivity -- the pick rate that counts as neutral, 1 (0) to 8 a second (1). Mirror: Resonance -- the tube's ends, from damped (0) to ringing (1). Amnesia: Chunk -- how long a forgotten stretch is, 50 ms (0: flickering) to 1 s (1: whole phrases). Negative Space: Wait -- how long you must be quiet before it answers, 0.1 (0) to 1 s (1).
params.label: Param 2

params.desc: Mode-specific. EP-3: Record Level -- -12 dB (0) to +12 dB (1) into the tape; 0.5 = 3 % distortion at -6 dBFS, the tape's maximum level. Up = the tape saturates and compresses the repeats. Canyon: Turbulence -- the air's, from a still evening (0) to a windy afternoon (1): the echo fades in and out (the highs most, the further the more) and its timing wanders slightly. Moonbounce: Libration -- how fast the Moon appears to rock (0.5 = a typical day): faster = a faster flutter. Memory Man: Drive -- -12 (0) to +12 dB (1) into the chips: up = their bend (2.5 % at 0.9 Vrms) and grit. Kinetic: Floor -- its roughness, 10 um (0: polished: the ball buzzes on to a long rattle) to 3 mm (1: it stops early and rolls). Time Cube: Wall -- copper pipe (0) to soft rubber hose (1): slower, softer, a little darker. Oil Can: Erase -- what the wiper leaves, 5 % (0) to 50 % (1): the ghost a turn later. Tidal: Surf -- the waves on the tide (faster, irregular swells). Erosion: Drift -- the remaining grains slide up or down a step each pass (blown sand: inharmonic, metallic). Entropy: Order -> Chaos -- the attractor's rho: below 0.4 it settles to a steady state; 0.6 the classic chaos (rho 28); beyond, wilder, with periodic windows. Doppler: Glide -- how fast the shift follows you, 50 ms (0) to 2 s (1). Mirror: Glide -- how fast the space follows your pitch, 50 ms (0) to 1 s (1); 0.3 ~ 120 ms. Amnesia: Drift -- how far a guess wanders in pitch as it goes. Negative Space: Voice -- 0: your own notes, re-timed; 1: predicted notes, synthesised (a plucked string); between: a mix, note by note.
params.label: Param 3

params.desc: Wet level.
params.label: Level

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Delay.usage: Placement: after the drive, before or after the amp. Classic EP-3 slapback: Time 90-130 ms, Repeats 0.1-0.2, Mix 0.3. Rhythmic echo: Sync 1/8 dot, Repeats 0.35-0.5, Mix 0.25-0.35. Runaway oscillation: Repeats 0.9-1, then slide Time for the classic swoops. Dirty tape: Record Level 0.7-0.9, Bias 0.3. Seasick: Wear 0.8-1. Mountain echo: Canyon, Time 0.8-1.5 s, Repeats 0, Mix 0.25; Rock 0.3-0.5. Canyon ping-pong: Canyon, Time 0.4-0.7 s, Repeats 0.6-0.9 (the wall behind, at 1.5x: a dotted rhythm). Moon echo: Moonbounce, Band 0.6 (1296 MHz), Station 0.5, Mix 0.3; Sync 1/4 to put it on the beat. Deep space: Moonbounce, Band 0.2 (144 MHz), Station 0.3: the echo emerging from the hiss. Memory Man: Time 300-450 ms, Repeats 0.5, Depth 0.2, Rate 0.3: the classic wobbly analog echo; Depth 0, Time 41-80 ms for slapback. Bouncing ball: Kinetic, Time 0.3-0.6 s, Bounce 0.7-0.85, Material 0.6, Mix 0.3: every phrase answered by a settling ball. Time Cube doubling: Time 14 ms (the original), Mix 0.4, Ends 0.3: a dark, wide double from two hoses; 60-110 ms for a hose slapback. Oil can surf: Oil Can, Time 120-200 ms, Repeat 0.4, Oil 0.4, Brushes 0.4, Mix 0.3. Ebb and flow: Tidal, Time 400-600 ms, Repeats 0.5, Tide 0.5, Period 0.4, Surf 0.2: echoes that swell and recede like the sea. Dissolving: Spectral Erosion, Time 350-500 ms, Repeats 0.7, Erosion 0.4, Grain 0.3, Drift 0.1. Chaotic decay: Entropy, Time 300-500 ms, Repeats 0.7, Entropy 0.6, Rate 0.3, Order -> Chaos 0.6. Red shift: Doppler, Time 350 ms, Repeats 0.5, Depth 0.3, Glide 0.4: fast runs climb away, held notes sink. Shape-shifting space: Resonant Mirror, Time 400 ms, Repeats 0.5, Range 0.8, Resonance 0.6, Glide 0.3. Fading memory: Amnesia, Time 450 ms, Repeats 0.7, Forget 0.3, Chunk 0.4, Drift 0.3. Ghost duet: Negative Space, Sync 1/4, Density 0.6, Wait 0.3, Voice 0 (yourself) or 1 (a predicted counter-melody), Mix 0.5. On the beat: any mode, Sync 1/4 or 1 bar (the TonePi tempo).
