Distortion.description: Craig Anderton's Tube Sound Fuzz, the original CMOS-inverter "tube sound" project (the ancestor of the Red Llama), modelled from its circuit in both published versions. 1977 (Guitar Player, Feb 1977): a 741 x3.7 front end, then two CD4049UB inverters run as linear amplifiers until they saturate, their inputs pulled low by resistors to ground so they clip asymmetrically (strong even harmonics). 1980 (the book Electronic Projects for Musicians): no op-amp, the first inverter's gain set by the Fuzz pot and a Rhythm / Lead switch, both inverters self-biased, and the 100-ohm-fed supply sagging and recovering with the signal. Each inverter is a MOSFET pair, so its transfer curve and output stiffness come from the devices. Matches ngspice of both circuits within 0.15 dB small-signal, 0.05 dB per sine fundamental and 0.01 dB RMS on guitar.
Distortion.name: Anderton Tube Sound Fuzz

params.desc: 1977 version: DIST, a 500k rheostat (linear) into the first inverter, whose 390k feedback sets its gain: x0.8 at 0, its full open-loop gain (~x20 in circuit) at 10. Even 0 is a fuzz -- the second inverter runs near open loop. No effect on the 1980 version
params.label: Dist

params.desc: 1980 version: FUZZ, a 1M rheostat (linear) in the first inverter's feedback: x1 to x11 on Rhythm; on Lead (10M in series) it changes little. No effect on the 1977 version
params.label: Fuzz

params.desc: Volume (10k audio). 5 = unity at the default Dist / Fuzz (each version calibrated); 10 = about +21 dB
params.label: Volume

params.desc: 1980 version: the Rhythm / Lead switch -- 100k or 10M in the first inverter's feedback. Lead is about 4 dB louder, more saturated and darker. No effect on the 1977 version
params.label: Mode

params.desc: 1977: the Guitar Player circuit (741 front end, Dist; AMZ drawing). 1980: the book circuit (Fuzz + Rhythm / Lead, no op-amp)
params.label: Version

Distortion.usage: Guitar Player 1977: Version=1977, Dist=5, Volume=5. Thick, buzzy fuzz at unity level. Gritty edge: Version=1977, Dist=0, Volume=6. The least gain the circuit has -- still a fuzz, but it cleans up with the guitar's volume. Full Dist: Version=1977, Dist=10, Volume=4.5. The first inverter at open-loop gain: saturated, compressed, sustaining. Book Rhythm: Version=1980, Mode=Rhythm, Fuzz=5, Volume=5. Brighter, more open fuzz; Fuzz sets the first inverter's gain (x1 to x11). Book Lead: Version=1980, Mode=Lead, Volume=3.5. The first inverter at near open-loop gain, the 10 pF across its 10M rolling the top off (-3 dB near 5 kHz): a darker, saturated, singing lead (Fuzz does little here).

Distortion.description: Ken Willmott's Differential Distortion (Popular Electronics, August 1995; redesigned by the author in 2014) modelled from his schematics: a low-noise common-emitter stage drives one side of a long-tailed transistor pair whose other base is fed the first stage's own collector voltage, averaged through 470k / 0.01 uF. The pair steers its 40 uA tail from one output to the other, so it clips the moment the signal leaves a ~0.1 V window, and the averaging keeps the window centred on the signal -- a buzzy, compressed square-wave fuzz on a microamp battery drain. The 2014 version adds Gain (negative feedback from the pair back to the first stage), Bias (the pair's offset: symmetric at 10, gated and lopsided toward 0), Tone (a 250k pot across a 2 nF input cap: bass cut toward 0), a Hi Cut switch and the shop drawing's clean output. Version 1995 is the magazine circuit (2N5088 / 2N3906, no controls). Matches ngspice of the same circuits within 0.3 dB small-signal and 0.06 dB per fundamental at large signal.
Distortion.name: Willmott Differential Distortion

params.desc: Gain (VR2 10k linear): its wiper takes Q2's output back into Q1's emitter through 4.7k + 1 uF. 10 = wiper grounded, Q1 fully bypassed, fuzzes earliest; toward 0 the feedback around the pair lowers the gain (about 14 dB less small-signal at 0) -- softer onset, more pick dynamics
params.label: Gain

params.desc: Bias (VR1 10k linear across R2 3.9k): where Q3's averaged reference is tapped. 10 = the pair closest to balance (symmetric clipping, most sensitive); toward 0 the pair is offset by up to ~0.12 V -- gated, sputtering, strong even harmonics until you dig in
params.label: Bias

params.desc: Tone (VR3 250k linear rheostat across the 2 nF input cap C9): 10 = shorted, full range; toward 0 a bass cut below ~300 Hz (about -7 dB at 0) -- the author's input high-pass
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Hi Cut switch: C7 0.022 uF from the fuzz output to ground (with R9 4.7k, a 1.5 kHz roll-off). 2014 fuzz output only
params.label: Hi Cut

params.desc: Output switch (the 2014 shop drawing's S4): Fuzz = Q3's collector through C6; Clean = Q1's emitter through R7 2.7k + C3 0.1 uF (a buffered clean signal, 3.5 dB below the input on the real pedal, levelled here to unity)
params.label: Output

params.desc: 2014: the author's redesign (MMBT9014 / MMBT9015, the controls above). 1995: the Popular Electronics original -- 2N5088 with 1M / 100k bias and an unbypassed 6.2k emitter, 2N3906 pair, output from a 1k collector load (11 dB quieter on the real thing, levelled here to unity); the knobs and switches do nothing in this version
params.label: Version

Distortion.usage: Stock: Gain=5, Bias=5, Tone=5. The 2014 pedal at noon: buzzy, compressed fuzz at unity. Full fuzz: Gain=10, Bias=10, Tone=10. Emitter fully bypassed, the pair at its most balanced, full bass: fuzzes on the lightest touch, longest sustain. Sputter: Gain=5, Bias=0, Tone=5. The pair offset to one side: quiet notes gate and split, hard picking breaks through lopsided (strong 2nd harmonic). Smooth lead: Gain=7, Bias=8, Tone=7, Hi Cut on. C7 rolls the buzz off above 1.5 kHz. Thin and cutting: Gain=6, Bias=7, Tone=0. The 2 nF input cap alone: bass shelved down about 7 dB below ~300 Hz. Clean: Output=Clean. The shop drawing's clean tap from Q1's emitter (a buffer, levelled to unity). 1995 original: Version=1995. The magazine circuit as published: no controls, harsher.

Distortion.description: Boss DS-1 (the DS-1A circuit, 1994 on), modelled from its schematic: the 2SC2240 transistor booster (~35 dB) that clips by itself and shifts its own bias on a hard pick -- the source of the DS-1's even harmonics --, the LM2904 gain stage (Distortion, x1 to x22), 1N4148 hard clipping to the bias, and the Big Muff-style tone stack with its mid scoop. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.4 dB small-signal below 10 kHz, 0.3 dB per fundamental and 0.1 dB RMS on guitar.
Distortion.name: Boss DS-1

params.desc: Distortion (VR1 100k linear): the op-amp gain, x1 at 0 to x22.3 at 10. The booster stage clips on its own even at 0
params.label: Dist

params.desc: Tone (VR3 20k linear): blends the low-pass and high-pass halves of the tone stack. 0 = dark, 10 = bright, 5 = the mid scoop
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Level (VR2 100k linear). 5 = unity at Dist 5, Tone 5
params.label: Level

Distortion.usage: Classic DS-1: Dist=5, Tone=5, Level=5. The orange box: crunchy, scooped, unity level. Hard rock rhythm: Dist=7, Tone=4, Level=5. Thicker, a little darker. Cutting lead: Dist=9, Tone=7, Level=6. Full gain, bright for single notes. Into a clean amp: Dist=6, Tone=5, Level=6. The DS-1 as the amp's dirt. Boost a dirty amp: Dist=1, Tone=6, Level=8. Even at zero the booster stage still adds bite.

Distortion.description: Electro-Harmonix Hot Tubes (EH-3075, 1978), modelled from the factory schematic: an RC4558 buffer and x3.75 stage, then CD4049UB CMOS inverters run as linear amplifiers until they saturate -- the Overdrive stage, a second inverter at near open-loop gain into the tone stack, and an output inverter that clips too. Each inverter is a MOSFET pair, self-biased low in the 8.4 V supply, so it clips softly and asymmetrically (strong even harmonics) and its output stiffens as it saturates. Big Muff-style Tone control, or the tone switch's raw bypass path. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.1 dB small-signal below 8 kHz, 0.05 dB per fundamental and 0.01 dB RMS on guitar.
Distortion.name: EHX Hot Tubes

params.desc: Overdrive (2M rheostat, reverse-audio "C" taper): the first inverter's input resistor, 2M at 0 to 8.2k at 10 -- x0.07 to x12. The second inverter adds ~x13 of its own, so even low settings clip on a hard pick
params.label: Overdrive

params.desc: Tone (10K linear): Big Muff-style blend of the low-pass (237 Hz) and high-pass (1.3 kHz) halves. 0 = dark, 10 = bright, 5 = the mid scoop. No effect with the tone switch on Bypass
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Volume (10K audio). 5 = unity at Overdrive 5, Tone 5; 10 = about +21 dB
params.label: Volume

params.desc: Tone: the tone stack and its x6.7 inverter. Bypass: a plain x2.3 inverter instead -- rawer, about 3 dB louder
params.label: Tone Switch

Distortion.usage: Classic Hot Tubes: Overdrive=5, Tone=5, Volume=5. Thick, warm saturation at unity level. Warm crunch: Overdrive=3, Tone=4, Volume=6. Edge-of-breakup -- the Hot Tubes has a lot of gain even low on the knob. Raw, tone bypassed: Overdrive=6, Tone switch=Bypass, Volume=4.5. No tone stack: brighter, more mids, more aggressive. Singing lead: Overdrive=9, Tone=6, Volume=5. Full saturation, long sustain. Dark saturation: Overdrive=8, Tone=2, Volume=5.5. The low-pass half of the tone stack: fat and woolly.

Distortion.description: Electro-Harmonix Muff Fuzz -- the 1970s LM1458 op-amp Muff, not the Big Muff Pi -- modelled from its schematic: an x4.7 inverting stage that rails on a hot pick, then an x47 inverting stage with a diode pair in its feedback (1N34A germanium in the early units, 1N4148 silicon later) and a 100 pF cap that rolls the fuzz off above 3.4 kHz. One knob: Volume. Soft, compressed, rounded fuzz with a 159 Hz low cut; the 1458's bias current offsets the diodes slightly, so the clipping is a touch lopsided. Matches ngspice of the same circuit within 0.1 dB small-signal, 0.1 dB per fundamental and 0.1 dB RMS on guitar.
Distortion.name: EHX Muff Fuzz

params.desc: Volume (100k, audio taper assumed). 5 = unity with the 1N34A diodes; 10 = +21 dB
params.label: Volume

params.desc: Which clipping diodes D1/D2 the unit has: 1N34A germanium in the early units (softer, lower clipping level), 1N4148 silicon later (about 9 dB louder, harder edges). Not a switch on the pedal -- the version
params.label: Diodes

Distortion.usage: Early Muff: Volume=5, Diodes=1N34A. The germanium version: soft, dark, compressed, unity level. Late Muff: Volume=3, Diodes=1N4148. Silicon clips 0.3 V higher: about +9 dB at the same Volume (3 is near unity), brighter and harder. Push the amp: Volume=7, Diodes=1N34A. The fuzz hitting a clean amp's input harder. Quiet texture: Volume=3, Diodes=1N34A. Fuzz under a band at a lower level.

Distortion.description: Electro-Harmonix Big Muff Pi (the '76-'77 red/black NYC version 3), modelled from its schematic: the input booster, two transistor clipping stages with 1N914 pairs in their feedback (each band-limited by its Miller cap), the passive tone stack's ~1 kHz scoop and the output recovery stage, solved as one circuit so the Sustain pot and the tone stack load their neighbours as on the real board. Matches ngspice of the full schematic within ~0.5 dB.
Distortion.name: EHX Big Muff Pi

params.desc: 0=some dynamics, 5=moderate fuzz, 10=infinite sustain wall
params.label: Sustain

params.desc: 0=dark/bassy, 5=balanced, 10=bright/treble
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Volume (100k). 5 = unity at Sustain 5.
params.label: Volume

Distortion.usage: classic rock guitarist lead: Sustain=7, Tone=3, Vol=5. Dark, singing, sustain for days. Mascis buzzsaw: Sustain=8, Tone=7, Vol=6. Bright, aggressive, wall of fuzz. alt-rock band: Sustain=9, Tone=5, Vol=5. Balanced, thick, Siamese Dream. Bass fuzz: Sustain=6, Tone=2, Vol=7. Full bottom, dark top. Works great on bass. Pair with mid boost: The 4-stage fuzz scoops mids — stack a mid-hump OD or EQ to fill the gap in a band mix.

Distortion.description: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (Arbiter England, two AC128 germanium PNPs), modelled from its schematic: Q1 and Q2 direct-coupled with R4's feedback from Q2's emitter, both transistors full Gummel-Poon devices with germanium leakage and charge storage, solved together at 4x -- so its bias moves under the signal the way the circuit's does: soft asymmetric clipping on a light touch, square at full Fuzz, cleaning up as you play softer. Matches ngspice of the ElectroSmash schematic within 0.25 dB small-signal, 0.25 dB per fundamental and 0.01 dB RMS on guitar. Input: the Fuzz Face's input impedance is only 0.5-8 k (it falls as Fuzz goes down), so what drives it is half the sound -- Single coil / Humbucker put a pickup's resistance and inductance in front of it (darker, softer, cleans up more), Buffer an ideal source (a buffered pedal before it: brighter, harsher, more gain).
Distortion.name: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face

params.desc: Fuzz (1k linear at Q2's emitter, wiper to the 20u bypass cap): 0 = the 1k fully in the emitter (more feedback, less gain), 10 = emitter fully bypassed
params.label: Fuzz

params.desc: Volume (500k audio). 5 = unity at Fuzz 5 with the single-coil input; 10 = +21 dB
params.label: Volume

params.desc: Internal trim: Q2's collector voltage (the R3 trimmer builders fit; stock 8.2k gives 4.4 V). 4.5 V = the classic setting. Q2's current is set by Q1 through the feedback, so the trim only moves where Q2 clips: lower = it saturates sooner (lopsided, quieter, strong 2nd harmonic), higher = more swing before it does (louder, more symmetric)
params.label: Bias

params.desc: What drives the jack: Buffer = an ideal source (a buffered pedal or a DI before it), Single coil = 6k + 2.5 H, Humbucker = 8.5k + 4 H in series with the signal. The Fuzz Face loads the pickup with 0.5 k (Fuzz 0) to 8 k (Fuzz 10)
params.label: Input

Distortion.usage: Hendrix: Fuzz=10, Volume=6, Input=Single coil. Full fuzz into a clean amp; roll the guitar back for the clean-up. Classic noon: Fuzz=5, Volume=5. Asymmetric, touch-sensitive, unity level. Gilmour lead: Fuzz=8, Volume=6, Input=Single coil. Thick and singing. Low-gain grit: Fuzz=2, Volume=6. Soft asymmetric crunch that follows the pick. Low bias: Fuzz=8, Bias=3.5 V. Q2 hits saturation early: lopsided, compressed, more 2nd harmonic. After a buffer: Input=Buffer, Fuzz=7, Volume=4. The harsh "fuzz after a tuner" sound.

Distortion.description: Heathkit TA-28 Fuzz (the late-60s Heathkit 'Distortion Booster' kit), modelled from its schematic (AMZ, verified against an original): a silicon NPN (2N3391) direct-coupled to a silicon PNP on ONE 1.5 V penlight cell, ~+48 dB of gain between rails 1.5 V apart, so it squares off on any pickup -- a buzzy, near-square fuzz. A passive tone blend after it fades from a dark, flat end to a 7 kHz high-pass that differentiates the square into spiky buzz. Both transistors are full Gummel-Poon devices with their junction capacitances, solved together at 4x. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.22 dB small-signal, 0.24 dB per sine fundamental and 0.01 dB RMS on guitar. The real unit has no volume control and is ~12 dB quieter than bypass; here Distortion 5 / Tone 5 is unity.
Distortion.name: Heathkit TA-28 Fuzz

params.desc: Distortion (the 50k input pot, the kit's 'distortion degree'; audio taper assumed -- the schematic does not mark it): how much of the guitar reaches Q1. 0 = only the 3.3k leg (6 %), 10 = all of it. The gain is fixed at ~+48 dB, so this sets how hard it squares, with output level moving only ~3 dB
params.label: Distortion

params.desc: Tone (50k blend, linear assumed): 0 = the 6.8k / 1k divider end (full range, darkest), 10 = the 0.022u / 1k end (a 7 kHz high-pass: thin, spiky buzz). In between it mixes the two through the pot
params.label: Tone

Distortion.usage: Kit default: Distortion=5, Tone=5. The TA-28's square buzz at unity. Full fuzz: Distortion=10, Tone=5. All of the guitar into the pair: hardest square, most sustain, about +1 dB. Dark wool: Distortion=7, Tone=0. The flat 6.8k / 1k end: thick and woolly, about +4.5 dB over the default. Buzzsaw: Distortion=10, Tone=10. The 0.022u high-pass end: the square's edges as spikes -- thin, ripping, cuts through anything. Low-degree grit: Distortion=0, Tone=5. Only the 3.3k leg of the input pot feeds the pair (6 %): still a fuzz (the gain is that high), but it clips later and less square, about -2 dB. The Distortion knob mostly sets how early and how square it clips, not level (the output is set by the 1.5 V rails); Tone moves level by about 4 dB end to end.

Distortion.description: Ibanez SD-9 Sonic Distortion (1982), modelled from its schematic: a Tube Screamer cousin with the clipping moved. The JRC4558 gain stage (x71 to x600 above ~1.5 kHz, falling 6 dB per octave below it: about x23 at 100 Hz at noon) is driven into its own rails, then 1N914 diodes clip hard to ground after it -- RAT / DS-1 style -- into a Big Muff-style tone stack. Tight lows, a raw upper-mid bark. Matches ngspice of the circuit within 0.16 dB small-signal, 0.04 dB per fundamental and 0.01 dB RMS on guitar.
Distortion.name: Ibanez Sonic Distortion

params.desc: Distortion (250k linear in series with 33k): gain above ~1.5 kHz from x71 at 0 to x600 at 10 (into the op-amp rails); below ~1.5 kHz the gain falls 6 dB per octave
params.label: Distortion

params.desc: Tone (20k): blends the low-pass and high-pass halves of the tone stack. 0 = dark, 10 = bright, 5 = the mid scoop
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Level (100k linear). 5 = unity at Distortion 5, Tone 5
params.label: Level

Distortion.usage: Classic SD-9: Distortion=5, Tone=5, Level=5. Crunchy, mid-forward, unity level. Tight rhythm: Distortion=7, Tone=4, Level=5. Palm mutes stay tight: the bass gets far less gain than the mids. Lead: Distortion=9, Tone=6, Level=6. Full gain, a little brighter for single notes. Dark and thick: Distortion=6, Tone=2, Level=6. The low-pass half of the tone stack. Edge of breakup: Distortion=0, Tone=6, Level=4. Still x71 above 1.5 kHz: crunch on the pick attack.

Distortion.description: Maestro Fuzz-Tone FZ-1 (1962, the 'Satisfaction' fuzz) and FZ-1A (1965), modelled from their schematics: three germanium PNP transistors biased by nothing but their own leakage, on a 3 V (FZ-1) or 1.5 V (FZ-1A) supply. Q1 buffers, Q2 and Q3 sit near cutoff and only switch on when the string swings far enough -- the gated, sputtery, brassy square wave -- and the coupling caps charging on each note give the slow swell at low Attack. A 3.3 nF 'differentiating' output makes it thin and buzzy. Matches ngspice of the same circuits within 0.23 dB small-signal, 0.27 dB per fundamental at large signal and 0.07 dB RMS on guitar.
Distortion.name: Maestro FZ-1 Fuzz-Tone

params.desc: Volume (FZ-1 500k, FZ-1A 50k, audio taper) after the 3.3n output cap. 5 = unity at Attack 7; 10 is about +21 dB
params.label: Volume

params.desc: Attack (50k audio rheostat across Q2's 22k base resistor): how far the leakage biases Q2 on. 0 = gated and slow (notes swell in, sputter, cut off), 10 = fastest attack and most sustain -- as the Maestro manual says, 'at zero the attack is slowest, at ten it is fastest'
params.label: Attack

params.desc: FZ-1 (1962): 2N270s, 3 V, 20u couplings, 1.5k Q2 collector, 56k || 500k output. FZ-1A (1965): 2N2613s, 1.5 V, 1u couplings, 470k bias to Q2, 10k Q2 collector, 50k output -- each the full component set of its schematic
params.label: Version

Distortion.usage: Satisfaction: FZ-1, Attack=8, Volume=4.5. The 1965 riff: square, brassy, near unity. Full fuzz: FZ-1, Attack=10, Volume=4.5. Maestro's own chart for tuba / sax: fastest attack, most sustain. Brass swell: FZ-1, Attack=6, Volume=6. Notes bloom in after the pick instead of starting on it -- the horn imitation it was sold for. Sputter gate: FZ-1, Attack=4, Volume=9. Only hard picking gets through; decays break up and cut off. FZ-1A: Version FZ-1A, Attack=7, Volume=5. One 1.5 V cell, 1u couplings: tighter, less swell, softer gating. Play single notes on the lower strings (Maestro's own advice); chords turn to intermodulation mush.

Distortion.description: The Big Muff Pi circuit in six versions, each the full component set of one traced schematic, checked against ngspice: the 2000 NYC reissue (Kit Rae, V9 1st version), a '73 Ram's Head (V2 73 #3), the most common Triangle (V1 67 #1), the '76-'77 NYC Pi (ElectroSmash's V3), the green Sovtek Russian (V7B/7C) and a '76 Ram's Head with Kit Rae's mids switch on flat.
Distortion.name: EHX Big Muff Pi (Versions)

params.desc: 0=some dynamics, 5=moderate fuzz, 10=infinite sustain wall
params.label: Sustain

params.desc: 0=dark/bassy, 5=balanced, 10=bright/treble
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Volume (100k). 5 = unity at Sustain 5.
params.label: Volume

params.desc: 0 NYC reissue (2000, Schottky diodes), 1 Ram's Head ('73, smooth), 2 Triangle ('71 most common V1), 3 NYC Pi ('76-'77 V3), 4 Green Russian (Sovtek, warm, lower gain), 5 flat mids ('76 Ram's Head, mids switch flat) -- each the full component set of a traced schematic.
params.label: Version

Distortion.usage: Smooth (classic rock guitarist): Mode=1, Sus=7, Tone=3. Dark, scooped, smooth lead. Triangle (bassy): Mode=2, Sus=6, Tone=5. Original 1969 growl. Cuts through. Pi (Corgan): Mode=3, Sus=9, Tone=5. Hardest clipping, maximum aggression. Russian (warm): Mode=4, Sus=7, Tone=4. Garage fuzz, mushy, warm. Mid Forward (bright): Mode=5, Sus=5, Tone=6. Almost distortion-like, less gain. boutique (modern): Mode=0, Sus=7, Tone=5. Most dynamic, best for bass.

Distortion.description: MXR Distortion+ (M-104), modelled from its circuit: a 741 op-amp in a non-inverting stage (Distortion: x2 to x213, the bass below 3..720 Hz left at unity) with the 741's own limits -- 1 MHz gain-bandwidth (the top rolls off above ~5 kHz at full gain), 0.5 V/us slew, output 1 V short of each 9 V rail, and its input bias current, which makes it rail asymmetrically (even harmonics) --, then 1N270 germanium diodes to ground behind 10k: soft, low (~0.25 V) clipping. No tone control. Matches ngspice of the schematic within 0.05 dB small-signal and per fundamental, 2 dB on every harmonic above -50 dBc.
Distortion.name: MXR Distortion+

params.desc: Distortion (1M reverse audio rheostat in the gain leg): op-amp gain x2 at 0, x11 at 5, x213 at 10. More gain also thins the bass going into the diodes
params.label: Distortion

params.desc: Output (10k audio). 5 = unity at Distortion 5; 10 is +21 dB
params.label: Output

Distortion.usage: Classic Distortion+: Dist=5, Output=5. Mild, fuzzy crunch at unity level. Edge of breakup: Dist=2, Output=6. Germanium softness on a clean amp; dig in for grit. Seventies lead: Dist=8, Output=5. Saturated, compressed, singing. Full tilt: Dist=10, Output=4. The 741 rails into the diodes: fuzzy, with the even-harmonic edge. Dirty amp boost: Dist=3, Output=8. Mid-forward push into an already driven amp.

Distortion.description: Peavey's 1980s solid-state amp distortion -- the ganged Saturation control, Jack Sondermeyer's US patent 4,405,832 (1983), the 'Peavey Tube-Sound Distortion' on AMZ -- modelled from the patent's circuit and run as a pedal. One op-amp: at Saturation 0 a plain x100 stage (bass rolled off below ~500 Hz) that hard-clips on its +-13.5 V rails; turning Saturation up adds a tee in the feedback that lifts the mids to a +64 dB bell around 1 kHz, while the same gang pans the output from the op-amp's rail-clipped signal over to a pair of silicon diodes. Volume is the patent's FIG. 6 control: it lowers the gain and the output together. Matches ngspice of the circuit within 0.15 dB small-signal and 0.1 dB per fundamental.
Distortion.name: Peavey Saturation (Tube-Sound Distortion)

params.desc: Saturation (ganged 10k + 1k, linear -- the patent gives no taper): 0 = the x100 stage straight out (rail clipping only); up adds the R5/R4 tee (a mid bell up to +64 dB at ~1 kHz) and pans the output to the diode-clipped side. Output level drops as it goes up.
params.label: Saturation

params.desc: FIG. 6 Volume (10k, wiper grounded, linear assumed): 10 = full gain; turning it down raises the op-amp's ground-leg resistance (less gain) and shunts the output at once. 10 = unity at Saturation 5.
params.label: Volume

params.desc: Footswitch 28 on point A. On = grounded (saturation in). Off = lifted: no added gain, the diodes out of circuit (they still conduct a little in series with R4 at high levels).
params.label: Footswitch

Distortion.usage: Classic Saturation: Saturation=5, Volume=10. Mid-heavy crunch, unity level. Raw rail crunch: Saturation=0, Volume=10. Just the op-amp hitting its rails: a bright, square-edged fuzz on the pick. Full saturation: Saturation=10, Volume=10. The 1 kHz bell into the diodes: smooth, compressed lead tone (quieter than noon). Lower gain: Saturation=5, Volume=6. Volume also cuts the op-amp's gain: less distortion and less level. Footswitch off: Footswitch=Off. Point A lifted: no added gain and the diodes out of circuit -- the x100 stage alone.

Distortion.description: ProCo RAT (RAT2), modelled from its circuit: the LM308 with its 30 pF compensation cap (0.5 MHz gain-bandwidth, 0.2 / 0.29 V/us slew) inside its frequency-shaping feedback network (bass thinned before clipping, gain falling at high frequency at high Distortion), 1N914 diodes to ground, the Filter RC (475 Hz .. 32 kHz) and the 2N5458 output follower. Matches ngspice of the ElectroSmash schematic within 0.1 dB small-signal and 1 dB per harmonic (test/spice/rat).
Distortion.name: ProCo RAT 2

params.desc: Op-amp gain into clipping. 0=light breakup, 5=crunch, 10=saturated fuzz
params.label: Distortion

params.desc: Post-clip LP. 0=full treble (bright), 10=dark (cut HF). Reversed from most pedals
params.label: Filter

params.desc: Volume (100k audio taper). 5 = unity at Distortion 5.
params.label: Volume

Distortion.usage: Classic Rat: Dist=5, Filter=5, Vol=7. Mid-gain crunch with balanced tone. Thick fuzz: Dist=8, Filter=3, Vol=6. High gain, dark — almost fuzz territory. Bright bite: Dist=4, Filter=8, Vol=7. Lower gain, lots of treble — cutting lead. Into clean amp: Dist=6, Filter=5, Vol=8. The Rat IS the amp sound. Stacking: Dist=3, Filter=6, Vol=8 into a dirty amp. Tightens and adds edge.

Distortion.description: Jack Orman's Rex's Fuzz (AMZ, 1995) modelled from its schematic: a dual op-amp fuzz in the Muff Fuzz family. An x10 inverting stage that rails on a hot pick, then an inverting stage whose feedback is 10k plus the 1M Drive pot (x1 to x101) shunted by a 1N914 diode pair and 51 pF -- the diodes hold the output near +-0.6 V, so Drive sets how early and how square it clips (and, at the top, a 3 kHz roll-off). Volume is a 10k pot after it. Op-amp not named on the drawing: a 4558 is assumed. Matches ngspice of the same circuit within 0.1 dB small-signal, 0.1 dB per fundamental and 0.01 dB RMS on guitar.
Distortion.name: Orman Rex's Fuzz

params.desc: Drive (1M rheostat in series with 10k in stage 2's feedback, audio taper assumed): x1 to x101 into the 1N914 pair
params.label: Drive

params.desc: Volume (10k, audio taper assumed). 5 = unity at Drive 5; 10 = +21 dB
params.label: Volume

Distortion.usage: Rex: Drive=5, Volume=5. The stock setting: compressed op-amp fuzz, unity level. Low drive grit: Drive=1, Volume=5. Stage 2 near x1: picks dynamics through, softer clipping (about 2 dB quieter). Full fuzz: Drive=10, Volume=5. x101 into the diodes with the 51p roll-off at 3 kHz: square, darker, sustaining. Push the amp: Drive=7, Volume=7. The fuzz hitting a clean amp's input harder (about +9 dB).

Distortion.description: Jack Orman's '60s Style Fuzz Box (AMZ, 1995), modelled from its schematic: a silicon emitter follower behind a 100k input resistor, the Fuzz pot feeding a germanium PNP that the bias divider holds in saturation, and a silicon switch after it. At rest nothing passes; a note only comes through when the string swings the germanium stage out of saturation, and then it is a full square wave -- a hard, sputtering, gated 60s fuzz. Fuzz sets how much of the signal reaches that stage, i.e. the gate threshold: on a normal pickup only the top of its range opens the gate (Fuzz 8.5 is still ~30 dB below Fuzz 10); with a hot pickup or a boost in front, lower settings open too. The germanium base also rectifies into its coupling cap on hard picking, so the threshold breathes with the playing. Matches ngspice of the same circuit within 0.6 dB small-signal, 0.2 dB per fundamental away from the gate threshold and 4.9 dB worst harmonic on sines.
Distortion.name: Jack Orman '60s Style Fuzz Box

params.desc: Fuzz (5k pot, taper unmarked -- linear assumed): how much of Q1's output reaches the saturated germanium stage, i.e. the gate threshold. 10 = the gate opens on a normal pickup's notes; below ~9 a normal pickup barely gets through (a hotter input opens it again)
params.label: Fuzz

params.desc: Volume (10k "Vol.", audio taper assumed) after the 5u output cap. 5 = unity at Fuzz 10; 10 is about +21 dB
params.label: Volume

Distortion.usage: Full fuzz: Fuzz=10, Volume=5. The gate wide open on a normal pickup: square, buzzy, sputtering decays, unity level. Loud: Fuzz=10, Volume=8. About +12 dB: pushing a clean amp. Sputter: Fuzz=9.6, Volume=7. Right at the threshold (about unity): only hard picking gets through, notes choke and break up as they decay. After a boost: Fuzz=6, Volume=5. With a +12 dB boost (or a very hot pickup) in front a lower Fuzz opens the gate; about unity re the boosted signal. Play single notes on the lower strings; chords collapse to a square-wave buzz.

Drive.description: EP-3-style JFET preamp boost, modelled from its circuit: one 2N5457 common-source stage on an 18 V rail, Boost as the source degeneration (the dB on the knob is the small-signal gain). Clean up to ~+19 dB with the JFET's soft even-harmonic squash on hot picking. Bright DIP: a cap across the degeneration (treble keeps full gain); Bass DIP: a larger bypass cap.
Drive.name: Xotic EP Booster

params.desc: Small-signal gain at 1 kHz. 0 = unity; tops out near +19 dB (the stage at full bypass)
params.label: Boost

params.desc: 0=normal, 1=bright cap engaged (more presence at low volume)
params.label: Bright (0/1)

params.desc: 0 = 2.2u bypass (the boost thins below ~100 Hz), 1 = 10u (full-range boost)
params.label: Bass (0/1)

Drive.usage: Always-on magic: Boost=3-6dB. The EP-3 coloring fattens everything subtly. Amp push: Boost=12-15dB. Drive your amp harder with the EP-3's warm character. Bass switch: Thickens single coils. Combined with the built-in bass warmth = very full. Bright switch: Compensates for dark pickups or long cables. Opens up the top end. Stacking: EP Booster before a mid-hump overdrive or transparent adds body and warmth to the drive.

Drive.description: Tube Screamer drive and Uni-Vibe in one box, both modelled from their circuits. Drive: the TS clipping stage and tone circuit (Green = the stock 720 Hz mid hump; Red = the full-range 220n mod). Vibe: four LDR phase-shift stages with the Uni-Vibe's staggered caps (15n / 220n / 470p / 4.7n) under one lamp -- the lopsided CdS pulse (fast attack, slow decay); Chorus = dry + phased, Vibrato = phased only. Mono in, mono out, like the pedal.
Drive.name: Eventide Riptide

params.desc: 0=clean, 5=moderate crunch, 10=heavy overdrive
params.label: Drive

params.desc: 0=dark (800Hz), 5=balanced (3.8kHz), 10=bright (6.8kHz)
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Output volume. Squared taper for natural feel
params.label: Level

params.desc: 0=Green (TS-style mid-hump), 1=Red (full-range smooth OD)
params.label: Drive Voice (0=Green 1=Red)

params.desc: Vibe depth. Chorus mode: wet/dry mix. Vibrato mode: effect depth
params.label: Vibe

params.desc: 0=slow throb (0.3Hz), 5=medium (4.8Hz), 10=fast warble (9.3Hz)
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Allpass stage frequency spread. 0=narrow notch, 10=wide sweeping notch
params.label: Intensity

params.desc: 0=Green (300-1500Hz classic Shin-ei), 1=Red (150-3000Hz deeper sweep)
params.label: Vibe Voice (0=Green 1=Red)

params.desc: 0=Chorus (dry+phased swish), 1=Vibrato (100% phased pitch wobble)
params.label: Vibe Mode (0=Chorus 1=Vibrato)

params.desc: 0=Drive then Vibe (cleaner mod), 1=Vibe then Drive (animated fuzzy throb)
params.label: Order (0=Drv>Vibe 1=Vibe>Drv)

params.desc: 0=bypass drive, 1=drive active
params.label: Drive On (0/1)

params.desc: 0=bypass vibe, 1=vibe active
params.label: Vibe On (0/1)

Drive.usage: Classic Uni-Vibe: DriveOn=off, VibeOn=on, Vibe=7, Speed=5, Intensity=5, Mode=Chorus. Pure Hendrix throbbing. Vibrato mode: Mode=Vibrato, Vibe=8. Pure pitch wobble, no dry signal — warped vinyl feel. Green drive: DriveOn=on, Drive=5, Tone=5. Mid-hump TS-style crunch. Red drive: DriveVoice=Red, Drive=6. Fuller range smooth overdrive. Vibe into drive: Order=Vibe>Drive. Vibe modulation hits the drive — more animated, fuzzy throb. Drive into vibe: Order=Drive>Vibe (default). Cleaner modulation on distorted signal. Red vibe + Red drive: Both Red, full combo. Deep sweep + smooth OD = massive sound.

Drive.description: Electro-Harmonix LPB-1 Linear Power Booster, modelled from its schematic (AMZ): one common-emitter silicon transistor (2N5088, the 2N5133 class of the first units) with an unbypassed 360 ohm emitter -- a flat ~+27 dB -- straight into the 100k audio Volume pot, no buffer. Clean at normal picking; on a hot pickup or with something in front of it, the transistor saturates on one half of the wave and cuts off on the other, an asymmetric, even-harmonic clip, and the bias walks on hard hits. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.1 dB small-signal and 0.02 dB per sine fundamental.
Drive.name: EHX LPB-1

params.desc: Volume (VR1 100k audio taper, the only control): the share of the transistor stage's ~+27 dB that reaches the output. 5 = unity, 10 = +21 dB, 0 = silence. The stage clips the same at every setting
params.label: Volume

Drive.usage: Unity / always on: Volume=5. The LPB-1's flat buffer-plus-a-little: same level, a touch of grit on hard hits. Clean boost for a solo: Volume=7. About +8 dB over unity, still clean on most pickups. Push a dirty amp: Volume=8-9. Hits the amp's input 13-17 dB harder than unity: more gain and compression from the amp itself. Cranked: Volume=10. +21 dB over unity into the amp -- the classic cranked-LPB-1 bite. The transistor's own clipping does not depend on Volume: it comes from how hard the guitar (or a pedal in front) hits it. Stacking: In front of a fuzz or overdrive it adds gain; after one, it is a level boost (and clips the drive's peaks asymmetrically).

Drive.description: Electro-Harmonix Mole bass booster (the vintage Mole / early Hog's Foot circuit), modelled from its schematic (AMZ): the LPB-1's single common-emitter silicon transistor (2N5088 modelled for the drawn 2N5133) with its values tilted to the bass -- 3.3u coupling, a 390 ohm unbypassed emitter (about +25 dB in the lows) and 0.1u across the 10k collector load, so the response is -3 dB at about 180 Hz and falls 6 dB per octave above: a big low-end lift with the highs rolled away, straight into the 100k audio Volume pot, no buffer. Hot bass notes clip in the transistor, the positive half first (cutoff), with the harmonics filtered by the same collector cap. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.01 dB small-signal to 2 kHz (0.3 dB at 10 kHz) and 0.02 dB per sine fundamental.
Drive.name: EHX Mole

params.desc: Volume (100k audio-taper pot, the only control): the share of the transistor stage's bass-tilted gain (+25 dB in the lows) that reaches the output. 5 = unity, 10 = +21 dB, 0 = silence. The stage clips the same at every setting
params.label: Volume

Drive.usage: Unity / dark always-on: Volume=5. Same overall level as bypass, but the weight moves to the lows: 100 Hz sits 14 dB above 1 kHz. Fat lead boost: Volume=7. About +8.5 dB over unity with the treble rounded off -- a thick, woolly neck-pickup lead. Bass into a dirty amp: Volume=8-9. Slams the amp's input with low end; the amp breaks up fat and loose. Use the amp's treble or a later EQ to get some bite back. Cranked: Volume=10. About +21 dB over unity. The transistor's own clipping does not depend on Volume: it comes from how hard the guitar (or a pedal in front) hits it, mostly on low notes. On bass: what it was built for -- a low-end lift for a bass guitar; on guitar it is a dark boost. Stacking: In front of a fuzz it feeds the fuzz a bass-heavy, treble-cut signal (a thick, smooth fuzz); after a drive it is a dark level boost.

Drive.description: Electro-Harmonix Screaming Bird treble booster, modelled from its schematic (AMZ): the LPB-1's circuit with 0.002 uF coupling caps in and out -- one common-emitter silicon transistor (2N5133) with an unbypassed 390 ohm emitter, ~+25 dB of treble, the lows rolled off at 12 dB/octave below ~2 kHz, straight into the 100k Volume pot, no buffer. Thin and cutting on its own; in front of a dirty amp it tightens the low end and makes the top end scream. On hot input the transistor cuts off on one half of the wave and saturates on the other, an asymmetric clip, and the bias walks on hard hits. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.03 dB small-signal and 0.05 dB per sine fundamental.
Drive.name: EHX Screaming Bird

params.desc: Volume (100k audio-taper pot, the only control): the share of the transistor stage's ~+25 dB of treble that reaches the output. 5 = unity on a typical guitar, 10 = +21 dB, 0 = silence. The stage clips the same at every setting
params.label: Volume

Drive.usage: Unity treble lift: Volume=5. Same overall level as bypass on a typical guitar, but the bass is gone and the top end is up: a thin, cutting voice. Cutting lead: Volume=7. About +8 dB over unity, all of it in the upper mids and treble -- a solo that slices through a band. Bright amp pusher: Volume=8-9. In front of a cranked or dirty amp: the amp's low end tightens and the treble drives it hard -- the classic treble-booster-into-a-stack sound. Screaming: Volume=10. +21 dB over unity. The transistor's own clipping does not depend on Volume; it comes from how hard the guitar (or a pedal in front) hits it. Tip: Roll the guitar's tone or volume back to tame it; put a fuzz or overdrive after it for a bright, tight lead.

Drive.description: JFET clean boost, modelled from its circuit: two J201 common-source stages on 9 V with a dual-gang gain pot in their sources, drains trimmed to mid-swing. Up to +35 dB; clean at low settings, the J201s' square-law warmth and then the 9 V swing at high settings. Bright: a cap across the first stage's pot.
Drive.name: JFET Clean Boost

params.desc: Clean gain boost in dB. 0=unity, 20=loud, 35=extreme
params.label: Boost

params.desc: 0=normal, 1=bright cap engaged (more presence at low volume)
params.label: Bright (0/1)

Drive.usage: Unity signal fattener: Boost=0dB. Just the JFET circuit coloring your tone. Moderate push: Boost=12dB. Enough to push a clean amp into breakup. Solo boost: Boost=20dB. Step on it for solos — significant volume lift. Extreme: Boost=35dB. JFET compresses heavily. Thick, warm, squashed. Bright switch: For single coils or dark setups. +3dB shelf at 2kHz.

Drive.description: Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer, modelled from its circuit: the op-amp clipping stage with the 1N914 pair in its feedback (the input plus its 720 Hz-humped, diode-limited excess -- why a TS keeps the note's fundamental clean), the active tone stage and the audio-taper level. Validated against ngspice (the whole pedal from the ElectroSmash schematic: fundamental within 0.1 dB, harmonics within 0.7 dB) and a real TS9 (ToneTwist, ESR 0.014-0.016).
Drive.name: Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer

params.desc: The 500k drive pot (audio taper): gain from about 12 to 118 into the diodes.
params.label: Drive

params.desc: 0=dark/bassy, 5=balanced, 10=bright/treble
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Output level (audio taper, like the pedal). 5 = unity at Drive 5, 10 = about +21 dB.
params.label: Level

Drive.usage: Amp push (clean boost): Drive=0, Level=8. Mid-hump tightens the amp's bass. Light OD: Drive=4, Tone=5, Level=5. Classic bluesy breakup. Full drive: Drive=8, Tone=5, Level=4. Smooth, compressed, mid-focused. Into dirty amp: Drive=3, Level=7. The TS tightens and focuses the amp's distortion. Tone: 0=dark/muffled, 5=balanced, 10=full treble. Most players: 4-6. mid-hump OD vs vintage OD: the same circuit and op-amp; the TS9's output resistors (RB 470 / RC 100k) make it 0.12 dB louder. Pick either.

Drive.description: Klon Centaur, modelled from its circuit: input buffer, the op-amp gain stage driving germanium (or silicon) diodes to ground, the two clean feed-forward paths the dual-gang Gain pot fades against the dirty one, the summing amp, the active treble shelf and the output pot (and the anti-pop resistor that bleeds a little clean signal to the jack). Verified against ngspice of the full ElectroSmash schematic: within 0.5 dB small-signal and 0.3 dB per harmonic.
Drive.name: Klon Centaur

params.desc: The dual-gang Gain pot: up = more op-amp gain into the diodes AND less clean feed-forward -- the Klon blend.
params.label: Gain

params.desc: Active treble shelf above ~400 Hz: x0.4 (-8 dB) to x8 (+18 dB); flat below.
params.label: Treble

params.desc: Output pot. 5 = unity at Gain 5; 10 = about +6 dB (+10 dB at Gain 10).
params.label: Output

params.desc: Clipping diodes: germanium 1N34A (the original, softer) or silicon 1N914 (harder, more compression).
params.label: Diodes

Drive.usage: Transparent boost: Gain=0, Output=8. Clean boost with transparent's body and warmth. Light overdrive: Gain=4, Output=5. Touch-sensitive — picks up gently, breaks up on hard strums. Full drive: Gain=8, Output=4. Still retains clean fundamental underneath. Treble: 0=warm, 5=neutral, 10=present. Higher than typical — refined, not harsh. Stacking: transparent into a slightly dirty amp is THE classic use. Set Gain=3-5, Output=6.

Drive.description: BK Butler Tube Driver (B.K. Butler's patent 5,022,305, the circuit of the original Tube Driver), modelled from its schematic (AMZ, drawn from the patent): a JRC4558 buffer and inverting gain stage (the 500k audio Tube Drive pot in its feedback, up to about x245, rolled off above ~2.7 kHz at full drive) feeding a real 12AX7 run starved on the 9 V adapter -- both plates on about 8.5 V, both cathodes grounded. V1a's grid goes to ground through 3.3k and conducts on the positive half; V1b's grid is pulled UP to B+ through 470k (the patent's trick), so it sits conducting at +0.3 V: positive swings are swallowed by grid current, negative ones drive it to cutoff -- a strongly asymmetric, even-harmonic overdrive whose coupling caps shift bias as you dig in. At high Drive the op-amp clips first and the tube stages round and compress what it sends. Then the passive Tone (treble cut) and Volume. The triodes are Koren's 12AX7 equations with grid current, solved inside each stage's network. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.05 dB small-signal to 5 kHz (0.25 dB at 10 kHz) and 0.1 dB per sine fundamental.
Drive.name: BK Butler Tube Driver

params.desc: Tube Drive (500k audio-taper rheostat, the op-amp's whole feedback resistor): gain 0 at 0, about x22 at 5, x245 at 10 into the 12AX7. Higher settings also darken the op-amp stage (120p across the pot)
params.label: Tube Drive

params.desc: Tone (10k linear): a passive treble cut after the tube (the pot between 10n from the plate and 47n to ground). 10 = brightest, 0 = darkest (about -23 dB at 5 kHz relative to 10)
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Volume (100k audio-taper pot). 5 = unity at Drive 5, Tone 5; 10 = about +21 dB
params.label: Volume

Drive.usage: Classic Tube Driver: Drive=5, Tone=5, Volume=5. Unity level: warm, compressed tube overdrive with the tube's even-harmonic grind. Edge of breakup: Drive=2, Tone=6, Volume=6.5. Little op-amp gain -- the 12AX7 stages do the work; cleans up with the guitar's volume knob. Blues lead: Drive=7, Tone=6, Volume=6. Thick, singing sustain; the op-amp is starting to clip into the tubes. Saturated: Drive=10, Tone=4, Volume=5. Full gain: the 4558 squares the signal and the starved tubes round it off; Tone down tames the fizz. Into a clean amp: the original's job -- a small tube amp's overdrive in a pedal; set Volume for the amp's input, Tone to taste (it only cuts treble). Note: Drive at 0 is silence (the pot is the whole feedback resistor, as on the unit); the useful range starts around 1.

Drive.description: Ibanez TS808 Tube Screamer, modelled from its circuit (the same clipping and tone circuit as the TS9 block; the TS808's output stage, RB 100 / RC 10k for the TS9's 470 / 100k, is 0.12 dB quieter). Op-amp clipper with 1N914s in the feedback, 720 Hz hump, active tone, audio-taper level. Validated against ngspice (the whole pedal, from the ElectroSmash schematic) and a real TS9.
Drive.name: Ibanez TS808 Tube Screamer

params.desc: The 500k drive pot (audio taper): gain from about 12 to 118 into the diodes.
params.label: Drive

params.desc: 0=dark/bassy, 5=balanced, 10=bright/treble
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Output level (audio taper, like the pedal). 5 = unity at Drive 5, 10 = about +21 dB.
params.label: Level

Drive.usage: Amp push: Drive=0, Level=8. Same circuit as mid-hump OD. Smooth OD: Drive=5, Tone=5, Level=5. The original "creamy" mid-hump overdrive sound. SRV tone: Drive=4-5, Tone=6, Level=6 into a Twin or similar clean amp. Into high-gain: Drive=2, Level=7. Tighten the bass, add mid focus. vintage OD vs mid-hump OD: the same circuit and op-amp; only the output resistors differ (0.12 dB). Pick either.

Drive.description: A drive, distortion or fuzz picked from every measured pedal -- circuit models at their knob settings and NAM pedal captures -- by where you put the puck: gain across, voice up. Swaps crossfade; LEVEL MATCH keeps the level into the amp the same, PUSH boosts on top. SPLIT turns it into the pedal it is playing.
Drive.name: XY Drive

params.desc: Target gain, 0 = cleanest boost, 1 = most distortion.
params.label: Gain

params.desc: Target voice, 0 = darkest against the input, 1 = brightest.
params.label: Voice

params.desc: VOICE counts the air band (6.3-10 kHz) too, not only 2-6.3 kHz against 160-800 Hz.
params.label: + Air

params.desc: Match: every pedal leaves at the input's loudness.
params.label: Level

params.desc: Level on top of the match (or of the natural level).
params.label: Push

params.desc: The pad filter: {group: [chips]}; empty = everything.
params.label: Filter

params.desc: What the puck resolved to (set by /api/xy/move).
params.label: Resolved

Drive.usage:
Pad: X = gain (clean boost to fuzz), Y = voice (dark to bright, against the input).
Level: MATCH = every pedal leaves at the guitar's loudness; OFF = natural levels.
Push: a trim on top.
Filter: type, source, family, CPU.
Split: replace this block with its current pedal and level.

Dynamics.description: Pulls down the breaths between phrases. Acts only on material that is both unvoiced and quiet, so consonants and quiet sung tails are untouched — which a gate cannot manage.
Dynamics.name: Breath Control

params.desc: Depth of the reduction. 0 = inactive.
params.label: Amount

params.desc: How far BELOW programme level unvoiced material counts as breath. Relative, not absolute dBFS, so it does not move with the mic or its gain.
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: Maximum reduction applied to a breath.
params.label: Depth

params.desc: Where the voiced/unvoiced line sits. Higher = stricter about calling something unvoiced.
params.label: Voicing

params.desc: How quickly the reduction moves. Slewed, never gated.
params.label: Speed

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Dynamics.usage: Placement: after the gate, before compression. Breaths still audible? Raise Threshold so more of the breath falls below it, or raise Depth. Consonants dulling? Lower Threshold — consonants are unvoiced but LOUD, so the level test is what spares them. Phrase ends clipped? Lower Voicing — a quiet tail still has a fundamental and should read as voiced.

Dynamics.description: Studio compressor. Seven circuit voicings, soft knee, parallel mix, limiter and output saturation.
Dynamics.name: Logic Pro Compressor

params.desc: 0 Platinum, 1 Studio VCA, 2 Studio FET, 3 Classic VCA, 4 Vintage VCA, 5 Vintage FET, 6 Vintage Opto. Same threshold/ratio law on all seven; they differ in what escapes on a transient
params.label: Circuit

params.desc: Level above which compression begins
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: Compression ratio. 1=none, 4=moderate, 20=limiting, 30=hard limiting
params.label: Ratio

params.desc: Width of the soft transition either side of the threshold. 0 is a hard knee
params.label: Knee

params.desc: How fast compression engages. Lower=faster, catches transients
params.label: Attack

params.desc: How fast compression lets go
params.label: Release

params.desc: Program-dependent recovery. How far it bends is the circuit’s own character
params.label: Release Auto

params.desc: Gain after the gain computer, to restore the level compression took away
params.label: Make Up

params.desc: Trim before the detector
params.label: Input

params.desc: Trim at the very end, after the limiter
params.label: Output

params.desc: 100 is fully compressed; below that is parallel compression, blending the untouched signal underneath
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Brick-wall ceiling after the compressor
params.label: Limiter

params.desc: Where that ceiling sits
params.label: Limit

params.desc: Pass the signal through untouched
params.label: Bypass

params.desc: 0 Off, 1 Soft, 2 Hard, 3 Clip. Output saturation, oversampled 4x. Shares a ceiling; the modes differ in how sharply they turn
params.label: Distortion

params.desc: As Logic: adds back the gain reduction a signal at that level would get, so compression does not drop the volume. 0 dB = a guitar peak, -12 dB = a guitar body
params.label: Auto Gain

Dynamics.usage: Light squeeze: Threshold=-18, Ratio=2, Attack=10, Release=100. Gentle leveling. Heavy compression: Threshold=-30, Ratio=8. Squashed, sustaining. Parallel: Ratio=10, Mix=50. Holds the peaks down without flattening the picking. Fast attack: Catches transients. Smooths out picking dynamics. Slow attack: Lets the pick attack through, compresses the sustain. More natural.

Dynamics.description: Narrows the gap between the pick attack and the note body. Set the gap you want in dB; peaks that rise further above the body level are pulled back to it with a 2 ms look-ahead, so it works the same at any playing level and does not clip or fizz.
Dynamics.name: Crest Limiter

params.desc: How far peaks may rise above the average level of the playing. Lower = denser. 12+ does almost nothing to a cab signal; 6 is heavy.
params.label: Gap

params.desc: Averaging time of the playing level the gap is measured from. It has to span several notes: a short one rises with each attack and treats the whole front of the note as "body", so nothing narrows. Held through silence, so a phrase after a pause is measured against the level you were playing at.
params.label: Average

params.desc: How fast the reduction lets go after a peak. Short keeps the note body untouched; long smooths more but can pump.
params.label: Release

params.desc: Most the block will ever take off a peak.
params.label: Max Reduction

params.desc: 1 = fully limited. Lower blends the untouched signal back in (parallel), keeping some attack.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Output level. Raise by about the typical reduction to turn the lower peaks into more average level.
params.label: Output

Dynamics.usage: Gap is the whole control: how far peaks may rise above the average level of the playing. Raw guitar sits around 12-15 dB after an amp and cab. Transparent: Gap=10, Release=60 ms. Takes 2-4 dB off the hardest picks only. Tight clean: Gap=8, Release=50 ms. Even, "produced" clean rhythm. Dense: Gap=6, Release=40 ms, Output +4 dB. Near-constant level; pick attack mostly gone. Parallel: Gap=5, Mix=50%. Body gets louder, attack stays. Where: after the cab (the cab reshapes peaks) and before time effects. Expect: the result lands 1-2 dB above Gap, and it works on the note envelope -- clean and edge-of-breakup tones gain most. On high gain the gap is inside the waveform itself and this block can do little. First note: the reference is held through pauses; only the very first note after a chain load, before any level has been measured, passes untouched. For a louder result raise Output by roughly what the Reduction takes off -- the average level barely moves, only the peaks come down.

Dynamics.description: DOD 525 Compressor Limiter, modelled from its schematic: a CA3094 OTA gain cell (22k / 1k input divider, a DC servo on its (-) input) whose current a TL062 turns into voltage through 220k -- up to +33 dB of gain at rest, which the detector pulls down. The detector is a feedback one: the TL062's output drives a 2N4124 phase splitter and two transistor charge pumps that discharge a 4.7 uF cap (through ATTACK), and a TL022 follower on that cap sets the OTA's bias current through COM/LIM. Hard picks clip the TL062 for the first milliseconds before the gain comes down (the limiter's bite); the 1/2-supply node sits inside the loop and rolls the bass off below 30-270 Hz as the gain rises. Matches ngspice of the same schematic: held-gain response within 0.4 dB, harmonics within 3 dB, the gain-control cap within ~0.1 V on bursts, guitar RMS within 0.35 dB. Level: unity at the defaults (the bare pedal is +4.3 dB there).
Dynamics.name: DOD 525 Compressor Limiter

params.desc: COM/LIM (100k rheostat in the OTA bias line, read as audio law; 10 = 0 ohm): the resting gain the detector works against -- 0 = ~47 uA (gentle compression), 5 = ~260 uA, 10 = ~500 uA (hard limiting, more bass cut)
params.label: Com/Lim

params.desc: Attack (500k rheostat || 47k between the pump and the 4.7 uF, read as audio law): 0 = the gain drops within a few ms, 10 = ~40 ms (and a longer recovery)
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Level (100k audio pot from the TL062 output to 1/2 supply): output volume; 5 = unity on a typical DI, 10 = about +15 dB. Below ~3 the output is mostly the 1/2-supply node's own signal, as on the pedal
params.label: Level

Dynamics.usage: Sustain: COM/LIM=5, Attack=3, Level=5. Even, squashed clean tone; notes hold longer. Limiter: COM/LIM=10, Attack=0. Maximum gain with the fastest gain reduction -- a hard ceiling with a bit of pick bite. Gentle: COM/LIM=0. Little gain to take back: light levelling, the most natural attack. Bloom: Attack=10. The gain comes down slowly: the pick transient pops through before the squash.

Dynamics.description: DOD R825 rack compressor (the compressor path; its de-esser and external side chain are not modelled), from its schematic: an input stage with INPUT LEVEL gain, a dbx 2150A VCA, and a feedback side chain -- a precision full-wave rectifier after a 159 Hz high-pass (the bass doesn't pump it), a fixed threshold (0.2 V at the VCA's output), RATIO (0-10x), and a precision peak detector into 20 uF through ATTACK (1-40 ms), released through RELEASE (0.18-1 s). The VCA takes 6.1 mV of that held voltage per dB of gain reduction -- the same scale as the unit's threshold LEDs (3/6/10/20 dB). Clean, transparent studio compression; INPUT sets how hard the threshold is hit. Matches ngspice of the same schematic (the VCA behavioural on both sides): held-gain response within 0.01 dB, control voltage within 2 mV on bursts, guitar RMS within 0.05 dB. Level: unity at the defaults.
Dynamics.name: DOD R825 Compressor

params.desc: Input level (U11 gain 1.2x-6.2x after the 1/2 input pad, audio law): how hard the signal hits the fixed threshold -- the R825 was built for line level, so a guitar needs it high
params.label: Input

params.desc: Ratio (100k rheostat / 10k: the side-chain gain 0-10x, audio law): 0 = no compression, higher = harder limiting above the threshold
params.label: Ratio

params.desc: Attack (51 ohm + 100k || 2k into 20 uF): ~1 ms at 0 to ~40 ms at 10
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Release (100k || (10k + 100k) across 20 uF): ~0.18 s at 0 to ~1 s at 10
params.label: Release

params.desc: Output level (U10 gain (10k + 100k rheostat) / 20k, audio law): make-up gain; 5 = unity at the defaults, 10 = about +15 dB
params.label: Output

Dynamics.usage: Guitar levelling: Input=8.5, Ratio=5, Attack=3, Release=5. Picks peak 3-6 dB into reduction, sustained notes even out. Squash: Input=10, Ratio=10, Attack=0, Release=3. Up to ~14 dB of reduction on hard picks. Transparent: Input=7, Ratio=3. Only the loudest peaks are touched. Output makes up level after compression (5 = unity at the defaults).

Dynamics.description: DynaGate60. Revv G8-inspired gate with 60Hz hum-aware sidechain (5-notch), 2ms lookahead, Schmitt hysteresis, adjustable reduction floor.
Dynamics.name: Dynamic Gate

params.desc: Signal level below which gating/compression begins
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: Gate release speed. 0=instant, 5=moderate, 10=slow fade
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Gate floor. -80=full silence, -20=gentle duck, 0=off
params.label: Reduction

params.desc: 0=normal, 1=monitor the sidechain signal
params.label: Key Listen (0/1)

Dynamics.usage: Single coil hum: Threshold=-45, Decay=5, Reduction=-80. The 60Hz notch sidechain handles hum without false triggers. High-gain gate: Threshold=-35, Decay=3, Reduction=-60. Tight stop between palm mutes. Gentle duck: Threshold=-50, Decay=8, Reduction=-20. Signal fades out gracefully. Key Listen: Enable to hear what the sidechain detects — useful for tuning the threshold.

Dynamics.description: Sidechain-driven dynamic cut at 2-5 kHz. Removes the metallic ring after reverb without losing pick attack.
Dynamics.name: Dynamic De-Metallizer

params.desc: Tap-envelope level above which the 3 kHz tap starts ducking. Lower = more cut, more often.
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: 0 = no cut, 1 = full 4:1 ratio. The interpolation between dry and ducked tap.
params.label: Amount

params.desc: Low-shelf @ 200 Hz, post-duck.
params.label: Warmth

params.desc: High-shelf @ 8 kHz, post-duck.
params.label: Air

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Dynamics.usage: Reverb tail taming: Place AFTER reverb. Threshold -18 dB, Amount 0.6 is a good start. Too dull? Raise Threshold (cuts less often) or lower Amount. Add body: Warmth +2 dB compensates for any energy lost in the cut. Air on dark cabs: +1.5 dB air recovers sparkle without re-introducing harshness.

Dynamics.description: FET limiting amplifier modeled on the 1176LN. JFET gain reduction with feedback topology (sidechain after gain element). Program-dependent attack: faster at higher input levels. Four ratio modes plus "all buttons" mode with harmonic distortion. Fast attack (200us-800us), punchy character.
Dynamics.name: UREI 1176LN

params.desc: Input drive into compressor. Higher = more compression
params.label: Input

params.desc: Makeup gain. Match to bypassed level
params.label: Output

params.desc: 0=slow (800us), 10=fast (200us). Reversed like the real 1176
params.label: Attack

params.desc: 0=slow (1.1s), 10=fast (50ms). Reversed like the real 1176
params.label: Release

Dynamics.usage: Gentle leveling: Ratio=4:1, Attack=5, Release=5, Input=4. Smooth dynamics control. Punchy drums: Ratio=8:1, Attack=3, Release=4, Input=6. Fast attack grabs transients. Vocal limiting: Ratio=12:1, Attack=5, Release=5, Input=5. Firm control without pumping. All-buttons smash: Ratio=All, Attack=3, Release=3, Input=7. Aggressive, distorted compression. Parallel crush: Mix with dry. Ratio=20:1, Attack=2, Release=3, Input=8.

Dynamics.description: A synth-style Attack / Decay / Sustain / Release volume envelope, triggered by every pick. Optionally shifts the pitch during the sustain and release phases (off by default).
Dynamics.name: Guitar ADSR

params.desc: Fade-in after each pick. Long = violin-style volume swell.
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Time to fall from full level to the sustain level.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Level the note is HELD at while it rings, as a fraction of its peak (0.7 = 3 dB under). Sustain Hold keeps it there as the string fades.
params.label: Sustain

params.desc: Fade-out once the note ends.
params.label: Release

params.desc: A guitar has no note-off: the release starts when the note has died this far under its peak. Lower = earlier release. Not used when Sustain Time is set.
params.label: Release Point

params.desc: Hold the note this long in sustain, then release -- a synth note of fixed length. 0 = release when the note fades (Release Point).
params.label: Sustain Time

params.desc: Pitch shift during the sustain phase, in semitones. 0 = off.
params.label: Sustain Pitch

params.desc: Pitch the release bends to, in semitones, evenly across the whole release. 0 = off (from a shifted sustain: bends back to the played pitch).
params.label: Release Pitch

params.desc: Time to bend into the Sustain Pitch. 0 = jump. (The release always bends over the whole Release time.)
params.label: Pitch Glide

params.desc: In the shifted phases: 1 = only the shifted pitch, 0.5 = both (a harmony).
params.label: Pitch Mix

params.desc: HQ = the Pitch Shifter HQ engine: natural, ~60 ms behind. Fast = granular: ~25 ms behind, grainier.
params.label: Shifter

params.desc: HQ only: keep the guitar body's formants when shifted, so big shifts still sound like a guitar.
params.label: Formant

params.desc: Picks are recognised ~3-6 ms late. With a short Attack, 6 ms here keeps the whole pick, at 6 ms extra latency.
params.label: Lookahead

params.desc: Output level.
params.label: Level

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

params.desc: How readily a pick restarts the envelope. Lower if a ringing note re-swells or snaps back in pitch on its own; raise if soft re-picks of a ringing note are missed.
params.label: Pick Sensitivity

params.desc: How far the block may lift a fading note to hold it at the Sustain level. More = longer, flatter sustain (and more string noise at the end). 0 = no hold: the note fades naturally.
params.label: Sustain Hold

params.desc: Shape of the fade (it always lasts Release). Linear = even. Exponential = drops fast, long soft tail. Inverse Exp = holds, then falls away at the end.
params.label: Release Curve

presets.desc: In front of Harmonic Wave (or any synth fed by the guitar): holds each note at its picked level while the string rings, so it sustains like a keyboard note instead of dying with the string; the synth's own envelope does the shaping. Measured on Jupiter against the real Vital patch from MIDI: level 1 s into a note -9.9 dB (real -7.0; -20 without), harmonics within 3.4 dB.
presets.name: Synth Sustain

Dynamics.usage: Volume swell: Attack 400 ms, Decay 1 ms, Sustain 1.0, Release 300 ms. Synth pluck: Attack 1 ms, Decay 250 ms, Sustain 0.2, Release 150 ms, Lookahead 6 ms. Octave bloom: Sustain Pitch +12, Pitch Glide 150 ms, Pitch Mix 0.5 -- the octave grows in behind each note. Dive on release: Release Pitch -12, Release 1500 ms, Release Curve Inverse Exp -- the note stays loud while it dives. Long synth sustain: Sustain 1.0, Sustain Time 4000 ms, Sustain Hold 30 dB -- the note stays at full level for 4 s, then releases. Gated notes: Sustain Time 300 ms cuts every note to a fixed length. Note re-swells by itself? lower Pick Sensitivity. Placement: after the gate and guitar_xform, before drive -- a swell into drive sounds most like a bowed instrument.

Dynamics.description: Brick-wall limiter based on UREI 1176 topology.
Dynamics.name: Limiter

params.desc: Signal level below which gating/compression begins
params.label: Ceiling

Dynamics.usage: Safety ceiling: Ceiling=-1dB. Prevents clipping downstream. Aggressive limiting: Ceiling=-6dB. Heavy gain reduction, loud and squashed.

Dynamics.description: Native-C 4-band stereo compressor with fixed LR4 crossovers (150/500/3500 Hz) and stereo-linked gain reduction. Per-band threshold/ratio/makeup live; attack/release fixed (5/50 ms scaled per band). Lighter on CPU and tighter image than the Faust multiband_compressor when you don't need adjustable crossovers.
Dynamics.name: Multiband Comp

params.desc: Sub band threshold (0–150 Hz)
params.label: Sub Thresh

params.desc: Sub band ratio (1 = bypass)
params.label: Sub Ratio

params.desc: Sub band makeup gain
params.label: Sub Makeup

params.desc: Low band threshold (150–500 Hz)
params.label: Low Thresh

params.desc: Low band ratio
params.label: Low Ratio

params.desc: Low band makeup gain
params.label: Low Makeup

params.desc: Mid band threshold (500–3500 Hz)
params.label: Mid Thresh

params.desc: Mid band ratio
params.label: Mid Ratio

params.desc: Mid band makeup gain
params.label: Mid Makeup

params.desc: High band threshold (3500 Hz–Nyquist)
params.label: High Thresh

params.desc: High band ratio
params.label: High Ratio

params.desc: High band makeup gain
params.label: High Makeup

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass (0/1)

Dynamics.usage: Bands: Sub (0–150 Hz), Low (150–500 Hz), Mid (500–3500 Hz), High (3500 Hz–Nyquist). Crossovers fixed. Stereo linking: The gain reduction is computed from max(L, R) envelope and applied identically to both channels — keeps the image stable. Threshold/Ratio: Standard. Ratio=1 means band passes through. Makeup: Per-band level trim post-compression. Attack/Release: Per-band, baked at chain-init: sub 30/200, low 15/120, mid 8/80, high 4/40 ms.

Dynamics.description: 4-band multiband compressor with an LR4 crossover tree (all-pass compensated: flat at any band gains), soft-knee gain computer (6dB knee), RMS level detection (50ms), and asymmetric attack/release per band. Crossover frequencies adjustable. Guitar-optimised defaults: slow bass attack, fast presence attack.
Dynamics.name: Multiband Compressor

params.desc: Crossover 1: bass/low-mid split frequency
params.label: XO1

params.desc: Crossover 2: low-mid/high-mid split frequency
params.label: XO2

params.desc: Crossover 3: high-mid/presence split frequency
params.label: XO3
