Dynamics.usage: Transparent control: Default settings. Tightens bass, controls mids, tames highs. Crossovers: XO1=200Hz (bass/mid split), XO2=1kHz (mid split), XO3=5kHz (mid/presence split). Per-band: Each band has independent Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release, Makeup. Bass tip: Slow attack (30ms+) lets bass transient punch through before clamping. Presence tip: Fast attack (4ms) controls pick noise and string squeak.

Dynamics.description: Simple noise gate with threshold, attack, and release.
Dynamics.name: Noise Gate

params.desc: Signal level below which gating/compression begins
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: How fast compression engages. Lower=faster
params.label: Attack

params.desc: How fast compression releases. Lower=faster
params.label: Release

Dynamics.usage: Light gate: Threshold=-50dB. Cuts hiss during pauses without affecting playing. Tight gate: Threshold=-35dB, fast attack/release. For high-gain — silences between notes.

Dynamics.description: Native-C noise gate with asymmetric envelope follower, hysteresis, hold time and lookahead. Same control surface as noise_gate_pro but coefficient updates are range-cached so live slider drags don't spike CPU. Use when you need the cleanest possible chatter-free gate.
Dynamics.name: Noise Gate 2

params.desc: Gate open threshold (RMS)
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: Open/close threshold separation
params.label: Hysteresis

params.desc: Minimum gate-open time after threshold cross
params.label: Hold

params.desc: Envelope attack time
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Envelope release time
params.label: Release

params.desc: Sidechain pre-delay so the envelope sees the transient before the audio. IN-PATH ON EVERY SAMPLE, not predictive: this is latency you pay while playing, to protect the first pick out of silence. The gain now opens across exactly this window, so 1 ms lands the gate 96% open with no measurable attack loss -- better than 3 ms managed before
params.label: Lookahead

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass (0/1)

Dynamics.usage: Threshold: Open level. Drop below silences. Hysteresis: Open/close gap (typ 8 dB). Wider = more chatter rejection, less responsive. Hold: Min open time after threshold cross — natural sustain on note tails. Attack/Release: Asymmetric — fast attack preserves pick, slow release lets notes ring. Lookahead: Pre-delay so the envelope sees the transient before opening — clean attack, no swallowed pick.

Dynamics.description: Studio-grade noise gate with asymmetric envelope follower, hysteresis (separate open/close thresholds), hold time, smooth 0..1 gain curve, and lookahead pre-delay. Eliminates chatter near threshold, keeps natural note sustain, and avoids clipping the pick attack.
Dynamics.name: Noise Gate Pro

params.desc: Level above which the gate opens. Set just above the noise floor
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: Gap between open and close thresholds. 2-6=tight, 8-12=musical
params.label: Hysteresis

params.desc: Gate stays fully open this long after signal drops below threshold
params.label: Hold

params.desc: Gate opening speed. 1-3 ms = fast (paired with lookahead), 5+ = softer attack
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Gate closing speed after Hold expires. 50=tight, 150=natural, 400=gradual
params.label: Release

params.desc: Audio pre-delay so the gate opens before the transient arrives
params.label: Lookahead

Dynamics.usage: Clean rhythm: Threshold=-60, Hysteresis=6, Hold=150, Attack=2, Release=150. High-gain: Threshold=-50, Hysteresis=10, Hold=100, Attack=1, Release=80. Tight but musical. Palm-mute metal: Threshold=-45, Hysteresis=12, Hold=60, Release=50. Snaps shut between chugs. Lead / sustain: Threshold=-55, Hysteresis=8, Hold=300, Release=400. Long natural decays. Hysteresis: gap between open & close thresholds. Higher = no chatter near the noise floor. Lookahead: 3 ms default — the envelope detector runs ahead so the gate is already open before the pick transient arrives. Two-gate chains: For high-gain rigs, place one Noise Gate Pro at the front (catches input hum/buzz) AND a second AFTER the amp+cab (catches saturator state-decay tails and amplified hiss the front gate can't see). The second instance is loaded with the "Post-Amp Tight" or "Post-Amp Smooth" preset — same block, just calibrated thresholds for post-amp signal levels.

Dynamics.description: Analog optical compressor with LED/LDR vactrol gain control. Dual-sidechain topology creates a natural soft knee with no hard threshold. Program-dependent ratio (~1.5:1 at quiet, ~6:1 at forte). Fixed 5ms vactrol attack preserves pick transients, variable release controls sustain character.
Dynamics.name: Optical Compressor

params.desc: LED drive sensitivity. 0=transparent, 5=moderate (-4 to -6dB), 10=heavy limiting
params.label: Compression

params.desc: Vactrol recovery. 0=fast/punchy (50ms), 5=smooth (275ms), 10=bloomy (500ms)
params.label: Release

params.desc: Output makeup gain. Range -40..+15 dB to cover Helix-style deep cut at low knob settings.
params.label: Level

Dynamics.usage: Subtle sustain: Comp=3, Release=5, Level=+2dB. Barely there — evens out dynamics without squashing. Studio clean: Comp=5, Release=5, Level=+5dB. Classic optical compression — smooth, transparent. Country squish: Comp=7, Release=3, Level=+8dB. Fast release, heavy comp — chicken pickin' attack. Slow bloom: Comp=6, Release=8, Level=+6dB. Notes swell and sustain into each other. Peak limiter: Comp=10, Release=2, Level=+12dB. Heavy limiting — tames hot pickups before an amp.

Dynamics.description: MXR Dyna Comp (M102), modelled from its schematic: the CA3080 OTA as the gain cell (its gain set by the bias current Iabc, its tanh input clipping above ~50 mV), the treble pre-emphasis into the OTA and the 1 nF de-emphasis after it, the transistor phase splitter, and the two-transistor charge-pump detector on C8 that pulls Iabc down as the output grows -- a feedback compressor: a near-flat output above its knee, a pick overshoot that settles in ~30 ms (3 ms at full Sensitivity), a slow (~2 s) recovery, and the OTA's own grit on hard picks. Matches ngspice of the same schematic (transistor-level CA3080) within 0.2 dB on the static curve and envelopes.
Dynamics.name: MXR Dyna Comp

params.desc: Sensitivity (RV1 500k linear, a rheostat to the CA3080's bias pin): the OTA's bias current at rest, so its gain and how early it compresses: 0 = ~12 dB of gain (its knee near -24 dBV in at 1 kHz), 5 = ~18 dB (-29 dBV), 10 = ~37 dB (-49 dBV). Linear, as stock: most of the change is in the top quarter
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: ElectroSmash's attack mod: R13 (C8's recharge resistor) as 10k + a 150k reverse-audio pot. 5 = stock (146k): ~30 ms attack, ~2 s recovery. Lower = faster attack and recovery, less squash (0 = 10k: ~17 ms / ~0.2 s)
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Output (RV2 50k linear). 5 = unity at Sensitivity 5, Attack 5
params.label: Output

Dynamics.usage: Country squish: Sensitivity=7, Attack=3, Output=5. Classic squishy chicken pickin'. Funk snap: Sensitivity=5, Attack=1, Output=5. Fast recovery: every pick snaps through. Sustain: Sensitivity=9, Attack=6, Output=4. Long, even sustain for clean leads. Light touch: Sensitivity=2, Attack=5, Output=6. Gentle levelling. Full squash: Sensitivity=10, Attack=10, Output=4. Maximum squash, the slowest recovery.

Dynamics.description: Simulates palm muting on a normally-picked signal. Decay time and filter corner are measured from matched open/palm-muted recordings of the same guitar (Pianobook RJS), not estimated: the mute is a one-pole roll-off at ~650 Hz plus an exponential decay of ~72 ms time constant. Follows the pick transient and imposes a synthetic decay, so it works the same on a clean DI or after a high-gain amp where an expander would just act as a noise gate. Ring sets how long the note sings before the clamp; Decay sets how fast it closes; Depth scales the whole effect from transparent to fully muted.
Dynamics.name: Palm Mute

params.desc: Master mute amount: 0 = transparent, 1 = full mute
params.label: Depth

params.desc: How long the note rings fully open before the clamp begins. A measured hand mute rings ~100 ms.
params.label: Ring

params.desc: Time CONSTANT of the imposed decay, not a time to silence. Measured on the RJS matched recordings: 72 ms palm muted, 185 ms muted softly, against 895 ms open. Both are defaults for one guitar -- another will differ.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Pre-amp (filter only) or post-cab (filter + volume)
params.label: Position

params.desc: Detector gain only — audio path is unaffected
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Darkest cutoff at Depth 100%. Measured one-pole corner of a real mute: 651 Hz palm muted, 923 Hz muted softly.
params.label: Min Freq

params.desc: Open cutoff — effectively transparent on the attack
params.label: Max Freq

params.desc: The decay ASYMPTOTE -- where a muted note ends up, not a static cut. Deliberately not claimed as measured: a sample library cannot give it (the RJS muted set is recorded 4 dB HOTTER than its open set), so this is the one value here that is taste. Shallower after a hot amp, where a deep VCA makes hiss breathe.
params.label: VCA Floor

params.desc: How far the treble is cut, as a FLOOR rather than a slope. A hand on the strings reduces the top by a bounded amount: measured, the real mute plateaus near -10..-13 dB above 2 kHz instead of falling forever. 0 dB disables the cut entirely.
params.label: HF Floor

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass (0/1)

Dynamics.usage: Depth: The master control. 0% is transparent, 100% is a full mute. Scales both the filter floor and the volume drop together. Ring: How long the note stays fully open before clamping. 0 ms is a dead pizzicato chug; 50 ms lets it bloom and then mutes. Decay: The time constant of the imposed decay. 72 ms is a measured palm mute, 185 ms a soft one, 895 ms is an open note -- so shorter is a tighter chug. Position: Both positions mute by level and by filtering. Pre (before the amp) lifts the filter floor an octave, because a high-gain amp regenerates the harmonics you remove ahead of it. Post (after the cab) filters as configured. Sensitivity: Detector gain only; does not change the audio. Raise it if soft picking is not triggering. Min Freq / VCA Floor: The darkest cutoff and the deepest volume cut reached at Depth 100%.

Dynamics.description: Lead-note sustain after the amp. As a note decays, it resynthesises the note's own partials to hold it up -- no pitch tracking, so chords, double-stops and bends work. The dry signal passes through untouched, with no latency.
Dynamics.name: Spectral Sustain

params.desc: How slowly the held note fades (time to fall 60 dB). Must be longer than the note's own decay to be heard: after a high-gain amp a note already takes ~13 s, so 20-60 s is the useful range.
params.label: Sustain

params.desc: Infinite sustain: the note stays up until the next pick or a mute, its top end slowly warming as a feedback-held string does. Good on a footswitch.
params.label: Hold

params.desc: How much of the lost level is put back. 1 = the note stays at its held level; 0.5 = half way; above 1 the note blooms louder as it rings.
params.label: Amount

params.desc: How readily a new pick lets go of the held note. Raise if fast notes smear into each other; lower if a held note drops out on its own.
params.label: Pick Sensitivity

params.desc: How fast the sustain lets go when you mute the strings.
params.label: Release

params.desc: High-cut on the sustained part only. Lower for a warmer, rounder hold.
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Level of the sustained part. The dry note is never changed.
params.label: Level

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Dynamics.usage: Placement: after the amp, cab and EQ, before delay and reverb. Singing lead: Sustain 30 s, Amount 1 -- notes hold close to their peak and fade slowly. Infinite hold: put Hold on a footswitch; the note stays until the next pick or a mute. Bloom: Amount 1.3 -- held notes swell a little louder as they ring. Fast runs smear? raise Pick Sensitivity. Too bright on hold? lower Tone to 4-5 kHz. (The held upper partials already fade faster than the low ones, so a held note warms rather than turning metallic.)

Dynamics.description: Vital's multiband compressor: three bands (crossovers 120 Hz and 2.5 kHz), each pulled into a level window -- quiet parts raised, loud parts pushed down -- then given its own gain. Same parameters as Vital, and presets taken from Vital patches.
Dynamics.name: Vital Multiband Comp

params.desc: Where the signal sits against the thresholds. Vital's thresholds assume Vital's internal level; a guitar-driven voice is usually quieter. The same amount comes off after the compressor, so this does not change the level.
params.label: Input

params.desc: Output trim.
params.label: Level

params.desc: Vital's attack: 0.5 = 2.8 / 1.4 / 0.7 ms (low / band / high), x e^4 at 1.
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Vital's release: 0.5 = 40 / 28 / 15 ms (low / band / high), x e^4 at 1.
params.label: Release

params.desc: Compressed against dry, per band.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: The top of the low band's window: louder than this is compressed down.
params.label: Low Upper Threshold

params.desc: The bottom of the window: quieter than this is raised (with a positive lower ratio).
params.label: Low Lower Threshold

params.desc: Above the upper threshold: 0 = no compression, 1 = a hard ceiling (Vital's scale; 0.857 is about 7:1).
params.label: Low Upper Ratio

params.desc: Below the lower threshold: positive raises quiet signal toward it (upward compression), negative pushes it further down.
params.label: Low Lower Ratio

params.desc: The low band's level after compression.
params.label: Low Gain

params.desc: The top of the band band's window: louder than this is compressed down.
params.label: Band Upper Threshold

params.desc: The bottom of the window: quieter than this is raised (with a positive lower ratio).
params.label: Band Lower Threshold

params.desc: Above the upper threshold: 0 = no compression, 1 = a hard ceiling (Vital's scale; 0.857 is about 7:1).
params.label: Band Upper Ratio

params.desc: Below the lower threshold: positive raises quiet signal toward it (upward compression), negative pushes it further down.
params.label: Band Lower Ratio

params.desc: The band band's level after compression.
params.label: Band Gain

params.desc: The top of the high band's window: louder than this is compressed down.
params.label: High Upper Threshold

params.desc: The bottom of the window: quieter than this is raised (with a positive lower ratio).
params.label: High Lower Threshold

params.desc: Above the upper threshold: 0 = no compression, 1 = a hard ceiling (Vital's scale; 0.857 is about 7:1).
params.label: High Upper Ratio

params.desc: Below the lower threshold: positive raises quiet signal toward it (upward compression), negative pushes it further down.
params.label: High Lower Ratio

params.desc: The high band's level after compression.
params.label: High Gain

Dynamics.usage: From a Vital patch: pick the patch from Presets; its compressor settings load as they are. Input: set it so the signal sits where the patch's did (a guitar voice is often 5-10 dB under Vital's internal level). Input does not change the output level. Ratios: Vital's scale -- upper 1 is a hard ceiling, 0.857 about 7:1; a positive lower ratio raises quiet signal (what makes Vital's OTT-style sustain). Only multiband: Vital's single-band modes (Low Band / High Band) are not offered.

Dynamics.description: Automatic LPF that closes during reverb tails and opens for fresh notes. Surgical fix for metallic-ringing tails.
Dynamics.name: Tail Tamer

params.desc: Slow-env level below which detection halts (LPF held). Higher = more conservative, less surprise sweeps.
params.label: Detect Floor

params.desc: LPF cutoff at full tail (closed). Lower = darker tail.
params.label: Min Cutoff

params.desc: LPF cutoff during fresh notes (open). Higher = more transparent for non-tail material.
params.label: Max Cutoff

params.desc: How smoothly the LPF interpolates between open and closed as the tail score changes.
params.label: Smooth Time

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Dynamics.usage: Default works for most: Floor -40, Min 3 kHz, Max 16 kHz, Smooth 300 ms. Heavier taming: Drop Min Cutoff to 2 kHz for very dark tails. Less aggressive: Raise Min Cutoff to 4-5 kHz, Smooth 500-800 ms. Sweep audible? Increase Smooth Time. Sweep too slow to react? Decrease it. LPF chattering on noise? Raise Detect Floor toward -30 dB.

Dynamics.description: Smooths harsh throat-voice and shouted high notes. Acts only when the voice is actually pushed, not merely loud, and spares consonants.
Dynamics.name: Vocal Smoother

params.desc: Overall depth. Scales BOTH layers. 0 = inactive.
params.label: Amount

params.desc: Sharpness above which the voice counts as pushed. THE control to calibrate. Measured on one singer: relaxed singing runs 0.92-1.30, pushed 1.08-1.48, so the two overlap and 1.26 is the last point that leaves relaxed singing untouched while a pushed phrase still loses 7.7 dB at its peak. Level-invariant, so mic gain does not move it.
params.label: Strain Thresh

params.desc: Maximum reduction the strain layer may apply.
params.label: Range

params.desc: Centre of the strain bell. 3-4 kHz for most voices; lower for a chesty bark.
params.label: Focus

params.desc: Strain-bell Q. Low = covers the whole harsh region but reaches into the air band; high = surgical. 1.1 measured as the best trade.
params.label: Width

params.desc: Enable the 4 moving bells that chase individual resonances.
params.label: Resonance Hunt

params.desc: Maximum reduction per hunting bell.
params.label: Hunt Range

params.desc: How far a band must stand above its neighbours before a bell chases it. Lower = hunts more, at the risk of hollowing the tone.
params.label: Hunt Thresh

params.desc: How eagerly /s/ and /sh/ are recognised and spared. Raise if consonants dull, lower if harsh sung notes slip through.
params.label: Sibilance Guard

params.desc: Detector attack/release. Fast = catches the onset of a shouted note; slow = smoother, less likely to breathe.
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Dry/processed blend. Below 1 keeps some of the original edge.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Dynamics.usage: Placement: after the mic preamp/gate, before compression and reverb. Calibrate first: sing a relaxed phrase and note the Sharpness readout; set Strain Thresh just above it. Then push a high note - reduction should appear only then. Too dull? Raise Strain Thresh, or raise Width (narrower bell keeps the air). Lisping? Raise Sibilance Guard. Still stabby on one note? That is a resonance - turn Resonance Hunt on and lower Hunt Thresh a little.

EQ.description: Craig Anderton's Wah / Anti-wah (from his project book), modelled from Jack Orman's AMZ drawings: two TL072 band-pass filters fed in parallel, the pedal's 50k pot shunting one with each half -- rocking it sweeps one peak up while the other sweeps down, a wah and an anti-wah at once. Each band-pass peaks +14 dB with a fixed bandwidth (+8 dB each after the mixer); the cap pair of each (the builder's choice, .001 - .005 uF) sets its range. With the defaults (.005 / .001) the heel is a dark 300 Hz peak, mid travel has peaks at 360 Hz and 1.8 kHz, the toe a 1.5 kHz peak. Version: the original on two 9 V batteries, or AMZ's single 9 V version, which clips its op-amps on a hard pick at a peak. Matches ngspice of both drawings within 0.35 dB small-signal and 0.45 dB per fundamental. Level: unity at mid travel (the circuit is about +1 dB there).
EQ.name: Anderton Wah-Antiwah

params.desc: Pedal position. 0=heel (the C1/C2 filter at its lowest), 1=toe (the C3/C4 filter at its lowest)
params.label: Position

params.desc: Original: Anderton's circuit on two 9 V batteries (+-9 V, DC coupled). AMZ 9 V: Jack Orman's single-battery version (4.5 V bias, 10u in / out caps, 10k output load): 0.4 dB quieter and it clips at +-3 V
params.label: Version

params.desc: C1 = C2, the heel filter's caps (uF). Lowest peak (heel): .001 1.49 kHz, .002 745 Hz, .003 497 Hz, .004 372 Hz, .005 298 Hz
params.label: C1/C2

params.desc: C3 = C4, the toe filter's caps (uF). Lowest peak (toe): .001 1.49 kHz, .002 745 Hz, .003 497 Hz, .004 372 Hz, .005 298 Hz
params.label: C3/C4

EQ.usage: Rocking: bind Position to an expression pedal. 0 = heel, 1 = toe. One filter rises as the other falls: with the default caps the sweep goes from a dark 300 Hz peak through two peaks (360 Hz + 1.8 kHz at mid) to 1.5 kHz at the toe. Cap pairs: C1/C2 sets the heel filter's range (lowest at the heel), C3/C4 the toe filter's. Bigger cap = lower and narrower: .005 bottoms out at 300 Hz (68 Hz wide), .001 at 1.5 kHz (340 Hz wide). Swap them and the pedal works backwards; close values make the two peaks meet near mid travel (+8 dB louder there). Version: Original (+-9 V, clean headroom) or AMZ 9 V (one battery; the op-amps clip at +-3 V, so a hot pickup at a peak gets a hard edge).

EQ.description: Envelope-controlled wah. Filter frequency follows playing dynamics.
EQ.name: Auto Wah

params.desc: How much playing dynamics control the effect
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Resonance width. Low=wide, high=narrow/resonant
params.label: Q

params.desc: Modulation rate in Hz
params.label: Speed

EQ.usage: Funk: Sensitivity=0.7, Q=8, Speed=0.05. Quacky envelope filter. Subtle: Sensitivity=0.3, Q=3, Speed=0.1. Gentle touch-sensitive sweep. Slow sweep: Sensitivity=0.5, Q=5, Speed=0.2. Gradual, expressive.

EQ.description: Single-band parametric peak/bell EQ. Frequency, Q (bandwidth), and Gain. Use for surgical boost/cut at one frequency — e.g. notching out an amp honk, dialling in presence, or adding air. Stack multiple instances in a chain when you need more than one band.
EQ.name: Bell EQ

params.desc: Centre frequency of the bell. 80-250=low, 250-2000=mid, 2000-8000=upper mid, 8000+=air
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: Bandwidth. 0.7=wide (~2 octaves), 1.5=medium, 3+=narrow (surgical notch/boost)
params.label: Q

params.desc: Cut (-) or boost (+). 0 dB = flat (no effect regardless of Q/Freq)
params.label: Gain

EQ.usage: Presence boost: Freq=3000 Hz, Q=1.5, Gain=+3 dB. Adds bite without harshness. Mud cut: Freq=250 Hz, Q=1.5, Gain=-3 dB. Cleans up boxy amps. Air lift: Freq=10000 Hz, Q=0.7, Gain=+4 dB. Wide, gentle top-end shelf-like lift. Honk notch: Freq=800 Hz, Q=3, Gain=-4 dB. Surgical cut for nasal resonance. Q: 0.7 = wide (musical), 1.5 = medium (versatile), 3+ = narrow (surgical).

EQ.description: 3-knob master shaper: Tilt (700 Hz pivot), Body (200 Hz peak), Air (8 kHz shelf). Native biquad cascade.
EQ.name: Color Tilt

params.desc: Low<->high tilt around 700 Hz. Negative = warmer; positive = brighter.
params.label: Tilt

params.desc: Low-mid weight at 200 Hz.
params.label: Body

params.desc: High-shelf sparkle at 8 kHz.
params.label: Air

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

EQ.usage: De-fizz after reverb: Tilt -2, Air -1 takes the metallic edge off without dulling. Warm a digital amp: Tilt -3, Body +2. Bright a dark cab: Tilt +2, Air +3. Master polish: Body +1, Air +1.5 for a finished sound.

EQ.description: Dunlop Cry Baby GCB-95 wah, modelled from its schematic: the MPSA13 input buffer, the MPSA18 gain stage whose 500 mH inductor resonates against C2, and the pedal's 100k log pot setting how much of the output the Q2 follower feeds back -- the resonance sweeps 450 Hz (heel) to 1.6 kHz (toe) with an 18-21 dB peak, sharper at the heel. The transistor's own grit on a hard pick is in. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.22 dB small-signal (peak frequency within 1 Hz) and 0.4 dB per fundamental. Level: unity at mid travel (the real pedal is about +9 dB there).
EQ.name: Dunlop Cry Baby GCB-95

params.desc: Wah sweep position. 0=heel/dark, 1=toe/bright
params.label: Position

params.desc: DC resistance of the 500 mH inductor (ElectroSmash: 10-200 ohm across the inductors used in wahs, 15 typical). Higher = a softer, less peaky heel (150 ohm: heel peak 21 -> 14 dB)
params.label: Inductor DCR

EQ.usage: Rocking wah: bind Position to an expression pedal. 0 = heel (dark, 450 Hz), 1 = toe (bright, 1.6 kHz). Cocked wah: park Position at 0.3-0.6 for a fixed vocal mid-boost -- the classic "stuck wah" lead tone. Before or after drive: before a drive the wah sweeps the drive's input (classic); after it, a smoother, more vocal filter on the distorted tone.

EQ.description: Electro-Harmonix Wah-Wah pedal (the 1970s wah / volume pedal), modelled from the EHX schematic: the guitar straight into a 2N3565 gain stage whose 500 mH inductor resonates against the feedback caps, the pedal's 100k pot setting how much of the output a second 2N3565 feeds back. A 4-position Tone switch picks the feedback cap -- the sweep's range, from a bright 650 Hz - 3 kHz down to a bass-wah 180 - 710 Hz -- and the peaks are big (+31 dB at the heel, Q up to 12). Mode turns it into a passive volume pedal, Reverse flips the pedal's direction. The transistors' own clipping (the gain stage saturating, the follower cutting off) is in: a hard pick at the heel snarls. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.07 dB small-signal and 0.44 dB per fundamental. Level: unity at mid travel with Tone 2 (the real pedal is +17.6 dB there).
EQ.name: EHX Wah-Wah

params.desc: Pedal position. 0=heel, 1=toe (Normal: heel dark, toe bright)
params.label: Position

params.desc: The 4-position tone switch: the feedback cap (uF, beside the fixed .0022) that sets the sweep's range. Heel..toe peaks: 1 655 Hz-3 kHz, 2 446 Hz-2 kHz, 3 237 Hz-1 kHz, 4 179-711 Hz
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Mode selector: Wah, or Volume -- the input straight onto the pedal's 100k pot, the jack on its wiper (a passive volume pedal)
params.label: Mode

params.desc: Reverse switch: swaps the pot's ends. Normal = wah heel dark (volume: heel loud); Reverse = wah heel bright (volume: toe loud)
params.label: Reverse

EQ.usage: Rocking wah: bind Position to an expression pedal. 0 = heel, 1 = toe; Reverse swaps the direction. Tone: 1 = brightest range (650 Hz - 3 kHz), 2 = the classic wah range (450 Hz - 2 kHz), 3 = low (240 Hz - 1 kHz), 4 = bass wah (180 - 710 Hz). Cocked wah: park Position at 0.2-0.5 for a fixed, very vocal mid peak. Volume: Mode = Volume makes Position a passive volume control (with Reverse on, the toe is loud).

EQ.description: Aphex-style aural exciter. Highpass-isolates a band above the Frequency knob, drives it hard through tanh saturation to generate harmonics, then subtracts the original band so only the NEW harmonic content is added back to dry. Color=Symmetric gives odd harmonics (3/5/7, warm), Color=Asymmetric adds even harmonics (2/3/4, brighter, denser).
EQ.name: Exciter

params.desc: Highpass corner. Harmonics are generated above this band. 3000=presence, 5000+=air, <500=warmth
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: Amount of generated harmonic content added back to dry. 0=off, 0.3=classic, 1=maximum
params.label: Harmonics

params.desc: Saturation character. Symmetric=odd harmonics (warm). Asymmetric=odd+even (brighter, denser)
params.label: Color

params.desc: Include the dry signal at the output. Off=harmonics only (for parallel/send processing)
params.label: Dry

EQ.usage: Air / presence: Frequency=5000, Harmonics=0.3, Color=Symmetric. Subtle top-end sparkle. Acoustic brightness: Frequency=4000, Harmonics=0.4, Color=Asymmetric. Denser sheen. Bass warmth: Frequency=150, Harmonics=0.3, Color=Asymmetric. Even-order bloom. Midrange bite: Frequency=1500, Harmonics=0.5, Color=Asymmetric. Parallel send: Dry=Off — output is harmonics only; blend with parallel routing. Placement: Usually after cab/NAM, before final EQ. Don't stack — one exciter is plenty.

params.desc: Corner of the high shelf. Independent of the high cut.
params.label: High Shelf Freq

params.desc: On: the output is held at the loudness of the input, measured on what you play, so reshaping the curve never changes the level. Replaces Output while on.
params.label: Unity Gain

EQ.usage: Smiley scoop: Boost 64-125 Hz and 4-8 kHz, cut 500 Hz-1 kHz. Classic modern-metal curve. Mid hump: Boost 500 Hz-2 kHz, gently dip the rest. Lead cut. Presence: +3 dB at 4 kHz and 8 kHz adds bite without harshness. Bass tightening: Drop 32 Hz by -6 dB on high-gain to clean the low end. Q tips: 1.4 (default) sums adjacent bands cleanly at unity (true graphic-EQ behaviour). Drop one band to ~0.7 for a wide shelving feel, push another past 3 for a surgical notch — they're independent.

EQ.description: Lowpass filter with selectable slope (12 / 24 / 48 dB/oct). Cleanly removes everything above the corner — fizz, pick noise, hiss, aliasing from pitch shifters. Steeper slopes give a harder wall for de-harshing.
EQ.name: High Cut

params.desc: Corner frequency. Content above is attenuated at the selected slope
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: 12 / 24 / 48 dB/oct. Steeper = harder wall
params.label: Slope

EQ.usage: De-fizz: Freq=6000 Hz, Slope=24 dB/oct. Cuts fizzy drive tails without darkening. Cab pre-tone: Freq=8000 Hz, Slope=12 dB/oct. Rolls off before an IR cab. Warm top: Freq=4500 Hz, Slope=12 dB/oct. Darken an overly bright amp. Brick-wall air cut: Freq=7000 Hz, Slope=48 dB/oct. Surgical removal.

EQ.description: First-order high-shelf EQ. Boost or cut everything above the corner frequency by the Gain amount. Great for broad brightness or darkness shaping — air, presence, or de-harshing.
EQ.name: High Shelf

params.desc: Shelf corner frequency. Content above this is boosted or cut by Gain
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: Shelf gain. Positive=brighter, negative=darker, 0=flat
params.label: Gain

EQ.usage: Air lift: Freq=10000 Hz, Gain=+4 dB. Opens the top end. Presence: Freq=4000 Hz, Gain=+3 dB. Adds cut and bite. Dark shelf: Freq=5000 Hz, Gain=-3 dB. Tames harsh amps. De-fizz: Freq=6000 Hz, Gain=-4 dB. Calms pick-noise and fizzy drives.

EQ.description: Highpass filter with selectable slope (12 / 24 / 48 dB/oct). Cleanly removes everything below the corner — rumble, sub-bass mud, handling noise. Use steeper slopes when you need a hard wall below a bass-heavy effect.
EQ.name: Low Cut

params.desc: Corner frequency. Content below is attenuated at the selected slope
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: 12 / 24 / 48 dB/oct. Steeper = more aggressive brick-wall feel
params.label: Slope

EQ.usage: Rumble filter: Freq=80 Hz, Slope=12 dB/oct. Removes sub-bass without thinning. Tighten for drive: Freq=180 Hz, Slope=24 dB/oct. Cleans low end before overdrive. Brick-wall cut: Freq=250 Hz, Slope=48 dB/oct. Surgical removal for bass guitar rejection. Voice-lift: Freq=120 Hz, Slope=12 dB/oct. Gentle HPF for single-coil recordings.

EQ.description: First-order low-shelf EQ. Boost or cut everything below the corner frequency by the Gain amount. Natural-sounding, wide-band — pair with a Bell EQ for surgical work above it.
EQ.name: Low Shelf

params.desc: Shelf corner frequency. Content below this is boosted or cut by Gain
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: Shelf gain. Positive=boost, negative=cut, 0=flat
params.label: Gain

EQ.usage: Bass lift: Freq=200 Hz, Gain=+3 dB. Adds body without boom. Bass trim: Freq=150 Hz, Gain=-3 dB. Tightens bass before a drive pedal. Body warmth: Freq=400 Hz, Gain=+2 dB. Fills in thin tones. Scoop: Freq=250 Hz, Gain=-5 dB. Hollowed low-mid for metal voicings.

EQ.description: 3-band parametric EQ. Bass shelf, sweepable mid peak, treble shelf.
EQ.name: 3-Band Parametric EQ

params.desc: Low shelf gain in dB
params.label: Bass

params.desc: Mid peak gain in dB
params.label: Mid

params.desc: Center frequency of mid EQ band in Hz
params.label: Mid Freq

params.desc: High shelf gain in dB
params.label: Treble

EQ.usage: Mid boost (mix cut-through): Mid=+4dB, Mid Freq=800Hz. Fills the 4-stage fuzz's scoop. Bass tighten: Bass=-3dB. Reduces flub before a drive pedal. Presence lift: Treble=+3dB. Adds sparkle without harshness. Scoop: Mid=-4dB. Scooped "metal" tone. Caution: disappears in a band mix.

EQ.description: Cuts a reverb or delay's RINGING in the tail, and only there: a narrow dynamic notch on a band that decays at least 1.5x slower than the band around it, audible in its critical band. A static metallic peak is colouration, not ringing: this block will not engage on it -- use a static notch or the reverb's tone control. Notes, the rest of the tail's tone, its width and its decay are left alone; /api/tfx/ring_audit says whether a chain rings at all.
EQ.name: Ring Suppressor

params.desc: Find the ring and its width from the signal: the band whose level keeps growing against its neighbours through each decay. Off = Freq and Q below. What it finds is reported either way.
params.label: Auto Find

params.desc: Manual centre (Auto Find off).
params.label: Freq

params.desc: Manual width of the notch and its detector (Auto Find off). A near-pure line wants 30-60, a broad resonance 6-10.
params.label: Q

params.desc: Per channel: L and R each find and cut their own ring (the deepest null; can move the image). Linked, one notch: one detector on both channels. Linked, two notches: the two strongest rings, each cut on both channels (L and R of a stereo reverb often ring a little apart).
params.label: Stereo

params.desc: How far the band must stand out over what it normally does for this source (learned while you play) before the cut engages.
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: The cut stops this far above the band's learned normal: it can never push the band below what the source normally has there.
params.label: Guard

params.desc: Deepest cut.
params.label: Max Cut

params.desc: Cut only once the signal is this far below its own recent peak (a decay). Relative, so the chain's level does not matter.
params.label: Decay Window

params.desc: How long "its own recent peak" is remembered.
params.label: Peak Memory

params.desc: How slowly the cut builds: slow enough that a brief bright burst never builds one.
params.label: Engage

params.desc: How fast it lets go inside a decay. A new note releases it at once.
params.label: Release

params.desc: After a pick (8 dB up in 5 ms), no cut for this long.
params.label: Pick Hold

params.desc: The band must fall this far under Threshold before the cut releases: no chatter.
params.label: Hysteresis

params.desc: A second, wider notch (Q/4, half the depth) under each: for a ring a chorus or LFO spreads into sidebands.
params.label: Skirt

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass (bit-transparent)
params.label: Bypass

EQ.usage: Where: after the reverb / delay that rings (a ring is not in the signal before it). Defaults find it: Auto Find on, Stereo = two notches. It locks within a few seconds of playing with gaps, and re-checks every 10 s (a new ring has to win by 3 dB). Notes are never cut: a pick, or the signal returning to its peak, releases the cut at once. It under-cuts by design: Guard keeps the band at or above what your playing normally puts there. Colouration is not ringing: a static metallic peak (bigsky Hall's 6.6/6.8 kHz decays WITH its neighbours) is never touched -- that is a static notch or the reverb's tone control. Static alternative: a fixed notch at the ring (Q ~12, -4 dB) takes most of it for ~1 dB of air at all times; this block takes it only in the decays, where it is heard.

EQ.description: Tilt EQ. Single knob shifts the tonal balance between dark and bright.
EQ.name: Tilt EQ

params.desc: Negative=darker, 0=flat, positive=brighter
params.label: Tilt

EQ.usage: Warm: Tilt=-4dB. Darkens the signal, adds bass weight. Bright: Tilt=+4dB. Opens up, adds air and presence. Subtle: Tilt=±2dB. Gentle correction without obvious EQ.

EQ.description: Vox V847 wah, modelled from its schematic: the Cry Baby's circuit family without its input buffer -- the guitar drives the 68k input resistor and the MPSA18 gain stage directly (510R emitter), whose 500 mH inductor resonates against C2, the pedal's 100k audio pot setting how much of the output the Q2 follower feeds back. The resonance sweeps 450 Hz (heel) to 1.6 kHz (toe) with a 17-20 dB peak, sharper at the heel; the 68k input loads the pickups as the real pedal does upstream. The transistor's grit on a hard pick is in. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.17 dB small-signal (peak frequency within 1 Hz) and 0.6 dB per fundamental. Level: unity at mid travel (the real pedal is about +8 dB there).
EQ.name: Vox V847

params.desc: Wah sweep position. 0=heel/dark, 1=toe/bright
params.label: Position

params.desc: DC resistance of the 500 mH inductor (ElectroSmash: 10-200 ohm, 15 typical). Higher = a softer, less peaky heel
params.label: Inductor DCR

EQ.usage: Rocking wah: bind Position to an expression pedal. 0 = heel (dark, 450 Hz), 1 = toe (bright, 1.6 kHz). Cocked wah: park Position at 0.3-0.6 for a fixed vocal mid-boost. vs Cry Baby: same family; the V847 has no input buffer and a slightly lower Q1 gain -- a touch smoother peak.

EQ.description: Manual wah. Resonant bandpass filter with position and Q control.
EQ.name: Wah

params.desc: Wah sweep position. 0=bass, 1=treble
params.label: Position

params.desc: Resonance width. Low=wide, high=narrow/resonant
params.label: Q

EQ.usage: Cocked wah: Set Position fixed at 0.3-0.5. Vowel-like filter color. Full sweep: Automate Position from 0 to 1. Classic wah-wah effect. High Q: Narrow, resonant, quacky. Low Q: wide, subtle.

EQ.description: Cry-Baby-style resonant bandpass. Native-C Chamberlin SVF with log-linear sweep 400 Hz–2200 Hz, position-dependent Q (3.5 heel, 5.5 toe). Use the Position knob for static wah, or drive it from a CC pedal / envelope to get the classic foot-pedal sweep.
EQ.name: Wah Filter

params.desc: Wah sweep position. 0=heel/dark, 1=toe/bright
params.label: Position

params.desc: Resonance multiplier on the Cry-Baby Q profile
params.label: Q Mult

params.desc: 0=dry, 1=full wah
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass (0/1)

EQ.usage: Position: 0=heel (400 Hz), 1=toe (2200 Hz). Drive from a pedal CC or envelope for sweeps. Q Mult: Scales the native Cry-Baby Q profile. 1.0=original, 0.5=mellow, 2.0=screaming. Mix: Wet/dry blend. 1.0=full wah, 0.5=parallel notch + dry.

Filter.description: Envelope-controlled resonant lowpass with threshold gate. The quack comes from the gate snapping the filter open/shut, not from resonant gain. Range sets bass frequency floor (100–600Hz). Sensitivity sets the threshold — below it, filter stays closed. Unity gain at low frequencies prevents clipping on bass.
Filter.name: Bass Envelope Filter

params.desc: Envelope threshold. 0=needs hard attack, 0.5=normal, 1=very responsive
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Base frequency floor. 0=100Hz (deep bass), 1=600Hz (guitar body)
params.label: Range

params.desc: Envelope release. 5ms=ultra snappy, 15ms=classic, 150ms=slow
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Dry/wet crossfade. 0=dry, 0.6=classic, 1=full filter
params.label: Blend

Filter.usage: Classic bass quack: Sensitivity=0.5, Range=0.3, Decay=15ms, Blend=0.6. Guitar funk: Sensitivity=0.6, Range=0.5, Decay=20ms, Blend=0.7. Higher Range for guitar register. Subtle warmth: Sensitivity=0.3, Range=0.2, Blend=0.4. Gentle opening on hard picks. Sensitivity: Sets threshold. Low=needs hard attack, high=responds to light touch. Range: Floor frequency. 0=100Hz (deep bass), 1=600Hz (guitar body). Filter sweeps up from here. vs Envelope Filter: Lowpass (not bandpass). Bass-friendly unity gain. Gate-based quack.

Filter.description: Karplus-Strong style tuned comb resonator. Delay line + damped LP feedback tuned to a MIDI note. Input excites the resonator continuously — partials near the tuned pitch build into a pitched drone that decays over Decay seconds. Damping controls loop LPF (high damp = shorter high-frequency decay, warmer tone).
Filter.name: Comb Resonator

params.desc: Resonator pitch, MIDI note number. 24 = C1 (32.7 Hz), 48 = C3 (130.8 Hz), 60 = C4 (261.6 Hz), 72 = C5 (523.3 Hz), 96 = C7 (2093 Hz).
params.label: Note

params.desc: Loop gain (0..0.999). Higher = longer ringing. Above ~0.98 the resonator will self-sustain on any input transient.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Loop LPF cutoff mapped 12 kHz .. 500 Hz. 0 = full bright resonance; 1 = dark, high partials die quickly (mellower drone).
params.label: Damping

params.desc: 0 = dry, 0.5 = equal blend (resonator sits under guitar), 1.0 = resonator only.
params.label: Mix

Filter.usage: String-simulator drone: Note=48 (C3), Decay=0.6, Damping=0.4, Mix=0.5. Guitar excites, drone rings. Metallic bell: Note=72 (C5), Decay=0.9, Damping=0.0, Mix=1.0. Long bright ring. Sub-octave add: Note=36 (C2), Decay=0.4, Damping=0.6, Mix=0.4. Warm sub-drone. Talkbox-ish: Note=60 (C4), Decay=0.3, Damping=0.5, Mix=0.7. Short pitched formant. Feedback squeal: Decay=0.99, Damping=0.1. Self-oscillates on excitation.

Filter.description: DOD 545 Wah Filter (an envelope filter), modelled from its schematic: a state-variable band-pass built from two CA3094 OTAs (each integrating into .01 uF, a Darlington buffering it), its Q set by the PEAK pot in the band-pass feedback. The envelope: a 1 kHz high-pass into a TL062 whose gain the SENSITIVITY pot sets (3x to 100x, clipping on its rails), a 1N4148 doubler and the ATTACK pot into a 4.7 uF hold cap, which drives both OTAs' bias current through a 2N4124 follower. At rest the filter sits around 80 Hz; picking sweeps it up to several kHz (7.5 kHz flat out) and it falls back over a few hundred ms. The OTAs' tanh and the Darlingtons' grit on hot signals are in. Matches ngspice of the same schematic: frozen-envelope response within 0.4 dB, harmonics within 3 dB, envelope within ~0.1 V on tone bursts, guitar RMS within 0.5 dB. Level: unity at the defaults (the bare pedal is +1.7 dB there).
Filter.name: DOD 545 Wah Filter

params.desc: Sensitivity (500k rheostat in the TL062's gain leg, read as audio law): the detector gain, 3x at 0 to 100x at 10. Higher = smaller picks open the filter further
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Attack (100k rheostat between the rectifier and the 4.7 uF hold cap, read as audio law): 0 = the filter snaps open on the pick, 10 = it swells open over ~0.5 s (the release slows too)
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Peak (100k rheostat in series with the band-pass feedback, read as audio law): the resonance. 0 = +5.6 dB, Q ~1; 5 = +8.5 dB; 10 = +20 dB, Q ~10
params.label: Peak

Filter.usage: Auto-wah: Sensitivity=5, Attack=3, Peak=5. Each pick opens the filter and it closes behind the note. Funk quack: Sensitivity=7, Attack=0, Peak=8. Snappy, vocal sweep on muted strums. Subtle: Sensitivity=3, Peak=3. Only hard picks lift the filter -- a touch-sensitive tone control. Slow bloom: Attack=10. The envelope charges through 100k: the filter swells open over a sustained note.

Filter.description: Electro-Harmonix Doctor Q envelope filter, modelled from Jack Orman's AMZ schematic, with AMZ's Dr. Quack rework as a version. A 1458 multiple-feedback band-pass (47k / .005u / .005u / 470k, +14 dB peak) whose resonance is set by a BC239C run as a base-current-controlled resistor (collector at 0 V): it sweeps about 210 Hz to 3 kHz (3.7 kHz at full Range), the Q rising with the frequency. The envelope comes from a 1458 rectifier stage with its + input on ground -- below the op-amp's own common-mode range on 9 V, so it idles at 1.78 V and half-wave rectifies around that --, a 1N914 into a 10 uF peak holder (attack ~1 V/ms, set by how much current the op-amp can source; release ~0.25 s through the Range pot) and a 22k into the transistor's base. The NORM/BASS switch turns the band-pass into a resonant low-pass that keeps the bass. Dr. Quack: a JFET input buffer, red LEDs on the rectifier (the filter parks lower and needs more signal to open), Range as a panel control. Faithful quirks: the filter's peak climbs at the top of the sweep and self-oscillates with Range near full and a hot envelope; hard attacks pull the unregulated supply down (a soft thump). Matches ngspice of the same schematics (transistor-level 741s): frozen-envelope response within 0.5 dB, envelope trajectory within ~0.05 V on tone bursts, guitar RMS within 0.4 dB.
Filter.name: EHX Doctor Q

params.desc: Sensitivity (100k audio pot across the input, feeding the rectifier): how hard the envelope is driven. 5 = 9 % of the input (only hard picks move it), 7 = 24 %, 10 = all of it (the 10 uF reaches 6 V and more)
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Range (25k linear pot between the envelope and the transistor's 22k base resistor; a trimmer inside the Doctor Q, a panel control on the Dr. Quack): how far a given envelope sweeps the filter. 0 = parked at ~210 Hz, 5 = up to ~3 kHz, 10 = up to ~3.7 kHz with a much sharper peak (self-oscillates with a hot envelope)
params.label: Range

params.desc: NORM/BASS (the DPDT): NORM = band-pass (+14 dB peak, no bass); BASS = the input enters the op-amp's summing node instead: a resonant low-pass, unity in the bass, the peak rising from +5 dB at the bottom of the sweep to +30 dB and more at the top
params.label: Mode

params.desc: Doctor Q = the E-H circuit (input straight into the pot and the filter, 1N914 rectifier, + on ground); Dr. Quack = AMZ's rework (2N5457 input buffer, red LED on the rectifier's + input and as its diode: the envelope idles lower, so the filter parks at the bottom and opens on firmer playing)
params.label: Version

Filter.usage: Classic quack: Sensitivity=7, Range=5, NORM. Each pick sweeps the peak up to ~2.3 kHz and lets it fall back over a quarter second. Subtle touch-wah: Sensitivity=4, Range=5. Only hard picks open it. Bass mode: Mode=BASS. A resonant low-pass instead of a band-pass: the low end stays, the resonance rides on top -- for bass, or a fuller guitar wah. Dr. Quack: Version=Dr. Quack, Sensitivity=9, Range=6. The rework: higher input impedance, the filter rests at the bottom and needs a firm pick to open. Squelch: Sensitivity=10, Range=9. Close to the edge: loud notes kick the filter to the top of its sweep where it rings hard (Range 10 tips it into self-oscillation on loud notes).

Filter.description: Electro-Harmonix Y-Triggered Filter (1976), modelled from its factory schematic: a TRIGGERED filter, not an envelope follower. A limiter (x58, diode-clipped), a precision rectifier and a log peak detector turn every note onset -- a step in level, however loud -- into a pulse, which a ringing op-amp stage and a transistor dump turn into a fixed sweep shape: a 'down' voltage that jumps on the attack and decays over ~150 ms, and an 'up' ramp that snaps low on the attack and climbs back over ~0.5 s. The Up/Down knob pans between the two into the CA3094 OTA that tunes the filter: a resonant (+4..+13 dB) peak sweeping from ~400 Hz to 2.3 kHz (3.3 kHz in Wide), over a fixed treble roll-off; hit hard, the OTA and its Darlington add their own grit. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.2 dB below 5 kHz at frozen control voltages, 0.07 dB per sine fundamental, 0.04 dB RMS on guitar, and within ~10-20 cents on the sweep of a clean attack. Level: unity at the defaults (the real circuit is +1.5 dB there).
Filter.name: EHX Y-Triggered Filter

params.desc: Up/Down (R38 100k linear): pans the OTA's control between the two trigger shapes. 0 = Down (closed at rest, opens on the pick and falls back in ~0.3 s), 10 = Up (open at rest, shut on the pick and back open over ~0.5 s). In between the shapes add: near 3 they cancel (the filter sits a third open and barely moves), 5-7 rest half open and dip on the pick
params.label: Up/Down

params.desc: The slide switch (positions marked DN / UP on the factory drawing). Wide (UP): R27 100k in the - input path, R31 shorted -- the peak reaches 3.3 kHz and rings harder (+7..+13 dB), with ~4 dB more bass. Narrow (DN): the peak tops out near 2.3 kHz, +4..+11 dB
params.label: Range

Filter.usage: Down sweep (classic): Up/Down=0, Range=Wide. Each pick opens the filter, then it falls closed -- the 'wow'. Up sweep: Up/Down=10, Range=Wide. Each pick snaps the filter shut and it rises over half a second -- a reverse, swelling 'bwow'. Tight funk: Up/Down=0, Range=Narrow. A smaller, darker quack for rhythm parts. Slow rise, narrow: Up/Down=10, Range=Narrow. Rising sweeps that stay in the mids. Half-open dip: Up/Down=6, Range=Wide. The filter rests half open and ducks on each pick, then recovers. Near 3 the two shapes cancel and the filter barely moves. Triggering wants an onset: legato notes that don't drop below a few mV between them won't retrigger -- pick each note, or mute between them.

Filter.description: Electro-Harmonix Zipper envelope follower (1977), modelled from its schematic: a 4558 state-variable filter whose two integrator resistors are 2N5457 JFETs, an LM324 half-wave rectifier (gain 150) charging a 4.7 uF envelope cap, and a third JFET in a servo loop that makes the filter's conductance follow the envelope current -- the filter sits at ~105 Hz and opens to ~1.1 kHz on normal playing (Range 5), past 2 kHz on a hard strum. Also in: the input's +21 dB bridged-T bump at 7.1 kHz, the JFETs slewing when the filter is nearly shut (its own grit), the rectifier's coupling caps that keep the sweep rising after you stop (toggle 1), the op-amp rails. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.4 dB small-signal across the sweep, 0.11 dB per fundamental, cutoff trajectory within a few cents on guitar. Level: unity at the defaults (the real pedal is ~9 dB louder there).
Filter.name: EHX Zipper

params.desc: Range (R39 10k, linear assumed): how much of the input the envelope detector hears, i.e. how far the filter opens. 0 = parked at ~105 Hz; 5 = up to ~1.1 kHz on normal playing, 10 = ~1.4 kHz (2 kHz+ on a hard strum)
params.label: Range

params.desc: Q (R38 100k, linear assumed): how little of the band-pass output is fed back as damping. 0 = a +3 dB bump, 5 = +13..18 dB peak, 10 = +16..23 dB
params.label: Q

params.desc: The toggle (DPDT). 1: the detector hears the whole signal and charges C16 through 33k (~0.15 s rise), and its coupling caps keep it charging for ~60 ms after the note stops: a swelling sweep that falls by half in ~0.2 s and settles in ~1 s. 2: .0033 uF in the detector's input (it hears mostly the pick, 3-8 kHz) and D7-D9 + 100 ohm charge C16 in milliseconds: it snaps open within ~10 ms of each attack and falls by half in ~0.1 s
params.label: Attack

params.desc: The slide switch: the low-pass (B2) or band-pass (A2) output of the state-variable filter
params.label: Mode

params.desc: The internal R32 25k trim pot (its setting is not on the schematic; 5 = mid assumed). It scales the whole sweep: 1 = ~170 Hz-5 kHz, 2.5 = ~120 Hz-2 kHz, 5 = ~105 Hz-1.1 kHz, 10 = ~50-750 Hz on the same playing (Range 5)
params.label: Trim

Filter.usage: Classic Zipper quack: Range=6, Q=6, Attack=1, Mode=BP. A vocal sweep that swells up on each phrase and lingers after it. Pick quack: Range=8, Q=7, Attack=2, Mode=BP. The detector hears mostly the pick: every note pops open and falls back within ~0.3 s. Slow swell: Range=7, Q=4, Attack=1, Mode=LP. Darker, rounded opening that hangs on through the next notes. Funk bass filter: Range=5, Q=7, Attack=2, Mode=LP. Low-pass squelch that follows every attack. Talking vowel: Range=6, Q=10, Attack=1, Mode=BP. Narrow, near-singing peak. Wider sweep: raise the internal trim's reach (Trim below 5): 2.5 sweeps ~120 Hz-2 kHz, 1 ~170 Hz-5 kHz on the same playing.

Filter.description: Envelope-controlled resonant filter (auto-wah).  Picking dynamics sweep a peak across [Frequency, Frequency+FreqDepth] on an exp curve.  Selectable Type (LP / BP / HP / PEQ).  BP is a parallel resonant-peak + gentle-skirt architecture (HX40 K22) that gives audible HP/LP edge sweep alongside the resonance.  Asymmetric envelope follower (user Attack + Decay) drives the filter; a sens-dependent floor (sens^12 × 0.95) holds fc high at Sensitivity=1.0 so modulations read as movement instead of full-range washing.  Quadratic + tanh soft-saturation injects analog-style 2nd-harmonic content.  FilterGain emphasises the wet peak; Level trims the overall output.  Designed to A/B against Helix HD2_FilterAutoFilter — surface widened from 5 to 11 params in HX40.
Filter.name: Envelope Filter

params.desc: Envelope gain. 0=needs hard picking, 0.4=Helix-tuned classic, 0.7=responsive, 1.0=very responsive (fc held high through note sustain via sens^12 floor).
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Resonance Q. 0.7=wide gentle, 6=classic wah, 7.5=Helix-tuned, 12=narrow vocal.
params.label: Peak

params.desc: Envelope attack time. 0.001=instant snappy, 0.011=Helix-tuned, 0.05=classic spongy, 0.15=slow vocal rise, 0.3=very slow.  Above ~30 ms the fc smoothing (always-on 100 ms LP) dominates the perceived attack character.
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Envelope release time. 0.01=snappy, 0.052=Helix-tuned (sharp per-pick re-trigger), 0.08=classic, 0.25=slow, 1.0=very slow, 2.0=hold-style.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: 0=Up (filter opens on attack), 1=Down (filter closes on attack).  ID kept as `mode` for backward compatibility with pre-HX40 chains.
params.label: Direction

params.desc: Filter sweep floor frequency in Hz.  50 Hz is the Helix-tuned default — gives a deep sub-bass quack at the bottom of the sweep.  Legacy hardcoded floor was 200.
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: Sweep range above the Frequency floor.  Sweep covers [Frequency, Frequency+FreqDepth] on an exp curve.  3500 is the Helix-tuned default — full 50..3550 Hz wah range.
params.label: FreqDepth

params.desc: 0=LP (low-pass, smooth open/close, fundamentals pass), 1=BP (parallel resonant peak + gentle skirts — Helix-tuned classic auto-wah), 2=HP (high-pass), 3=PEQ (peaking EQ — full dry passes at unity with a boost at fc).
params.label: Type

params.desc: Wet-path makeup gain.  Drives the soft-saturator that gives the analog 2nd-harmonic character.  9 dB is the Helix-tuned default; 0 = clean filter only, 18+ = heavy analog grit.
params.label: FilterGain

params.desc: Crossfade dry/wet. 0=dry only, 0.8=strong narrow peak, 1=wet only (Helix-tuned default).
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Output level trim (applied to dry+wet sum).  Mirrors Helix Level.
params.label: Level

Filter.usage: Helix-style vintage auto-wah: Sensitivity=0.4, Peak=7.5, Attack=0.011, Decay=0.052, Direction=Up, Frequency=50, FreqDepth=3500, Type=BP, FilterGain=9, Mix=1.0. Matches the Helix HD2_FilterAutoFilter default voicing — full sub-bass quack to bright wah quack range with analog-style saturation and held-high modulation at high Sensitivity. Classic funk: Sensitivity=0.5, Peak=6, Decay=0.08, Direction=Up, Type=BP, FilterGain=0. Quacky single-coil auto-wah. Subtle sweep: Sensitivity=0.3, Peak=4, Decay=0.12. Gentle filter opening. Sharp resonance: Peak=10+. Narrow, vocal, almost self-oscillating. Down direction: Direction=1. Filter closes on attack — darker, inverse wah feel. Wide sweep: Frequency=50, FreqDepth=3500. Reaches from sub-bass to bright wah — much wider than the legacy 200..3000 Hz range. LP mode: Type=LP. Smoother filter that opens and closes; less "vowel-like" than BP — lets dry note fundamentals pass under the resonance peak. PEQ mode: Type=PEQ. Full dry signal passes at unity with a boost at fc — useful when chaining with downstream tonal blocks that need the full-band dry intact. Decay: 10ms=snappy, 80ms=classic, 250ms=slow return, 1s=very slow, 2s=hold-style.

Filter.description: 3-band resonant formant filter with Peterson & Barney vowel table (A/E/I/O/U). Continuous vowel morphing via smooth interpolation. Shift transposes all formants by ±1 octave. Additive mix — formant peaks are boosted on top of the dry signal.
Filter.name: Formant Filter

params.desc: Vowel selection with morphing. 0=A, 1=E, 2=I, 3=O, 4=U. In-between values blend
params.label: Vowel

params.desc: Formant peak sharpness. 0=wide (Q=5), 1=narrow vocal (Q=30)
params.label: Resonance

params.desc: Transpose all formants. -1=octave down, 0=natural, +1=octave up
params.label: Shift

params.desc: Formant peak level. 0=dry only, 0.8=clear vowel character, 1=maximum resonance
params.label: Mix

Filter.usage: Vowel sweep: Automate Vowel 0→4 for wah-like A-E-I-O-U sweep. Fixed vowel: Set Vowel to 0=A, 1=E, 2=I, 3=O, 4=U for static tonal color. Resonance: 0=wide gentle peaks, 1=narrow vocal resonance. Sweet spot 0.5–0.7. Shift: -1=one octave down (deeper, darker vowels), +1=one octave up (brighter, thinner). Talk box effect: High Resonance + sweep Vowel manually or with expression.

Filter.description: High-pass that closes only while a plosive is present, so the voice keeps its chest weight the rest of the time. Detects the LF burst by shape, not level, so sung low notes pass untouched.
Filter.name: Plosive Tamer

params.desc: Depth of the sweep. 0 = inactive.
params.label: Amount

params.desc: How far the fast LF envelope must exceed its own slow baseline to count as a blast. Lower = triggers more readily.
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Resting high-pass cutoff, out of the way of the voice.
params.label: Rest Cut

params.desc: Cutoff when a blast is fully detected.
params.label: Max Cut

params.desc: Detector attack/release. Fast catches more of the blast front.
params.label: Speed

params.desc: How far the low band must exceed the 6 kHz band before anything is treated. THE control for false positives. Measured on an A-Z take, letters that pop and letters that do not OVERLAP on this measure, so this is an operating point, not a clean boundary: 24 sits above every non-popping letter and catches the ones actually heard popping. Lower to catch weaker plosives at the cost of thinning ordinary syllables. -99 disables the test.
params.label: Tilt Threshold

params.desc: How far BELOW programme level the low band may fall before triggering is blocked. Relative, not absolute dBFS, so it does not move with the mic or its gain. Without it the scale-free ratio fires on room tone.
params.label: Floor

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Filter.usage: Placement: first in the vocal chain, before the gate and compressor. Too many /p/ blasts still through? Lower Sensitivity or raise Max Cut. Low notes thinning? Raise Sensitivity — a sustained note raises the baseline and the ratio, not the level, is what triggers. Audible thump as it closes? Lower Speed.

Filter.description: Four classic analog synth filters -- Moog-style ladder, Oberheim SEM, Korg MS-20 and TB-303 diode -- with a filter envelope triggered by your picks, an envelope follower and an LFO. After a Harmonic Generator in Voice mode it turns the guitar into a synth voice with real filter sweeps, no MIDI needed.
Filter.name: Synth Filter

params.desc: Ladder = warm, fat Moog-style 24 dB low-pass. SEM = softer Oberheim-style 12 dB with low/band/high-pass, notch and morph. MS-20 = aggressive, screams at high resonance. Diode = squelchy TB-303 style.
params.label: Model

params.desc: Where the filter starts closing. The envelope, follower and LFO move it from here.
params.label: Cutoff

params.desc: Emphasis at the cutoff. Near 1 the Ladder, MS-20 and Diode whistle on their own (self-oscillation); the SEM never does, like the original. Ladder and Diode lose bass as it rises -- see Bass Comp.
params.label: Resonance

params.desc: Pushes the filter into saturation: thicker, grittier, and the resonance growls.
params.label: Drive

params.desc: SEM model only.
params.label: SEM Mode

params.desc: SEM Morph mode: 0 = low-pass, 1 = high-pass, in between a blend.
params.label: SEM Morph

params.desc: How far each pick opens the filter, in octaves above the cutoff (negative closes it). Picks come from the Harmonic Generator on the same Pick Bus.
params.label: Env Amount

params.desc: Time for the filter to open after a pick.
params.label: Env Attack

params.desc: Time to fall from fully open to the sustain level.
params.label: Env Decay

params.desc: How open it stays while the note rings (fraction of the full opening).
params.label: Env Sustain

params.desc: Closing time once the note has died away (a guitar has no note-off, so this starts when your playing falls silent).
params.label: Env Release

params.desc: How much harder picks open the filter further. 0 = every pick the same.
params.label: Env Velocity

params.desc: Which Harmonic Generator's picks trigger the envelope (match its Pick Bus). Off = no envelope.
params.label: Pick Bus

params.desc: Opens the filter with how loud you play (an auto-wah, on a synth filter). Octaves at full level.
params.label: Follow Amount

params.desc: How fast the follower reacts to getting louder.
params.label: Follow Attack

params.desc: How fast it settles back as you play softer.
params.label: Follow Release

params.desc: Depth of the cutoff wobble, in octaves.
params.label: LFO Amount

params.desc: Wobble speed when LFO Sync is off.
params.label: LFO Rate

params.desc: Shape of the wobble.
params.label: LFO Shape

params.desc: Locks the wobble to the session tempo (tap tempo, songs, drummer).
params.label: LFO Sync

params.desc: Restart the wobble on every pick.
params.label: LFO Retrigger

params.desc: Ladder and Diode: keeps the low end as resonance rises (the original circuits thin out).
params.label: Bass Comp

params.desc: Blend of filtered and unfiltered signal.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Output level.
params.label: Level

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

params.desc: 2x oversampling (keeps drive and resonance from aliasing). Leave on.
params.label: Oversample

Filter.usage: Start here: put it after a Harmonic Generator in Voice mode. Model Ladder, Cutoff 250 Hz, Resonance 0.5, Env Amount +4 oct, Decay 250 ms, Sustain 0.15 -- every pick plucks the filter open. Pads: SEM, Env Attack 400 ms, Decay 1.5 s, Sustain 0.6, a slow LFO. Acid: Diode, Resonance 0.85, Env Amount +4, Decay 180 ms, Sustain 0, Velocity high. Screaming lead: MS-20, Resonance 0.75, Drive 10 dB. Thin with resonance? raise Bass Comp (Ladder, Diode).
