Mastering.description: Final-stage true-peak limiter + LUFS meter. Every chain ends with one: it is pinned last and cannot be removed, only bypassed. With the default -1 dBFS ceiling, a chain that lives below -1 dBFS is bit-transparent — the only thing in path is a 3 ms look-ahead delay. When the chain does push past the ceiling, the limiter rides gain DOWN sample-accurately (instant attack via the look-ahead window) and releases over 100 ms.
Mastering.name: Bus Master

params.desc: True-peak ceiling. The limiter prevents output samples from exceeding this. Default -1.0 dBFS is broadcast-safe; -0.3 max for streaming.
params.label: Ceiling

Mastering.usage:
Ceiling: True-peak ceiling in dBFS. -1.0 is the broadcast-safe default. -0.3 squeezes more loudness at the cost of headroom for downstream DA jitter. -3.0 is mastering-safe.
Sticky: Every chain ends with this block, pinned last. No UI will delete it — bypass it (the dot on the block) to hear the chain unmastered. The meter publishes to /dev/shm/tonepi-busmaster.
Tonal character: If you see Gain Reduction > 2 dB in the meter, fix the gain stage upstream (lower NAM output_db, conv_cab level_db, or the amp master) rather than living on the limiter.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: Two engines. Classic: a modulated digital delay (sine LFO, gentle 8 kHz filtering, Mix knob). CE-2 models: the Boss CE-2 circuit -- pre/de-emphasis, 3rd-order Sallen-Key filters around the MN3007, the 106 Hz wet high-pass, triangle LFO and MN3101 clock -- checked against ngspice (test/spice/ce2).
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: Boss CE-2 Chorus

params.desc: Modulation speed in Hz. Low=slow sweep, high=fast wobble
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Full peak-to-peak delay swing. 1-2ms=classic chorus, 3-5ms=intense
params.label: Depth

params.desc: 0=fully dry, 0.5=equal blend, 1.0=fully wet
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Classic model only. 0=mono, 1=wide: right side carries the inverted wet (dry+wet / dry-wet, the CE-3 scheme)
params.label: Classic Stereo

params.desc: Classic = the original digital chorus (Rate/Depth/Mix/Classic Stereo). The CE-2 models are the Boss CE-2 circuit and use only CE-2 Rate and CE-2 Depth
params.label: Model

params.desc: CE-2 models: the pedal Rate knob (linear). Triangle LFO, 0.32 Hz at 0 to 3.56 Hz at 10
params.label: CE-2 Rate

params.desc: CE-2 models: the pedal Depth knob (linear). At 10 the delay sweeps 3.7 to 5.4 ms around 4.6 ms
params.label: CE-2 Depth

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Classic: Model=Classic; Rate, Depth, Mix and Classic Stereo apply. CE-2: Model=CE-2; only CE-2 Rate and CE-2 Depth apply, as on the pedal. Dry and wet are fixed 1:1, and the wet is added on top of the dry, so the output is slightly hotter in the mids. CE-2 Split: dry left, wet right -- the CE-1 two-output scheme. Wide in stereo, a normal chorus summed. CE-2 Wide: dry+wet left, dry-wet right (the CE-3 scheme). Collapses to dry in mono. Stereo input: CE-2 runs one pedal per side on one LFO; Split and Wide feed the pedal the L/R sum.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: MN3207 BBD flanger with Manual delay offset, bipolar resonance (negative=hollow, positive=metallic), triangle LFO with quadratic rate taper, and proper feedback loop topology. 1–13ms delay range, 4800Hz reconstruction filter.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: BBD Flanger

params.desc: Center delay offset. 0=1ms (treble comb), 5=7ms (mid), 10=13ms (bass comb)
params.label: Manual

params.desc: LFO swing around Manual center. 0=static comb, 10=full ±6ms sweep
params.label: Depth

params.desc: Manual LFO speed. 0=16s period, 5=~2.5Hz, 10=10Hz. Ignored when Sync is on
params.label: Rate

params.desc: 5=off. CCW(0)=negative/hollow. CW(10)=positive/metallic. Capped at ±0.70
params.label: Resonance

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=equal blend (hardware default), 1.0=wet only
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=manual Rate, 1=phase-locked to global BPM
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Classic sweep: Manual=5, Depth=5, Rate=5, Res=5. Balanced mid-range flange. Jet plane: Manual=5, Depth=8, Rate=3, Res=8. Positive feedback, wide sweep, metallic jet. Hollow tunnel: Manual=5, Depth=6, Rate=2, Res=2. Negative feedback, swooshing hollow. Manual: Sets center delay (1–13ms). Low=treble comb, high=bass comb. The defining control. Resonance: Center=off. CCW=negative (hollow), CW=positive (metallic). Never self-oscillates.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: Advanced chorus/vibrato with Warp shaping (sine→square), envelope-modulated depth, scalable Dimension/MultiLine (4/6/8 voices, Strymon Mobius-style), AR-followed wet-mix ducker (Strymon Ducked Chorus), and 90° stereo chorus. Inspired by Walrus Audio Julia + Strymon Mobius.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: Chorus / Vibrato

params.desc: Modulation rate in Hz
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Modulation depth. 0=none, 1=full ±4ms sweep
params.label: Depth

params.desc: 0=fully dry, 0.5=equal blend, 1.0=fully wet
params.label: Mix

params.desc: LFO shape: 0=pure sine (lush), 1=near square (aggressive clipped chorus)
params.label: Warp

params.desc: Picking dynamics affect depth. Positive=more depth when loud, negative=less
params.label: Env Influence

params.desc: 0=chorus (90° stereo), 1=dimension/multiline (quad/6/8 voice), 2=vibrato (wet only)
params.label: Type (0=Cho 1=Dim 2=Vib)

params.desc: Ducks the wet mix on transients. 0=off, 1=fully ducked at loud picking (Strymon Mobius Ducked Chorus). Bypasses on Vibrato (vib is always 100% wet).
params.label: Duck

params.desc: Duck envelope attack — fast=catches transient peak, slow=smoother ride.
params.label: Duck Attack

params.desc: Duck envelope release — how quickly the wet swells back after the transient.
params.label: Duck Release

params.desc: Voice count for Dimension/MultiLine mode. 2=two-tap (Helix 4Voice NumVoices=2 parity), 4=quad-phase Dim, 6/8=Strymon Mobius MultiLine (denser pad-like texture).  Voices each carry a phase-staggered LFO and a slightly different base delay so they cluster instead of phase-cancelling.
params.label: Voices (2/4/6/8)

params.desc: HPF on the wet/modulated signal — thins the chorus low-end pile-up.  40 Hz = effectively off.  Matches Helix HD2_Chorus4Voice HPFFrq.
params.label: Wet HPF

params.desc: High shelf on the wet signal — bright +3, dark -6.  Matches Helix HD2_Chorus4Voice HighShelf.
params.label: Wet HighShelf

params.desc: Output level trim — all Helix HD2_Chorus* blocks expose this as a wet/output multiplier separate from Mix.
params.label: Level

params.desc: Envelope threshold for the ducker — duck only activates when the input env crosses this level.  Models Helix HD2_FlangerDynamixFlanger Env Input.  Inactive when Duck=0.
params.label: Duck Threshold

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Chorus: Type=Cho, Warp=0, Duck=0. Clean 90° stereo chorus. Dimension (4 voices): Type=Dim, Voices=4. Quad-phase anti-phase pairs — classic Dimension-D widening. MultiLine (6 / 8 voices): Type=Dim, Voices=6 or 8. Strymon Mobius MultiLine pad — denser, more spread-out voices with staggered base delays so they cluster instead of phase-cancelling. Ducked Chorus: Type=Cho, Duck=0.5–1.0, DuckAttack=10 ms, DuckRelease=150 ms. Wet drops on the pick attack, swells back during the sustain — Strymon Mobius signature. Vibrato: Type=Vib. 100% wet pitch modulation (Duck ignored). Warp: 0=pure sine (transparent), 1=near square (aggressive clipped chorus). Env Influence: positive=more depth on loud picking, negative=less (independent of Duck).

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: DOD 565 Chorus (1981), modelled from its schematic: a Reticon SAD512D bucket brigade (512 stages, 2.4 to 5 ms) inside an NE571 compander -- the expander keyed from the undelayed compressor, so the wet accents each pick attack and carries the compander's ripple --, pre-/de-emphasis around it, a 7.5 kHz post-BBD filter, the TL062 relaxation-oscillator clock under a lopsided exponential TL022 LFO (0.45 to 11 Hz) that its 10 uF smoothing rounds and shrinks at speed. Dry and wet fixed 50/50, like the pedal. Matches ngspice of the same schematic: small signal within 0.4 dB to 6 kHz (1 dB to 10 kHz), sines within 0.3 dB, LFO rate within 2.5 %, delay sweep within 2 %.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: DOD 565 Chorus

params.desc: Speed (500k log rheostat with 18k): LFO 0.45 Hz at 0, ~3.5 Hz at 5, 11 Hz at 10
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Depth (100k linear): blends the LFO into the clock control against the Delay Time setting; at 10 the LFO alone sets the delay
params.label: Depth

params.desc: Delay Time (100k linear): the BBD clock centre, ~2.5 ms at 0 to ~5 ms at 10 (at Depth 0; Depth narrows its range)
params.label: Delay Time

params.desc: Which jack: OUT 1 (dry + wet) or OUT 2 (dry + inverted wet)
params.label: Output

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Classic 565: Speed=5, Depth=5, Delay Time=5. A gentle, warm chorus. Slow shimmer: Speed=1.5, Depth=8, Delay Time=4. Wide, slow pitch drift. Deep wobble: Speed=3, Depth=10. Depth at 10 takes the delay straight from the LFO -- Delay Time no longer matters. Fast vibe: Speed=8, Depth=7, Delay Time=3. The LFO filter tames the depth at speed, as on the pedal. Doubler: Speed=2, Depth=2, Delay Time=9. Longer, nearly static delay. (Depth 0 with Delay Time 10 stops the clock: dry only.) Output: OUT 1 = dry + wet (the mono jack), OUT 2 = dry - wet (the second jack: hollow, bass-light). A stereo node runs the same output on both sides.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: DOD 575 Flanger (Performer series, 18 V), modelled from its schematic: a SAD512 bucket brigade inside an NE571 compander, the input op-amp's pre-emphasis (which colours the dry path too: about -5 dB at 1-2 kHz, +4 dB at 10 kHz), Regen taken from the reconstruction filter back into the BBD input -- up to +16 dB comb peaks, and the filter's op-amp clips when it rings --, and a Schmitt / integrator LFO whose triangle reaches the CD4007 clock through three diodes, so the sweep lingers at its long-delay end (0.32-5.2 ms at full Width). Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.4 dB small-signal away from notch bottoms (comb peaks within 0.2 dB), 0.1 % in LFO rate, 0.5 % in delay, and 0.0 dB RMS on guitar.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: DOD 575 Flanger

params.desc: Speed (500K reverse log + 2K, the LFO integrator's charging resistor): 0 = 0.044 Hz (23 s), 2.5 = 0.14 Hz, 5 = 0.45 Hz, 7.5 = 1.6 Hz, 10 = 8.9 Hz
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Width (100K linear, between the LFO triangle and Vref): how much of the triangle reaches the clock. 0 = fixed 0.75 ms; 5 = 0.71-3.3 ms; 10 = 0.32-5.2 ms. The diodes in the control path stretch the long-delay end
params.label: Width

params.desc: Regen (100K linear): the filtered BBD output fed back into the BBD input. 0 = none (notches -25 dB), 5 = moderate, 10 = loop gain 0.95 (peaks +16 dB, rings)
params.label: Regen

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Classic: Speed=5, Width=5, Regen=5. A 2-second sweep between 0.7 and 3.3 ms, moderate resonance, unity level. Jet: Speed=2, Width=10, Regen=9. A slow 0.3-5 ms swoop with a ringing, metallic comb. Subtle: Speed=4, Width=3, Regen=0. A gentle shimmer, no resonance. Fast warble: Speed=8, Width=6, Regen=3. About 2 Hz, chorus-like. Static comb: Width=0. The sweep stops at 0.75 ms; Regen sets how much it rings. Regen 10: loop gain 0.95 in band: strong peaks, and the filter's op-amp clips on loud notes.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: Mu-Tron Bi-Phase / EH Dynamix-style envelope-driven flanger.  The delay-line sweep is steered by the player's picking envelope instead of a free LFO -- heavy attacks push the comb up the spectrum, lighter playing relaxes it back down.  Phasing morphs between vibrato (short delays, inverted wet), flange, and chorus (long delays) territory.  Recycle gates the feedback loop.  CV Tracking blends LFO and envelope drive; with CV Tracking on, the LFO contribution is fully replaced by the envelope.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: Dynamic Flanger

params.desc: Free-LFO speed.  Ignored when CV Tracking is on.
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Modulation depth.  0 = static delay (no sweep), 1 = full LFO / envelope swing across the Max Delay range
params.label: Depth

params.desc: Centre delay before LFO/envelope modulation. 0 = 1 ms (high comb), 1 = (Max Delay) ms (low comb)
params.label: Manual

params.desc: 0 = dry, 0.5 = equal blend, 1 = wet only
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Wet character morph.  -1 = inverted wet (vibrato/null comb), 0 = standard flange, +1 = chorus (longer wet delay offset)
params.label: Phasing

params.desc: 0 = single-pass comb, 1 = feedback loop enabled (metallic ring builds with successive taps)
params.label: Recycle (0/1)

params.desc: Envelope amount.  Scales how strongly the picking envelope drives the delay sweep when CV Tracking is on.
params.label: CV Dynamics

params.desc: Maximum delay value.  Sets the upper bound of the sweep range; lower values keep the wet in flange territory, higher values move to chorus.
params.label: Max Delay

params.desc: 0 = LFO drives the sweep, 1 = picking envelope drives the sweep (LFO disabled)
params.label: CV Tracking (0/1)

params.desc: Envelope follower attack/release time constant.  Short = snappy / quacky; long = slow / vowel-like.
params.label: Env Lag

params.desc: Envelope input sensitivity.  Scales the picking signal before it hits the follower; 0 = no response, 1 = max gain (peak follower output).
params.label: Env Input

params.desc: Output trim in dB
params.label: Level

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Bi-Phase wah-flange: CV Tracking=On, CV Dynamics=1.0, Env Lag=15 ms, Env Input=0.5, Phasing=-0.5, Recycle=On. Sweeps the comb with picking attack — funk / disco / Stevie Wonder Talking Book. Static LFO flange: CV Tracking=Off, Speed=0.5 Hz, Depth=0.6, Phasing=0, Recycle=Off. Classic free-LFO sweep. Helix Dynamix preset: CV Tracking=On, CV Dynamics=1.0, Manual=0.42, Mix=0.5, Phasing=-1.0, Recycle=On, Max Delay=10 ms, Env Lag=100 ms, Env Input=0.7 (HD2_FlangerDynamixFlanger stored defaults). Phasing: -1 = vibrato (inverted wet, comb nulls dominate), 0 = standard flange, +1 = chorus (long delays). Recycle: off = single-pass comb; on = feedback loop with positive coupling (metallic ring builds over taps).

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: Warm BBD flanger with Filter Matrix (LFO freeze for static comb filtering), sine LFO, positive-only Color feedback approaching self-oscillation, and Range control that opens the sweep downward. 3500Hz reconstruction filter for dreamy, dark character. 1.5–8ms delay range.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: EHX Electric Mistress

params.desc: Manual LFO speed. 0=0.05Hz (20s atmospheric), 0.5=~1.3Hz, 1=5Hz. Ignored when Sync is on
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Sweep width downward. 0=narrow (±0.1ms), 1=full (2–8ms sweep)
params.label: Range

params.desc: Positive feedback. 0=clean, 0.7=prominent resonance, 1.0=near self-oscillation
params.label: Color

params.desc: Freeze LFO → static comb filter. Position depends on where LFO was when engaged. Overrides Sync (FM freezes the LFO entirely)
params.label: Filter Matrix

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=equal blend (hardware default), 1.0=wet only
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=manual Rate, 1=phase-locked to global BPM. Filter Matrix=On overrides this (LFO is frozen).
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Classic sweep: Rate=0.3, Range=0.5, Color=0.3. Warm breathing flange. Filter Matrix: FM=on. Freezes the LFO — static comb filter for chimey, metallic tonal color. The Andy Summers sound. Self-oscillation: Color=0.9+. Creamy sustained resonance, warm vocal quality. Range: Sets how far the sweep opens downward. 0=narrow/subtle, 1=full 2–8ms sweep. vs BBD Flanger: Warmer (3.5kHz vs 4.8kHz filter), sine LFO (breathing vs chop), positive-only feedback.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: EH Polychorus / Bad Stone-style harmonic flanger. Three parallel delay lines at harmonically related base times (T0, T0/2, T0/3) so the comb peaks reinforce at musical intervals (octave + fifth) instead of the equally-spaced linear comb of a single-line flanger.  Bipolar Enhance (feedback) goes from hollow → metallic; Manual shifts the centre delay; Spread distributes the three voices across the stereo image.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: Harmonic Flanger

params.desc: LFO speed.  Low = slow sweep / drifting harmonics, high = fast metallic wobble
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Modulation depth.  0 = static comb (Filter Matrix-like), 1 = full ±4 ms LFO swing across all three voices
params.label: Depth

params.desc: Centre delay (T0).  0 = 1.5 ms (treble comb), 0.5 = 4.5 ms, 1 = 9 ms (bass comb)
params.label: Manual

params.desc: Feedback intensity.  0 = strong negative (hollow), 0.5 = clean (no feedback), 1 = strong positive (metallic)
params.label: Enhance

params.desc: Stereo distribution.  0 = mono (all voices centred), 1 = max width (voices hard L / centre / R)
params.label: Spread

params.desc: 0 = dry, 0.5 = equal blend, 1 = wet only
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Output trim in dB
params.label: Level

params.desc: 0 = manual Rate, 1 = phase-locked to global BPM
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Classic chime: Rate=0.5, Depth=0.6, Manual=0.5, Enhance=0.3, Spread=0.3. Shimmering harmonic comb. Jet octave: Manual=0.7, Depth=0.8, Enhance=0.7. Slow, deep sweep with metallic feedback. Mike Matthews / EH: Manual=0.84, Depth=0.8, Enhance=0.3 (Helix HD2_FlangerHarmonicFlanger stored defaults). Enhance: 0.5=off. CCW=hollow (negative feedback). CW=metallic (positive feedback). Capped at ±0.65 to stay below self-oscillation.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: Julia-style multi-mode chorus. D-C-V morphing (dry→chorus→vibrato), phase-lag stereo LFO, tri/sine waveshape switch. 8ms center delay for thick, lush character.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: Walrus Audio Julia

params.desc: Modulation speed in Hz. Low=slow sweep, high=fast wobble
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Full peak-to-peak delay swing. 1-4ms=classic chorus, 5-7ms=extreme
params.label: Depth

params.desc: Phase offset between L/R LFOs. 0=mono, 0.5=90° wide, 1=180° max spread
params.label: Lag

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=chorus (equal-power dry+wet, bass kept dry), 1.0=vibrato (wet only). Same level as bypass at every setting
params.label: D-C-V

params.desc: 0=triangle wave (classic), 1=sine wave (smoother)
params.label: Wave

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Chorus: D-C-V=0.5. Equal dry/wet blend — standard chorus. Vibrato: D-C-V=1.0. 100% wet, pure pitch modulation. Dry boost: D-C-V=0.0. Clean signal with just the body of the pedal. Lag: 0=mono, 0.5=90° stereo rotation, 1.0=180° max L/R opposition. Triangle: Classic CE-2 feel. Sine: smoother, more subtle.

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.description: Artificial double tracking. Two or four detuned, drifting copies panned around the dry voice — a solo singer sounds doubled without a pitch shifter, so consonants stay sharp.
Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.name: Vocal Double

params.desc: How many doubles. 2 = wide pair, 4 = thicker bed.
params.label: Voices

params.desc: Peak pitch deviation of the doubles, in cents. This sets how far the delay swings — it is not a pitch shifter.
params.label: Detune

params.desc: How fast each double wanders. Slow is more human; fast becomes chorus.
params.label: Drift

params.desc: Base offset of the doubles. Beyond ~30 ms they stop fusing and read as slap.
params.label: Delay

params.desc: Stereo width of the doubles. The dry voice never moves.
params.label: Spread

params.desc: Low-pass on the doubles only. Lower tucks them behind the lead.
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Loudness of the doubles against the dry voice.
params.label: Level

params.desc: Blend of the doubled signal.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Modulation / Chorus & Flanger.usage: Start here: 2 voices, Detune 8 c, Drift 0.25 Hz, Level 0.7. Wider: raise Spread, then go to 4 voices — level is compensated so it thickens rather than jumps. Too obviously an effect? Lower Detune first, then Level. Above ~15 cents it reads as chorus. Slap instead of thickening? Delay above ~30 ms stops fusing — bring it back to 18-25 ms. Doubles too present: lower Tone to tuck them behind the lead.

Modulation / Guitar Sim.description: Mono magnetic-pickup → mic'd acoustic transform. Five instrument morphs (Steel acoustic, Classical/Nylon, 12-string, Ukulele, Mandolin) with per-instrument body resonances, sympathetic strings, attack shaping driven by transient_detector, body cavity reverb, mic-distance simulation, optional double-track, and a body IR convolution stage with unity-bypass-at-zero. Capo (0–7) raises resonant + presence frequencies and shortens sympathetic delays (physics: capo raises pitch). String gauge re-balances bass/treble. Pair with a downstream stereo block for stereo width.
Modulation / Guitar Sim.name: Acoustic Simulator

params.desc: 0=Steel acoustic, 1=Classical/Nylon, 2=12-string, 3=Ukulele, 4=Mandolin. Live — switching resets filter states (audible glitch < 1 frame).
params.label: Instrument

params.desc: 0=bright/native character, 10=heavily darkened. Drives brightness EQ tilt + body cavity damping fc + attack-presence centre.
params.label: Darkness

params.desc: 0=damped/dead, 10=ringing/sympathetic. Drives body-mode Q, sympathetic mix, and body-cavity feedback gain.
params.label: Resonance

params.desc: 0=small/tight (parlour, ukulele body), 10=large/resonant (jumbo, dreadnought). Morphs ER timing, RT60, and bass response together.
params.label: BodySize

params.desc: Cut-through-the-mix EQ. -4 dB at 0, +4 dB at 10. Centre frequency morphs per instrument and rises with Capo.
params.label: Presence

params.desc: High shelf at 10 kHz. -3 dB at 0, +3 dB at 10. Mimics good condenser HF extension.
params.label: Air

params.desc: 0=near soundhole (warm, more bass), 10=bridge saddle (bright, thinner). Sets the pickup-correction LP/HP corners.
params.label: PickupPos

params.desc: 0=open, 1–7 = fret position. Raises resonance + presence frequencies AND shortens sympathetic delays by 2^(capo/12) — physically correct (capo raises pitch).
params.label: Capo

params.desc: 0=light/extra-light (bright, thin bass), 10=heavy (warm, fat bass). Re-balances brightness EQ.
params.label: StringGauge

params.desc: 0=close mic'd (boxy, proximity bass), 10=far mic'd (airy, more room HF, less proximity).
params.label: MicDist

params.desc: 0=off, 1=on. Adds a second take via micro-delay + slow drift LFO — natural thickening of an acoustic track.
params.label: DoubleTrack

params.desc: 0 = bypass body IR (output unaffected, unity gain). 1 = fully wet IR convolution. Per-instrument body IR loaded from the Acoustic IRs directory configured under Settings → Directory Paths → Acoustic IRs (/root/uploads/Acoustic by default). Convolver always runs so turning it up doesn't take ~1 frame to bloom.
params.label: IR Mix

Modulation / Guitar Sim.usage: Strummed steel acoustic: Instrument=Steel, Darkness=4, BodySize=7, Presence=6, IR=0.5. Open dread tone. Fingerstyle nylon: Instrument=Classical, Darkness=6, Resonance=7, MicDist=3. Warm, intimate. 12-string jangle: Instrument=12-string, BodySize=8, Resonance=7, Air=7. Lush octave shimmer. Ukulele: Instrument=Ukulele, BodySize=2, Darkness=2, Presence=7. Bright, percussive. Mandolin: Instrument=Mandolin, BodySize=1, Resonance=8, Presence=8. Tight, articulate. Doubled rhythm: Instrument=Steel, DoubleTrack=On, MicDist=6. Doubled-take texture. Capo'd folk: Instrument=Steel, Capo=5, BodySize=6. Resonances raised a 4th, sympathetic strings shortened. IR-only character: Set IR_Mix=1, BodySize=0, Resonance=0. Body IR alone (bypasses the biquad-modeled body).

Modulation / Guitar Sim.description: Mono PCM tone transformer. Applies a target guitar's pickup + body signature (Strat / Tele / HB) to the live signal via source de-colour EQ -> target peak -> body resonance -> magnetic nonlinearity -> pickup LP. Pass-through when no designer cfg has been pushed.
Modulation / Guitar Sim.name: Guitar Xform

params.desc: 0 = fully dry (input passes unchanged), 0.5 = equal blend, 1.0 = fully processed.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Per-band signal level below which the transform passes through raw (the 4-band split is low / low-mid / hi-mid / hi via Linkwitz-Riley crossovers at 250, 1k, 4k Hz). Bands where envelope < threshold cross-fade to dry, so the tanh nonlinearity / comb / body biquads do not shape the noise floor that sits in those bands. Smooth attack/release prevents clicks at the edge. Set to 0 dB to disable (always fully wet) — restores pre-2026-06 behaviour.
params.label: Noise Thresh

params.desc: Live output trim applied AFTER the mix, on top of the preset's baked-in `output_gain_db` (which only touches the wet path). Use to fine-tune per-guitar level so a humbucker doesn't slam downstream amp / NAM blocks harder than a single-coil. 0 = no change; typical HB trims land around -3 to -6 dB when the preset itself hasn't already accounted for the pickup.
params.label: Output Trim

params.desc: Compile-time preset selector. Edit via /guitar_xform designer. Replay chain to apply.
params.label: Preset

params.desc: 1 = read live cfg from /dev/shm/tonepi-gx-designer (v1 default).
params.label: Designer Mode

Modulation / Guitar Sim.usage:
Setup: Open the /guitar_xform designer modal to load a target preset (Strat neck SC, Tele bridge SC, HB, etc.) or build a custom one. All processing is designer-driven; the block reads config from /dev/shm/tonepi-gx-designer.
Bypass: use this block's standard bypass toggle.
Source de-colour: the 10-band EQ in section 1 should be tuned to FLATTEN your physical pickup's spectral signature so the rest of the chain starts from a neutral signal.

Modulation / Guitar Sim.description: MIDI-driven additive guitar synthesiser blended with dry PCM. 10 harmonics + PCM, each with own 10-band EQ + ADSR. Pickup comb + body resonance + optional non-linearity for realistic Strat / Tele / LP / Ibanez modeling. Pass-through when MIDI is inactive.
Modulation / Guitar Sim.name: MIDI Guitar Sim

params.desc: Compile-time preset selector. Edit via /midi_guitar_sim designer. Replay chain to apply.
params.label: Preset

Modulation / Guitar Sim.usage:
Setup: Open the /midi_guitar_sim designer modal to load a guitar profile (Strat, Tele, LP, Ibanez, etc.) or build a custom one. The block runs in designer mode only — all per-harmonic + per-channel + body-EQ configuration is pushed via shm from the modal.
Bypass: use this block's standard bypass toggle.
MIDI source: any Tripleplay-format hex-pickup feed (per-string MIDI channels). Block reads from /dev/shm/tonepi-midi.

Modulation / Guitar Sim.description: Standalone 12-string guitar emulator.  Frequency-split DSP: low band (< 500 Hz) drives a Signalsmith Stretch +1 octave shifter — the doubled lower 4 string pairs (E/A/D/G); high band feeds a modulated-delay chorus — the unison-doubled top 2 string pairs (B / high E) with their natural ~10-cent mechanical detune.  Onset gating fires the wet voice on each pick attack so the chime fades with the natural note envelope, matching Helix VIC_PitchTwelveString surface 1:1.
Modulation / Guitar Sim.name: Twelve String

params.desc: 0 = dry only (wet silent), 1 = wet voice at full level.  Dry stays at unity throughout (Helix wet-add semantics).
params.label: Blend

params.desc: Low-shelf on the WET only (dry unaffected).  0 = -6 dB, 0.5 = flat, 1 = +6 dB at 200 Hz.
params.label: Bass

params.desc: High-shelf on the WET only.  0 = -6 dB, 0.5 = flat, 1 = +6 dB at 4 kHz.
params.label: Treble

params.desc: 0 = Low (fires on light picks — most sensitive), 1 = Med (default), 2 = High (needs a hard pick — least sensitive).
params.label: OnsetThresh

params.desc: Output level trim, applied to the dry+wet sum.
params.label: Level

Modulation / Guitar Sim.usage:
Classic jangle: Blend=0.5, Bass=0.4, Treble=0.6, OnsetThresh=Med. Bright Byrds-style chime.
Subtle thickener: Blend=0.25, OnsetThresh=Low. Adds octave shimmer without dominating.
Aggressive ring: Blend=0.8, OnsetThresh=High. Wet voice fires only on loud picks but cuts through hard.

Modulation / MIDI & Arp.description: Sequenced pitch arpeggiator with 8 programmable steps. v2: native pitch_shift.h (handles ratio=1.0 cleanly, 5 ms internal ratio smoothing, per-instance delay lines), per-step velocity, direction control (Up / Down / Up-Down ping-pong), hold mode (run on silence), and step-count cap. Stereo detuning (±0.04 st) plus tiny ratio jitter (±5 cents) for natural thickening. Formant compensation restores guitar body (~350 Hz).

Voices: 1, 2, or 3 simultaneous harmony lines.
Key + Scale: determines what "diatonic third" / "fifth" / etc. mean.
Interval (per voice): scale degrees above (+) or below (-) the input. +2 = third, +4 = fifth, +6 = seventh, -3 = third below, etc.
Octave (per voice): additional ±N octaves.
Level (per voice): output gain for that voice in the sum.
Dry Level: dry guitar signal in the mix.
Latency: 60 ms (bass Stretch block, configurable via Settings → MIDI).

Modulation / MIDI & Arp.description: MIDI-driven pitch shifter. Shifts the audio by a configurable interval in semitones, gated so the wet voice only plays when there is both audio and a held Tripleplay MIDI note. Signalsmith Stretch engine at 20 ms latency with formant preservation. Falls through to dry when MIDI mode is off (tp_midi_active() == 0).
Modulation / MIDI & Arp.name: MIDI Pitch Shift

params.desc: Pitch shift in semitones (continuous; bend rides on top of integer semitones)
params.label: Interval

params.desc: 0 = dry only, 1 = wet only, 0.5 = balanced
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Mute wet output when no Tripleplay MIDI note is currently held
params.label: MIDI Gate

params.desc: Stretch only: 3 instances run at 15/30/60 ms blocks per frequency range. Off: each plays at its native latency (treble faster, bass slower — inconsistent feel and audible click on range crossings). On (default): all aligned to 60 ms — uniform feel, glitch-free crossfades. Ignored when Engine = PSOLA.
params.label: Align Latency

params.desc: Stretch: 3-instance phase vocoder, formant preservation, sample-rate-independent latency. Good for chord work and high-register material. Known artifact on low notes: dry harmonic leak + inharmonic spurs from STFT hop modulation. PSOLA: pitch-synchronous overlap-add driven by MIDI T₀. Strictly monophonic but artifact-free on low notes since synthesis is locked to the actual period — no FFT bin grid and no hop schedule.
params.label: Engine

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Modulation / MIDI & Arp.usage: Interval: Pitch shift in semitones (-24..+24). Fine resolution lets pitch-bend ride on top. Mix: 0 = dry only, 1 = wet only, 0.5 = balanced. Gate: Onset gate ON (default) waits for BOTH audio + MIDI before producing the wet voice — prevents stale-note bleed on note transitions. OFF lets the shifter run continuously (good for sustained tones, less crisp on note changes). Latency: 20 ms (Signalsmith Stretch block 960 / hop 240 at 48 kHz). The dry path is unaffected; only the wet voice carries the latency.

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.description: 4-stage allpass phaser with negative Color feedback for deep, resonant notches. Lower fc range (450–3600Hz) than Script Phaser for warmer body. Triangle LFO, exponential sweep. Color=0 is clean phasing; Color=1 is the haunting, vocal resonant sound.
Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.name: Color Phaser

params.desc: Manual LFO rate. 0=0.1Hz (10s period), 0.5=~1.3Hz (classic), 1=5Hz. Ignored when Sync is on
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Negative feedback intensity. 0=clean phasing, 0.5=moderate resonance, 1=deep haunting notch
params.label: Color

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=equal blend (hardware default, max notch depth), 1.0=wet only
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=manual Speed, 1=phase-locked to global BPM
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.usage: Color off: Color=0. Clean 4-stage phasing, warmer than Script Phaser. Color on: Color=1. Deep resonant notch with emphasis shoulders — the signature sound. Sweet spot: Color=0.5–0.8, Speed=0.3. Resonant but not extreme. Gilmour lead: Color=1, Speed=0.3, Mix=0.5. Sustained, singing, haunting. vs Script Phaser: Warmer (450–3600Hz vs 600–4800Hz), feedback adds resonance that Script lacks.

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.description: DOD 595 Phasor (Performer series, 18 V), modelled from the DOD factory schematic: six TL022 all-pass stages swept by three VTL5C4/2 vactrols (one LED, two light-dependent resistors each), a TL022 relaxation LFO whose 15 uF timing cap drives the LEDs through a buffer -- an exponential-triangle sweep that the cells' slow darkening (~0.2 s) rounds into a lopsided, lingering throb --, Regen feedback from the wet output into the first stage (resonant peaks up to +26 dB at 10), and a Tone control that is the pre-emphasis half of a pre/de-emphasis noise-reduction pair. The six stages put three notches in band, sweeping about 1.2-6.9 kHz for the stage corner (first notch ~250 Hz-1.9 kHz). Matches ngspice of the same schematic: LFO rate within 0.1 %, frozen-sweep response within 0.4 dB 20 Hz-10 kHz (0.75 dB at full Regen), guitar RMS within 0.05 dB with the LFO running.
Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.name: DOD 595 Phaser

params.desc: Speed (D500KRL reverse-log 500k rheostat + 4.7k charging the 15 uF timing cap): 0 = 0.095 Hz (10.5 s), 5 = 0.91 Hz, 7.5 = 2.7 Hz, 10 = 7.7 Hz. At high speeds the vactrols no longer reach their dark end and the sweep narrows to its top
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Regen (D100K linear): the wet output back through .047 uF + 4.7k into the first stage. 0 = no feedback, 10 = resonant peaks of +20..26 dB between the notches
params.label: Regen

params.desc: Tone (D500KRL rheostat in the input stage's pre-emphasis; the output mixer's de-emphasis is fixed): 5 = about flat (within 1.2 dB), 0 = -8 dB at 1 kHz to -11 dB at 8 kHz (dark), 10 = +8 dB at 3 kHz rising to +12.5 dB at 8 kHz
params.label: Tone

params.desc: The pedal's footswitch (CD4007 flip-flop -> J113 in the wet path, ramped by 1M / .047 uF: ~40 ms off, ~25 ms on). Off leaves the dry signal through the input / mixer buffers
params.label: Effect

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.usage: Classic DOD swirl: Speed=4, Tone=5, Regen=3. Half-hertz sweep, gentle resonance, unity level. Slow jet: Speed=1, Tone=6, Regen=8. A 5-second sweep with a strong resonant peak riding the notches. Fast warble: Speed=8, Tone=5, Regen=2. The cells can't fully darken at this rate: a narrower, brighter wobble. Dark and deep: Speed=3, Tone=2, Regen=5. Less pre-emphasis: rounder, the notches lower in the mix. Resonant sweep: Speed=2, Tone=7, Regen=10. Maximum regeneration, close to singing. Bypassed buffer: Effect=Off. The pedal's own bypass: the dry signal through its pre/de-emphasis buffer (3 dB below the effect at the default level cal).

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.description: Electro-Harmonix Bad Stone (1975, the CD4049 original), modelled from its schematic: five all-pass stages swept by CD4049UB inverters used as voltage-controlled resistors, plus a fixed sixth phase stage with x10 gain, the whole loop fed back through the Feedback control. A servo op-amp linearises the sweep (the sweep follows the LFO's current, not the CMOS threshold); the LFO is the pedal's own integrator / Schmitt / transistor oscillator with its lopsided exponential sweep -- 0.17 Hz to 64 Hz, a stage's corner swinging 125 Hz - 6.9 kHz at slow rates and shrinking at the fastest ones as the servo can't keep up. The output is dark (a -17 dB treble shelf above ~1.5 kHz at the output node, as drawn). The CMOS channels rectify near the slow end of the sweep: a little grit on hard picks. Matches ngspice of the same schematic: notches within ~1 %, 0.14 dB per fundamental, LFO period within 0.3 %, 0.15 dB RMS on guitar with the LFO running. Level: unity at the defaults (the real circuit is -8 dB there).
Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.name: EHX Bad Stone

params.desc: Rate (R53 1M rheostat, reverse-audio law): the LFO, 0.17 Hz at 0, 0.56 Hz at 2.5, 1.9 Hz at 5, 7.1 Hz at 7.5, 64 Hz at 10. Inactive in Manual
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Feedback (R51 100k rheostat, reverse-audio law): how much of the phase-shifted output returns to the input -- at 0 almost no notches, at 10 deep resonant ones (-5 dB level)
params.label: Feedback

params.desc: Manual Shift pedal (R52 100k linear). 0=heel (low end of the sweep), 1=toe down (top). Only in Manual mode
params.label: Position

params.desc: The slide / foot switch: Auto = the LFO sweeps; Manual = the Manual Shift pedal sets the sweep (the LFO is disconnected)
params.label: Mode

params.desc: The Color switch. On (closed, the normal phaser): the input and the feedback meet at the loop's input and feed the output. Off: no feedback and only the shifted signal at the output -- vibrato
params.label: Color

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.usage: Classic Bad Stone: Rate=3-5, Feedback=5, Auto, Color On. The slow, deep 70s sweep. Resonant: Feedback=8-10. Sharper, peaky notches (the level drops a few dB). Leslie-ish warble: Rate=7-8, Feedback=3. Vibrato: Color=Off takes the dry signal out of the output (wet only) -- a pitch wobble, best at Rate 5-7. Manual Shift (frozen phase): Mode=Manual and park or rock Position (bind it to an expression pedal): heel = the sweep's low end, toe = the top. Feedback full up for the most vocal 'cocked' sound.

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.description: 4-stage non-uniform allpass phaser with incandescent lamp thermal model. Wildly different capacitor values per stage (15nF/220nF/470pF/4.7nF) create notches in the body register (67–669Hz) rather than presence. Lamp asymmetry (20ms heat, 80ms cool) produces organic pulse-and-drag character that compresses depth at high speeds. Chorus/Vibrato modes.
Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.name: Shin-ei Uni-Vibe

params.desc: LFO rate. 0=0.5Hz (slow languid), 0.5=~2.4Hz (classic), 1=8Hz (fast Leslie)
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Lamp excursion / fc sweep width. 0=static, 0.7=classic, 1=full range
params.label: Depth

params.desc: 0=Chorus (dry+wet phasing), 1=Vibrato (wet only, pitch wobble)
params.label: Vibrato

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=equal blend (hardware default), 1.0=wet only
params.label: Mix

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.usage: Classic vibe: Speed=0.5, Depth=0.7, Chorus. Thick, warm, wobbly phasing. Slow & languid: Speed=0.1, Depth=0.7. Hendrix "Machine Gun" territory. Fast Leslie: Speed=0.9+. Depth self-compresses from lamp inertia — authentic. Vibrato: Vibrato=on. Wet only — pitch wobble, no phase cancellation. vs Script/Color Phaser: Notch is an octave lower (body register). Non-uniform stages create complex shimmer. Lamp gives organic, asymmetric character.

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.description: MXR Phase 90, modelled from its schematic (Script Logo, and the Block Logo's R28 feedback): four 2N5952 JFET all-pass stages whose channel resistance the LFO sweeps -- two notches, 66-1570 Hz and 385-8900 Hz at the slow end --, the 741 Schmitt-trigger LFO charging a 15 uF cap through the Speed pot (0.13 Hz to 9.8 Hz, a slightly lopsided triangle at the gates), and the 2N4125 mixer. The JFETs are SPICE's square-law channel: on a hard pick they bend the signal, most at the slow end of the sweep -- the Phase 90's grit. Matches ngspice of the same schematic within 0.5 dB small-signal (notches within 1 %), 0.4 dB per harmonic and 1 % in LFO rate.
Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.name: MXR Phase 90

params.desc: Speed (R36 470k reverse log + 4k7, the LFO's charging resistor): 0 = 0.13 Hz, 0.25 = 0.43 Hz, 0.5 = 1.3 Hz, 0.75 = 3.7 Hz, 1 = 9.8 Hz. Ignored when Sync is on
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Not on the pedal: the dry (R16) / phased (R8) resistors into the mixer as one split, keeping their total. 0.5 = stock (150k / 150k, the deepest notches); 0 = dry only; 1 = phased only (vibrato). The extremes are ~2-3 dB louder than 0.5 on guitar
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0 = the Speed knob, 1 = the LFO locked to the global tempo (the circuit's own waveform; its charging resistor is retuned each cycle)
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: LFO cycles per tempo division: 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth. The circuit tops out near 10 Hz
params.label: Sync Div

params.desc: Script = the 1974 circuit; Block = the later Block Logo with R28 (24k from the output back into the second stage): mid hump, more pronounced sweep
params.label: Version

Modulation / Phaser & Vibe.usage: Classic: Speed=0.5, Mix=0.5, Script. The sound: a 1.3 Hz swirl, no resonance. Slow and deep: Speed=0.15. A 4-second sweep. Fast jet: Speed=0.85. About 6 Hz, close to a rotary. Block Logo: Version=Block. R28 feeds the last stage back into the second: a mid hump (+9 dB near 2 kHz), shallower top notch, more vowel. Vibrato: Mix=1.0. The phased signal only: pitch wobble, no notches. Synced: Sync=on, Sync Div=1/4. The LFO follows the global tempo, one cycle per beat.

Modulation / Pitch.description: Bode single-sideband (SSB) frequency shifter. Shifts every partial by the SAME Hz — non-harmonic, metallic detune. Different from pitch_shifter (which is a ratio). Repeats stacks the shift through a filtered feedback loop for endless-glissando textures.
Modulation / Pitch.name: Frequency Shifter

params.desc: SSB shift amount in Hz. Positive = every partial moves up by this many Hz (non-harmonic). Negative = moves down. Small values (±1..±10 Hz) give shimmer/chorus-like beating; larger values sound clangorous/robotic.
params.label: Shift

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=equal blend (shifted + original — classic frequency shifter chorus), 1.0=shifted only.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Recirculates the shifted output back into the shifter — each pass shifts by another `shift_hz`. 0 = clean shift, 0.7 = strong cascade, 0.9 = self-oscillating tape-shift trail.
params.label: Feedback

params.desc: Low-pass in the feedback loop (500 Hz .. 12 kHz). Lower values tame the high-frequency buildup that heavy Feedback can produce; higher values keep the cascade brighter.
params.label: Tone

Modulation / Pitch.usage: Subtle detune shimmer: Shift=±3 Hz, Mix=0.5, Feedback=0. Metallic clank: Shift=±30 Hz, Mix=1.0, Feedback=0. Bell-ish inharmonic tone. Alien wobble: Shift=±120 Hz, Mix=0.6, Feedback=0. Endless glissando (rising): Shift=+8 Hz, Feedback=0.7, Tone=0.5. Cascading upward shifts. Endless glissando (falling): Shift=-8 Hz, Feedback=0.7, Tone=0.4. Robot voice: Shift=±60 Hz on a distorted rhythm guitar, Mix=0.7. Sound design: Automate Shift with an expression pedal for continuous through-zero sweeps.

Modulation / Pitch.description: Two-voice scale-quantised harmonizer built on Signalsmith Stretch (same engine as Pitch Shifter HQ).  Detects the input pitch and adds two harmony voices that stay in the selected key/scale.  Each voice has its own scale-degree Interval, Level, and Pan.  Matches Helix HD2_PitchTwinHarmony surface.  Sounds like the same guitar at a different note rather than the granular harmonizer's slight chorus / sideband artefacts.
Modulation / Pitch.name: Harmonizer v2 (HQ)

params.desc: Root note: 0=C, 1=C#, ..., 11=B
params.label: Key

params.desc: 0=Major, 1=Minor, 2=Dorian, 3=Phrygian, 4=Lydian, 5=Mixolydian, 6=Locrian, 7=Harmonic Minor, 8=Major Pentatonic, 9=Minor Pentatonic
params.label: Scale

params.desc: Voice 1 scale-degree offset: 0=unison, +2=3rd up, +4=5th up, +7=octave up, -3=4th down, -7=octave down
params.label: V1 Interval

params.desc: Voice 1 level (0=off, 1=full)
params.label: V1 Level

params.desc: Voice 1 stereo position. 0=full L, 0.5=centre, 1=full R. Default 0.375 mirrors Helix TwinHarmony.
params.label: V1 Pan

params.desc: Voice 2 scale-degree offset
params.label: V2 Interval

params.desc: Voice 2 level
params.label: V2 Level

params.desc: Voice 2 stereo position. Default 0.625 mirrors Helix TwinHarmony.
params.label: V2 Pan

params.desc: 0=dry only, 0.5=harmonizer blend, 1=harmony only
params.label: Mix

Modulation / Pitch.usage:
Standard 3rd + 5th in C major: Key=C, Scale=Major, V1_Interval=+2 (3rd), V2_Interval=+4 (5th), Mix=0.5.
4th below + 2nd above (Helix default): V1_Interval=-3, V2_Interval=+2, V1_Pan=0.375, V2_Pan=0.625.
Octaves wide: V1_Interval=-7, V2_Interval=+7, V1_Pan=0, V2_Pan=1.
Latency: ~79 ms wet (Signalsmith engine) + ~85 ms pitch-tracking sidechain (harmony output itself is per-sample).

Modulation / Pitch.description: Multi-mode harmonizer powered by Signalsmith Stretch — same engine as Pitch Shifter HQ and Harmonizer v2. Four modes: Subtle Detune (stereo-widening ±50 ¢, dry-aligned), Shimmer Wash (pitched voices into a diffuser+feedback tail), Diatonic (scale-quantised two-voice harmony via hm2, internally dry-aligned), Vintage Echo (pitched echoes in a delay-feedback loop). Mono in → stereo out. Mode is compile-time — replay the chain after changing it.
Modulation / Pitch.name: Eventide H90 Harmonizer

params.desc: COMPILE-TIME. 0=Subtle Detune, 1=Shimmer Wash, 2=Diatonic, 3=Vintage Echo. Replay the chain to switch.
params.label: Mode

params.desc: 0=dry, 5=equal, 10=wet
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Voice A shift in cents (±100 = semi, ±1200 = octave). Subtle Detune clamps to ±50. Diatonic: the cents pick the scale step (nearest of 2nd..octave), live.
params.label: Pitch A

params.desc: Voice B shift in cents. Vintage Echo / Shimmer Wash R-channel voice.
params.label: Pitch B

params.desc: Pre-delay voice A. Vintage Echo: per-iteration echo time (×5).
params.label: Delay A

params.desc: Pre-delay voice B
params.label: Delay B

params.desc: 0=single pass, 5=moderate sustain. Active in Shimmer Wash / Vintage Echo.
params.label: Feedback

params.desc: 0=dark (2 kHz), 5=balanced (7 kHz), 10=bright (12 kHz). Filters feedback path.
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Diatonic root (compile-time)
params.label: Key

params.desc: Diatonic scale (compile-time): 0=Major, 1=Minor, 2=Dorian, 3=Phrygian, 4=Lydian, 5=Mixolydian, 6=Locrian, 7=Harm Minor, 8=Maj Penta, 9=Min Penta
params.label: ScaleMode

Modulation / Pitch.usage: Subtle Detune: Mode=Subtle Detune, PitchA=10. Tight stereo widening with dry-aligned dry leg. Shimmer Wash: Mode=Shimmer Wash, PitchA=1200 (+octave), Feedback=5. Shimmering octave-up wash. Diatonic 3rd+5th in C major: Mode=Diatonic, Key=C, ScaleMode=Major, PitchA=400 (M3), PitchB=700 (P5). Replay chain after changing key/mode/pitch. Vintage Echo staircase: Mode=Vintage Echo, PitchA=100, DelayA=150 ms, Feedback=6. Climbing pitch echoes.

Modulation / Pitch.description: Three-voice octaver built on Signalsmith Stretch: -2 oct, -1 oct, dry, +1 oct.  Polyphonic — chords track cleanly on all voices, unlike v1's monophonic OC-2-style down voices.  Each voice has a dB level slider; Filter shapes the LP cutoff on the down voices, OctU Tone shapes the HP on the up voice.  79 ms wet-path latency (dry leg delay-aligned to match).
Modulation / Pitch.name: Octaver HQ

params.desc: Two octaves down level. -100 = off.
params.label: Oct2 dB

params.desc: One octave down level. -100 = off.
params.label: Oct1 dB

params.desc: Dry signal level. -100 = off.
params.label: Direct dB

params.desc: One octave up level. -100 = off.
params.label: OctU dB

params.desc: LP cutoff on down voices. 0=dark/sub-only, 1=full bandwidth. Default 0.6 = ~520 Hz.
params.label: Filter

params.desc: HP cutoff on up voice. 0=full body, 1=air-only shimmer.
params.label: OctU Tone

params.desc: High-pass on the two DOWN voices only (12 dB/oct): keeps the sub out of the kick / bass register. Parked at 20 Hz it is off.
params.label: Sub HP

params.desc: Low-pass on the two DOWN voices only (24 dB/oct), after Filter: a hard ceiling on what the sub spills upward. Parked at 20 kHz it is off.
params.label: Sub LP

params.desc: Mute the shifted voices while more than one note sounds (a two-note lick is where a pitch shifter smears beating and intermodulation into broadband junk). Subs: the down voices; All wet: the up voice too. Unison, octaves and fifths pass (they share a period and shift cleanly). The verdict is lined up with the 79 ms voices.
params.label: Chord Safe

params.desc: How readily Chord Safe mutes: higher mutes on milder doubt (thirds, seconds, chords at 0.6; palm mutes start to chop above ~0.7). Single notes and bends stay open at any setting.
params.label: Chord Sens

Modulation / Pitch.usage: Clean sub-bass: Oct1=0 dB, Direct=0 dB, Filter=0.4. Round POG-style octave-down. Sub + dry blend: Oct2=-6, Oct1=-3, Direct=0, Filter=0.3. Stacked low end. POG chorus: Direct=0, OctU=-3, OctU_Tone=0.2. Shimmer above the dry. Triple stack: Oct1=-3, Direct=0, OctU=-6. Fat organ pad. Latency note: 79 ms on the wet voices (Signalsmith intrinsic). Dry is delay-aligned so all four voices land together. Tight sub under a mix: Sub HP 60-80 Hz, Sub LP 250-400 Hz, Chord Safe = Subs: the sub stays in its own register and drops out on double-stops and chords instead of smearing them. Mono: the output is mono (L = R) -- the sub is already mono, so no sub-mono control is needed.

Modulation / Pitch.description: Two-tap granular pitch shifter with per-channel Semitones + Cents. Independent L and R pitchers with decorrelated grain jitter, Hanning windowing, 4th-order Lagrange interpolation, and formant-compensation lowpass. Great for unison (detune), harmonies (e.g. L=0, R=+7), whammy (octave), and wide-interval stereo spreads.
Modulation / Pitch.name: Pitch Shifter

params.desc: Grain window size. 30=better transients, 80=smoother. Latency = window/2
params.label: Window

params.desc: 0=dry only, 0.5=harmonizer blend, 1=pure pitch shift
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Left channel coarse shift. -12=octave down, 0=unison, +12=octave up
params.label: L Semitones

params.desc: Left channel fine tune. +/- 100 = +/- 1 semitone. Use with L_Semitones=0 for detune
params.label: L Cents

params.desc: Right channel coarse shift
params.label: R Semitones

params.desc: Right channel fine tune
params.label: R Cents

Modulation / Pitch.usage: Unison/detune: L_Cents=-7, R_Cents=+7, Mix=0.5. Classic chorus-y doubling. Major-third harmony: L_Semitones=0, R_Semitones=+4, Mix=0.5. Sits under the dry. Power fifth: L_Semitones=+7, R_Semitones=+7, Mix=0.5. Wall-of-fifths. Octave whammy: L_Semitones=+12, R_Semitones=+12, Mix=1.0. Wide spread: L_Semitones=-7, R_Semitones=+5. Stereo interval. Window: 30 ms = sharper transients but audible grain at big shifts; 60 ms = smoother, more latency (~30 ms). 50 ms is the usual sweet spot for guitar.

Modulation / Pitch.description: Studio-grade pitch shifter built on Signalsmith Stretch — phase-aware STFT with transient preservation and optional true-envelope formant compensation. Sounds like a guitar shifted, not a synthesised tone. Single-instance per chain (~5-10 % of one Pi 5 core, ~50-80 ms latency). For live monitoring use the granular pitch_shifter instead.
Modulation / Pitch.name: Pitch Shifter HQ

params.desc: 0=dry only, 0.5=harmonizer blend, 1=pure wet
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Coarse pitch shift. -12=octave down, +12=octave up.
params.label: Semitones

params.desc: Fine pitch shift. +/- 100 = +/- 1 semitone.
params.label: Cents

params.desc: 0=plain bin-shift (spectrum moves with pitch), 1=true-envelope preservation (body resonances stay at original pitch — sounds like the same guitar at a different note).
params.label: FormantComp

params.desc: Independent formant transposition in semitones. Only audible when FormantComp=On. +5 = sounds like a smaller body, -5 = larger body.
params.label: FormantShift

params.desc: Tonality limit: frequencies above this are treated as noise (no harmonic locking). Lower = more transient noise preserved; higher = cleaner sustained tones.
params.label: Tonality

Modulation / Pitch.usage: Fifth up harmony: Semitones=+7, Mix=0.5, FormantComp=0. Octave down (preserve body): Semitones=-12, Mix=1.0, FormantComp=1, FormantShift=0. The 'true envelope' keeps the guitar body resonances at their original pitch even as the note drops — avoids the chipmunk-inverse tone of bin-shift-only. Detune 5 cents: Semitones=0, Cents=+5, Mix=0.5. Subtle thickening for unison parts. Bigger formant shift: Set FormantShift independently of Semitones — e.g. Semitones=0 + FormantShift=+5 sounds like the same note played on a smaller guitar body.

Modulation / Special.description: Infinite hold. Toggle Active to capture the last Buffer ms of playing and sustain it forever. Dual-head crossfaded loop — loudness-flat, no click on release. Dry passes through so you can solo over the freeze; a downstream sidecar_vca can duck the freeze while you play.
Modulation / Special.name: Freeze

params.desc: 0 = dry passes through, block is capturing the last Buffer ms into RAM. 1 = write pointer freezes and the captured buffer loops forever. Bind to an FS via Wildcards toggle mode for stomp control.
params.label: Active

params.desc: Length of audio captured at freeze time (ms). Loop period = this value. Longer buffers reduce audible periodicity but need more of a coherent-sounding tail to feed in at capture time.
params.label: Buffer

params.desc: Wet level of the frozen loop (dry always passes). 0 = frozen loop silent, 1 = full-level held bed.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: High-pass on the frozen output. Cleans low rumble that a long chord loop can accumulate.
params.label: HP

params.desc: Low-pass on the frozen output. Darker settings (2–5 kHz) push the freeze into "pad" territory sitting behind lead lines.
params.label: LP

Modulation / Special.usage: Ambient chord bed: Buffer=800 ms, Mix=0.7, HP=80 Hz, LP=6 kHz. Play a chord, stomp Active, solo over it. Percussive hold: Buffer=250 ms, Mix=1.0. Short repeating stutter loop. Volume-swelled drone: Buffer=1500 ms, LP=3 kHz, Mix=0.5. Long dark pad. Ducked over solo: Add sidecar_vca after — freeze dips while you play new notes. FS binding: FS Mapping → wildcard.N → toggle on freeze/active with values [0, 1].

Modulation / Special.description: Plays a Vital preset's LFOs and random sources -- the same number, numbered as in Vital -- into the Harmonic Generator: vibrato on the generated pitch, tremolo on its level, movement on oscillator 2, the filter and the tone. Pick any Vital preset that modulates something the Generator has.
Modulation / Special.name: Modulator

params.desc: The Vital preset whose LFOs and routings this modulator plays (Vital registry id).
params.label: Vital Preset

params.desc: Every routing's depth x this: 1 = the patch's own depths, 0 = off, 2 = twice as deep.
params.label: Intensity

params.desc: Every LFO and random rate x this (tempo-synced ones follow the tempo, then this).
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Which pick bus restarts the LFOs, as a note restarts them in Vital. Off = free-running.
params.label: Retrigger

Modulation / Special.usage: Vibrato like the patch: put a Modulator in the chain with a Harmonic Generator and pick the Vital preset. Its LFOs drive the Generator as they drive the Vital oscillators. Intensity: the patch's depths x this. Speed: its rates x this. Retrigger: a pick restarts the LFOs as a key does in Vital (the Generator publishes picks on bus 1). Off lets them run free. Open Modulator Studio to see the LFO shapes and where each one goes.

Modulation / Special.description: Tape character insert — Helix HD2_RetroReel-style. Saturation, tape head HF rolloff (15/7.5/3.75 IPS), wow + flutter pitch wobble, Texture warmth. No delay/echo — pure tape coloration in series with the signal.
Modulation / Special.name: Retro Reel (Tape Character)

params.desc: Tape saturation drive. 0=near-clean, 1=heavy compression + harmonics.
params.label: Saturation

params.desc: 0=15 IPS (brightest), 1=7.5 IPS (warm), 2=3.75 IPS (dark)
params.label: Tape Speed

params.desc: Tape warmth / compression depth. 0=transparent, 1=heavy tape squash.
params.label: Texture

params.desc: Combined wow (slow 0.7Hz) + flutter (8Hz) pitch wobble. 0=stable, 1=worn-machine.
params.label: Wow/Flutter

Modulation / Special.usage: Subtle warmth: Saturation=0.3, TapeSpeed=15 IPS, Texture=0.4, WowFlutter=0.2. Clean signal with just a touch of tape glue. Classic 7.5 IPS: Saturation=0.5, TapeSpeed=7.5 IPS, Texture=0.5, WowFlutter=0.4. Reel-to-reel studio character. Worn cassette: Saturation=0.7, TapeSpeed=3.75 IPS, Texture=0.8, WowFlutter=0.7. Dark, heavily-compressed, wobbly. Lo-fi cassette wash: Same as worn but with high WowFlutter for the drifting / pitch-bend feel.

Modulation / Special.description: 4-quadrant ring modulator with 3-waveform carrier (sine/triangle/square), exponential LFO FM of carrier frequency, and 10Hz–10kHz carrier range. True suppressed-carrier multiplication with 6dB level compensation. Exponential carrier taper and FM for consistent musical intervals at any frequency.
Modulation / Special.name: Ring Modulator

params.desc: Carrier frequency. 0=10Hz (tremolo), 0.5=316Hz (musical zone), 1=10kHz (extreme)
params.label: Frequency

params.desc: LFO speed for carrier FM. 0=0.1Hz (slow sweep), 1=8Hz (fast warble)
params.label: LFO Rate

params.desc: Carrier FM depth in octaves. 0=static, 0.5=±1 octave, 1=±2 octaves
params.label: LFO Amount

params.desc: 0=Sine (clean, 2 sidebands), 1=Triangle (richer), 2=Square (dense, harsh)
params.label: Wave

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=equal blend (keeps original + sidebands), 1.0=ring mod only (full alien)
params.label: Mix

Modulation / Special.usage: Classic ring mod: Freq=0.5 (316Hz), Wave=Sine, Mix=0.5. Metallic sidebands + dry. Sub-audio tremolo: Freq=0.05 (10Hz), LFO=off. Ring mod becomes amplitude modulation. Harmonic tuning: Set carrier to a musical ratio of your input (octave, fifth) for strange chords. Alien texture: Wave=Square, Mix=1.0. Dense inharmonic sidebands, no original pitch. Swept ring mod: LFO Rate=0.3, Amount=0.5. Carrier sweeps ±1 octave — evolving metallic wash. Robot voice: Freq near unison with input, Mix=0.5. Deep beating + high shimmer.

Modulation / Special.description: Time-domain sample & hold. Snaps a fresh sample of the input at each Rate tick and holds it until the next. Rate below 30 Hz sounds like a rhythmic chopper; between 30–500 Hz it turns tonal and aliased (robotic); above 500 Hz it AM-modulates. Optional Lag smooths the steps into swept sweeps. Sync locks Rate to the global BPM.
Modulation / Special.name: Sample & Hold

params.desc: Sample clock frequency (Hz). Ignored when Sync is on. 0.5–30 = rhythmic chopper; 30–500 = tonal / robotic; 500+ = AM ringing.
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Post-hold smoothing. 0 = hard steps (classic S&H). 5+ ms rounds edges into ramps — turns S&H into a stepped LFO through audio.
params.label: Lag

params.desc: 0 = dry only, 0.5 = equal blend (subtle stepping under original), 1.0 = fully sampled.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0 = manual Rate slider, 1 = BPM-locked (Div sets subdivision).
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: Ticks per quarter note when Sync=1. 1=quarter, 2=8th, 4=16th, 8=32nd, 16=64th, 32=128th.
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Special.usage: Random-step vibe: Rate=6 Hz, Lag=0 ms, Mix=1.0. Classic S&H chop. Robot voice: Rate=180 Hz, Lag=0 ms, Mix=0.7. Aliased ring on top of dry. Bit-crushed edge: Rate=2000 Hz, Lag=0 ms, Mix=1.0. Rough top-end sizzle. Analog-y stepped LFO: Rate=4 Hz, Lag=20 ms, Mix=1.0. Steps soften into slopes. Sync 1/16 chop: Sync=1, Div=1/16 at 120 BPM. Rhythm-locked S&H.

Modulation / Special.description: Rhythmic stutter / glitch. Each cycle a short slice of the input is captured and looped for Slice% of the period; the rest of the period plays live. Crossfaded with a Smooth attack to prevent clicks. Great for beat-synced chops, glitch fills, and IDM textures.
Modulation / Special.name: Stutter

params.desc: Manual stutter frequency. Ignored when Sync is on
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Fraction of each cycle that loops the captured slice. 10=short gate, 50=half/half, 100=always looping
params.label: Slice

params.desc: Crossfade between live and stutter to prevent clicks. 1=sharp, 5=smooth, 20=very soft
params.label: Smooth

params.desc: Wet/dry blend. 0=bypass, 1=fully stuttered
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=manual Rate, 1=slice length locked to global BPM (no phase lock — stutter is time-only)
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Special.usage: Classic chop: Rate=4 Hz, Slice=50%, Smooth=5 ms. Rhythmic L-R pulse. 16th-note gate (120 BPM): Rate=8 Hz, Slice=50%. Slow glitch: Rate=1 Hz, Slice=80%, Smooth=10 ms. Long held slices. Granular: Rate=8 Hz, Slice=20%, Smooth=2 ms. Micro-loops. Subtle rhythm: Mix=0.4, Rate=2 Hz, Slice=50%. Blend under live signal. Rate: stutters per second. Slice: fraction of the period that is looped (vs. live). Smooth: crossfade into/out of the loop (higher = softer edges).

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.description: Constant-power stereo auto-panner. Sums the incoming signal to mono and sweeps it between left and right using a sine / triangle / square LFO. cos/sin pan law keeps RMS flat across the sweep — no volume dip at centre. Depth controls sweep width; Phase sets the LFO start position so multiple panners can be desynchronised.
Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.name: Auto Panner

params.desc: LFO speed. 0.1=8s per cycle (slow drift), 1=1Hz, 10=machine-gun
params.label: Rate

params.desc: Pan swing. 0=locked to centre, 0.5=moderate, 1=full L-to-R sweep
params.label: Depth

params.desc: 0=Sine (smooth), 1=Triangle (linear), 2=Square (hard ping-pong)
params.label: Wave

params.desc: LFO start position. 0=centre, 0.25=hard R, 0.5=centre (inverted), 0.75=hard L
params.label: Phase

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.usage: Classic slow sweep: Wave=Sine, Rate=0.5 Hz, Depth=0.8. Smooth L↔R drift. Helicopter: Wave=Square, Rate=4–8 Hz, Depth=1.0. Hard ping-pong, rhythmic. Leslie fast: Wave=Triangle, Rate=6 Hz, Depth=1.0. Trapezoidal swing. Subtle motion: Wave=Sine, Rate=0.2 Hz, Depth=0.3. Gentle widening — great before reverb. Phase: 0=start at centre, 0.25=start hard right, 0.75=start hard left. Signal shape: Output is always mono-panned (L+R=1×input when Depth=0). Place after cab/NAM so the timbre stays consistent as it pans.

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.description: Leslie 122-style rotary speaker simulation.  Active crossover splits the input into a treble horn (above ~800 Hz) and a bass drum (below).  Each rotor has its own Doppler-shift delay line (frequency modulation from rotor velocity), amplitude tremolo (beam pointing away from mic), and stereo mic split (90 degrees between L/R mic positions).  Speed toggles between Chorale (slow) and Tremolo (fast) with a configurable acceleration ramp matching the inertia of the real Leslie's belt drive.
Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.name: Leslie 122

params.desc: 0 = Chorale (slow rotation), 1 = Tremolo (fast rotation)
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Chorale rotation rate. 0 = 0.2 Hz horn / 0.15 Hz drum, 1 = 1.5 Hz horn / 1.0 Hz drum
params.label: Slow Speed

params.desc: Tremolo rotation rate. 0 = 4 Hz horn / 3 Hz drum, 1 = 10 Hz horn / 7 Hz drum
params.label: Fast Speed

params.desc: 0 = instant, 1 = medium (~1 sec), 2 = long (~5 sec) belt-drive inertia
params.label: Ramp Time

params.desc: Pre-rotor tube saturation. 0 = clean, 1 = heavily driven 6550 / 6L6 power-tube growl
params.label: Drive

params.desc: Horn/drum balance. 0 = bass drum only, 1 = treble horn only
params.label: Blend

params.desc: 0 = dry, 0.5 = equal blend, 1 = full rotary wet
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Stereo mic separation. 0 = mono, 1 = full 90-deg pair (authentic dual-mic studio capture)
params.label: Mic Spread

params.desc: Output trim in dB
params.label: Level

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.usage: Chorale (slow): Speed=Slow, SlowSpeed=0.24, FastSpeed=0.73 (Helix Rotary 122 stored defaults). Drifting, shimmering pitch sweep ~0.7 Hz horn / 0.5 Hz drum. Tremolo (fast): Speed=Fast. Faster ~7 Hz horn / 5.5 Hz drum — Hammond B3 / SRV / Stevie Ray rotary. Speed transition: RampTime sets how fast the rotors accelerate / decelerate when toggling. 0 = instant, 2 = long ~5 sec ramp (authentic 122 belt response). Drive: Pre-rotor tube saturation. Adds the warm growl of a 122's tube power section (40 W 6550 / 6L6). Blend: Horn/drum balance. 0 = bass drum only, 0.5 = balanced, 1 = treble horn only. Mix: 0 = dry, 0.5 = equal blend, 1 = full rotary.

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.description: Blackface optical tremolo with NE-2U neon lamp threshold and CdSe photocell response. Sine LFO is clipped by neon striking voltage into pulses — signal dips briefly when neon fires, stays full between pulses ("throb" not "pump"). Intensity controls both depth and duty cycle. Photocell asymmetry (25ms rise, 70ms fall) naturally compresses depth at high speeds.
Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.name: Fender Optical Tremolo

params.desc: Manual LFO rate, log curve fitted to the Helix: 0=2 Hz, 0.1=2.7 Hz, 0.4=6.5 Hz, 0.5=8.7 Hz, 0.7=15.7 Hz, 1=37 Hz. Ignored when Sync is on
params.label: Speed

params.desc: Neon drive level. Sets both depth AND pulse duty cycle. 0=off, 0.7=classic, 1=deep
params.label: Intensity

params.desc: 1.0=hardware default (fully processed). 0.5=parallel blend (never fully quiet)
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=manual Speed, 1=phase-locked to global BPM
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.usage: Classic surf: Speed=0.3, Intensity=0.7. Slow heartbeat throb. SRV/Dick Dale: Speed=0.5, Intensity=0.7. Medium, driving pulse. Fast shimmer: Speed=0.9, Intensity=0.8. Depth self-compresses — authentic. Intensity: Controls how hard the neon fires. Low=subtle (neon barely strikes). High=deep pulses. Mix=1.0: Authentic hardware (always processed). Mix=0.5 for parallel blend.

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.description: Electronic VCA tremolo with continuous triangle-to-square waveform morphing via tanh waveshaping. No optical lag — depth is consistent at all speeds. Volume peaks at LFO peak (opposite polarity to Optical Tremolo). Wave=0 is smooth pumping, Wave=1 is hard stutter gate.
Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.name: Wave Tremolo

params.desc: Manual LFO speed. 0=1Hz (slow swell), 0.4=~2.6Hz (classic), 1=11Hz (fast flutter). Ignored when Sync is on
params.label: Rate

params.desc: LFO shape. 0=triangle (smooth), 0.3=rounded (musical), 0.7=choppy, 1=square (stutter)
params.label: Wave

params.desc: Volume cycling amount. 0=off, 0.5=subtle, 1=full on/off
params.label: Depth

params.desc: 1.0=hardware default (fully processed). 0.5=parallel blend
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=manual Rate slider, 1=phase-locked to global BPM (tap-tempo / preset BPM)
params.label: Sync (0/1)

params.desc: Subdivision when Sync is on. 1=whole, 2=half, 4=quarter, 6=dotted-1/4, 8=eighth, 12=dotted-1/8, 16=sixteenth
params.label: Sync Div

Modulation / Tremolo & Rotary.usage: Classic tremolo: Rate=0.4, Wave=0.2, Depth=0.7. Smooth, slightly rounded pulse. Hard chop: Rate=0.4, Wave=0.7, Depth=1.0. Rhythmic stutter gate effect. Smooth swell: Rate=0.2, Wave=0, Depth=0.5. Gentle triangle — Tweed-era character. Wave: 0=triangle (smooth pump), 0.3=rounded (musical zone), 0.7=choppy, 1=hard square. vs Optical Tremolo: No depth compression at speed. Opposite polarity (swells, not dips). Wave morphing.

Preamp.description: FET amplifier (Boss FA-1 style), modelled from its circuit: a 2SK30 source-follower buffer, a switchable 720 Hz Lo-Cut coupling cap, an HA1457 non-inverting gain stage (Volume is its gain, with the op-amp's real bandwidth, slew rate and 9 V swing) and an active Baxandall (+-12 dB at 100 Hz / 8 kHz). Volume 0.5 = unity.
Preamp.name: Boss FA-1

params.desc: Preamp gain. Higher=more tube saturation
params.label: Volume

params.desc: Low frequency shelf. 0=thin, 5=neutral, 10=boomy
params.label: Bass

params.desc: High frequency shelf. 0=dark, 5=neutral, 10=bright
params.label: Treble

params.desc: 0=full range, 1=cut below 700Hz (thin for lead)
params.label: Lo-Cut (0=Off 1=On)

Preamp.usage: Clean boost: Volume=0.3, Lo-Cut=off. Transparent volume lift with FET sparkle. Edge of breakup: Volume=0.7. HA1457W op-amp starts to slew-limit transients. Full drive: Volume=1.0. Asymmetric soft clip — thick, not fizzy. Lo-Cut: Engage for lead work — tightens low end, focuses the midrange. Bass/Treble: ±14dB active Baxandall — powerful, use gently.

Preamp.description: Three-J201 clean preamp, modelled from its circuit: an input stage, a drive stage (Drive sets its source bypass), a passive Baxandall tone stack (flat at noon) and a recovery stage, all square-law JFETs on 9 V. Clean and touch-sensitive at low Drive, the J201s' soft asymmetric squash as it rises. Volume 0.7 = unity at Drive 0.5.
Preamp.name: Benson Preamp

params.desc: 0=clean, 5=moderate overdrive, 10=heavy saturation
params.label: Drive

params.label: Bass

params.desc: High frequency shelf. 0=dark, 5=neutral, 10=bright
params.label: Treble

params.label: Volume

Preamp.usage: Always-on warmth: Drive=0.2, Vol=0.7. Subtle JFET coloring, fattens single coils. Mild breakup: Drive=0.5, Vol=0.7. Touch-sensitive — clean up with guitar volume. Full drive: Drive=0.9, Vol=0.6. Compressed, harmonically rich. Roll Bass to tighten. Bass/Treble: Interactive — boosting one affects the other. Start at 5/5 and adjust.

Preamp.description: Tube console preamp (UA 610 style), modelled from its parts: input transformer iron (level-dependent low-end saturation), a 12AX7 stage and a 6072 stage as Child-law triodes in their circuits, true console shelving EQ (low 70/100/200 Hz, high 4.5/7/10 kHz, +-12 dB) and output transformer iron. Gain 0 / Level 7 = unity; Gain and Level push the triodes into even-then-odd harmonic saturation.

Preamp.usage: Subtle tube warmth: Gain=0dB, Level=5. The transformer and triodes add body. Pushed: Gain=+5dB, Level=7. Second triode starts to compress. EQ in NFB: Lo/Hi controls interact with the tube stages — boost adds harmonics. Output trim: Use to match levels when switching the 610 in/out of the chain.
