Reverb.description: BigSky MX-directional studio reverb with six structurally distinct machines: Hall (8-line Hadamard FDN, prime delays, modulated allpass diffuser, per-line HF damping), Plate (denser FDN + 4 kHz brightener), Spring (dispersive allpass cascades + box resonators), Room (16 ER taps + short FDN), Magneto (4-head tape echo) and Chorale (vowel formant bank). Shimmer, Bloom, Cloud and Nonlinear are the standalone rv_shimmer / rv_bloom / rv_cloud / rv_nonlinear blocks.
Reverb.name: Strymon BigSky

params.desc:
Machine selection — each maps to a structurally distinct topology (not parameter variants). par1 and Mod take on different meanings per machine. Live-switchable but uncrossfaded — switching during a sustained tail will click (~1 ms).

0=Hall: 8-line Hadamard FDN, 6-tap ER, modulated tap reads (BigSky manual page 9).
1=Plate: denser 8-line FDN, 6-stage diffuser, post-FDN 4 kHz brightener (page 10).
2=Spring: 4 dispersive Karjalainen-Välimäki allpass cascades (par1=Dwell drive) + 3-band box resonators (page 11).
3=Room: 16 ER taps + 4-line short FDN tail + 2-stage diffuser (par1=Diffusion) (page 8).
7=Magneto: standalone 4-head tape echo (Decay=last head time, par1=Diffusion, Mod=Feedback) (page 17).
9=Chorale: vocal formant filter bank (par1=Vowel, Mod=Resonance) (page 15).

Machines 4 (Shimmer), 5 (Bloom), 6 (Cloud), 8 (Nonlinear) were SPLIT into standalone blocks rv_shimmer / rv_bloom / rv_cloud / rv_nonlinear (HX26) and removed from this selector. The native dispatch in tonepi_bigsky.h still handles those values for backward compatibility (a legacy chain saved with machine_sel=5 will still play), but the chain.json migrator rewrites them to the new blocks so the dropdown only ever shows the current set.
params.label: Machine

params.desc: RT60 target in seconds. Per-FDN-line feedback gains are computed from this and the line length so all 8 lines decay together (no comb-tooth at long settings).
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Delay before the reverb engine engages. L/R pre-delays are offset by 3 ms for natural stereo decorrelation.
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: 0=dry, 1=fully wet. Equal-power crossfade — perceived loudness stays roughly constant across the range.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Per-line HF damping cutoff (1.2 kHz → 8 kHz, log scale). Low values = warm/dark tail, high values = bright/airy.
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Default: scales FDN-line LFO modulation depth (Hall/Plate/Room/Cloud/Shimmer/Nonlinear/Chorale tank). 0=nearly static (more comb-y), 10=full ±0.7 ms (most decorrelated). Machine overrides: Bloom=Feedback amount of bloom-generator loop (high+long Length → tails longer than Decay). Magneto=Feedback from last head into the loop. Chorale=Resonance/Q of vowel formant filters (3=MILD, 6=MEDIUM, 12=HIGH).
params.label: Mod

params.desc:
Machine-specific.
Hall/Plate: reserved (no effect).
Spring: Dwell — preamp drive (0-2.5=CLEAN outboard, 2.5-5=COMBO on-amp, 5-7.5=TUBE harmonic-rich, 7.5-10=OVERDRIVE trashy splash).
Room: Diffusion (0=discrete ER echoes, 10=smooth wash).
Shimmer: Amount (0=dry, 10=full shifted-voice mix).
Bloom: Length (0=quick bloom 8 ms gen delay, 10=gradual 110 ms).
Cloud: Diffusion intensity (0=grainy transients, 10=full ensemble smear).
Magneto: Diffusion (0=clean heads, 10=blurry/reverb-like).
Nonlinear: Shape (0-1.6=Gate, 1.6-3.3=Swoosh, 3.3-5=Reverse, 5-6.6=Ramp, 6.6-8.3=Gauss, 8.3-10=Bounce).
Chorale: Vowel (0=AAHHOO, 1.4=AAHH, 2.9=AAHHOH, 4.3=OH, 5.7=OOOHOH, 7.1=OOOO, 8.6=RANDOM).
params.label: Param1

params.desc: Hold the current tail: mutes new input and lifts feedback to ~unity. Releases on bypass / next chain swap.
params.label: Freeze

params.desc: Like Freeze but with a 30% input bleed so new playing layers on top of the held tail.
params.label: Infinite

params.desc: One-pole HPF on the wet output. Keeps mud out of long tails without affecting dry.
params.label: LoCut

params.desc: One-pole LPF on the wet output. Distinct from Tone (which damps per FDN line) — this trims the summed wet bus.
params.label: HiCut

params.desc: Wet-side level trim in dB. Applied to the wet bus before the dry/wet mix.
params.label: Level

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks (reverb only fills the gaps between taps). Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

Reverb.usage: Concert hall: Machine=Hall, Decay=4.0, Mix=0.30, Tone=6, Mod=3. Long lush tail. Tight room (Phase 1: Hall): Decay=1.2, PreDelay=8, Tone=4. Closer. Ambient wash: Decay=12, Mix=0.45, Mod=7, HiCut=6000. Dreamy. Tail freeze: Engage Freeze while strumming to hold the current decay indefinitely.

Reverb.description: cosmic reverb cosmic reverb. Allpass-inside-loop architecture with independent L/R tanks, sign-alternating diffusion, fractional-delay modulation, inverse gravity swell, resonant post-EQ, and freeze. Size scales allpass delays from metallic comb (1) through hall (50) to galactic (120). Gravity controls forward decay (5-10) or inverse swell envelope (0-5).
Reverb.name: Eventide Blackhole

params.desc: 0=fully dry, 0.5=equal blend, 1.0=fully wet
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 5-10=forward decay (5=short, 10=60s). 0-5=inverse swell (notes fade in). Feedback adds extra decay time
params.label: Gravity

params.desc: 1=metallic comb, 50=hall, 120=galactic. Scales allpass delay lengths
params.label: Size

params.desc: Adds 0-40s to decay time. Musical extension without runaway — always below unity gain
params.label: Feedback

params.desc: Gap before reverb onset. 0-20=tight, 30-80=hall, 500+=huge separation
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: Low shelf EQ at 350Hz on wet signal. Boost for rumble, cut for clarity
params.label: Lo

params.desc: High shelf EQ at 2kHz on wet signal. Boost for air, cut for dark
params.label: Hi

params.desc: 0=wide EQ (300Hz bandwidth), 10=narrow resonant peaks (20Hz). Adds harmonic ringing
params.label: Q

params.desc: Modulation depth inside allpasses. L/R have phase-offset multi-voice LFOs
params.label: Mod Depth

params.desc: 0=slow drift (0.1Hz), 5=moderate (1.1Hz), 10=fast chorus (2.1Hz)
params.label: Mod Rate

params.desc: 0=normal, 1=freeze tail (decay=300s, input muted). New notes do not enter
params.label: Freeze (0/1)

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

params.desc: Output level in dB (post mix). 0=unity, -24=mute, +12=boost.
params.label: Level

Reverb.usage: Cosmic wash: Gravity=7, Size=50, Mix=0.5. Classic huge reverb. Galactic: Size=100, Gravity=9, Feedback=6, Mod=5. Enormous, evolving stereo field. Inverse swell: Gravity=2, Size=60, Mix=0.6. Notes fade in slowly — reversed reverb feel. Freeze: Freeze=on. Infinite hold — new notes layer on top of frozen tail. Metallic: Size=3, Gravity=5. Tiny comb-like reverb, percussive. Dark ambient: Hi=-12dB, Lo=+6dB, Gravity=8, Size=80. Deep, rumbling wash. Resonant: Q=7, Hi=+6dB. Narrow EQ peaks add harmonic ringing to the tail.

Reverb.description: Eight-mode reverb (Mercury X-style): Ultraplate (dense plate + optional shimmer), Cathedra (long hall + intra-tank shimmer + slow swell), 78 Room/Plate/Hall (Lexicon 224 inspired bass/mid split), Spring (4-allpass cascade with twang), Prism (dual-tank wide stereo), Gravity (granular pad). All sliders live; instrument-style mode switching with sub-frame state reset. NEON-vectorised FDN damping LP.
Reverb.name: Meris Mercury X

params.desc: 0=Ultraplate (dense plate), 1=Cathedra (slow hall + shimmer), 2=78Room (Lexicon 224 short), 3=78Plate (Lexicon 224 medium), 4=78Hall (Lexicon 224 long), 5=Spring (4-allpass tank), 6=Prism (dual-tank wide stereo), 7=Gravity (granular pad). Switching glitches < 1 frame.
params.label: Mode

params.desc: 0=tight (0.3s), 1=infinite-feel (15s). Per-mode interpretation: spring uses for fb gain, gravity multiplies by 1.5 for pad density.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: High-pass on the wet output. Removes mud from the reverb tail without affecting dry.
params.label: LoCut

params.desc: Low-pass on the wet output. Also influences the per-machine FDN damping LP (brighter hi_cut = brighter tail).
params.label: HiCut

params.desc: Modulation depth applied to FDN line read positions (small fractional offsets, ±6 samples max). Adds chorus shimmer in the tail.
params.label: ModDepth

params.desc: Modulation rate (0.05-3.05 Hz). For Gravity: also drives the granular pitch LFO.
params.label: ModSpeed

params.desc: 0=dry, 0.5=equal, 1.0=fully wet. Applied in FAUST after native processing.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Delay before the reverb engine engages. 0-200 ms.
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: Input scattering — controls the onset density. Per-mode scaling: Cathedra/Hall use lower (slower build), Plate uses full.
params.label: Diffusion

params.desc: Mode-specific. Ultraplate: Size. Cathedra: Swell time. 78-modes: TankMod. Spring: Twang (allpass coef). Prism: Size. Gravity: Gain tame.
params.label: Param1

params.desc: Mode-specific (bipolar). Ultraplate/Cathedra: Pitch shimmer (-12 to +12 st). 78-modes: Crossover (200-1000 Hz). Spring: Damp. Prism: Distance. Gravity: ModFB.
params.label: Param2

params.desc: Mode-specific. Currently only Prism uses it: Dispersion (relative diffusion of the right tank).
params.label: Param3

params.desc: 0=normal, 1=freeze (FDN feedback set to ~1.0, input muted — captures the current tail and holds).
params.label: Freeze

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

params.desc: Output level in dB (post mix). 0=unity, -24=mute, +12=boost.
params.label: Level

Reverb.usage: Strummed steel acoustic plate: Mode=Ultraplate, Decay=0.5, Mix=0.4. Tight, dense plate. Shimmer wash: Mode=Cathedra, Decay=0.85, Param2=0.5, Param1=0.6. Slow swell + +octave shimmer. Vintage hall: Mode=78Hall, Decay=0.7, Param1=0.3, Param2=-0.3. Lexicon-style with bass-favoured tail. Boing spring: Mode=Spring, Param1=0.7 (twang), Param2=0.0 (mid damp). Wide stereo: Mode=Prism, Param1=0.7 (size), Param2=0.5 (distance), ModDepth=0.5. Granular pad: Mode=Gravity, Decay=0.9, Param1=0.4 (gain tame), ModDepth=0.6, ModSpeed=0.3.

Reverb.description: Instantaneous ambience for high-gain rhythm — wide, full and hall-like while notes ring, gone the moment the strings are damped (RT60 fixed 120 ms). Diffused 4-line FDN with allpasses inside the feedback loops for density. No gate or ducker, so sustained chords never chop. Mono-safe.
Reverb.name: Micro Tank

params.desc: Equal-power dry/wet crossfade. This is a tone thickener — 0.2-0.35 is the useful band for rhythm; past ~0.5 it starts to sound like a room instead of part of the tone.
params.label: Amount

params.desc: Delay before the wet path so the dry pick attack lands first — this is what keeps it punchy. 12 ms is well under the ~30 ms echo-fusion threshold so it still fuses into one sound. 0 ms smears the transient.
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: Modulation depth on the four delay lines. Supplies the micro-detune width (Doppler) without a pitch shifter. 0 = static tank.
params.label: Thickness

params.desc: Wet lowpass. Keeping the wet dark is what smooths high-gain fizz — a bright wet path on a distorted source sounds harsh. Lower = smoother.
params.label: Darkness

params.desc: Stereo width of the WET image (mid/side). 0 = wet collapsed to centre (mono), 1 = the tank's natural decorrelation, 2 = exaggerated. The mono sum is the mid signal and does NOT change with this knob, so widening can never cancel through a PA. Dry is untouched.
params.label: Spread

params.desc: Wet trim, post-mix.
params.label: Level

Reverb.usage: Start here: Amount 25%, PreDelay 12 ms, Thickness 0.8, Darkness 3.5 kHz. Too washy between chugs: lower Amount, or raise PreDelay toward 20 ms so the dry attack leads further. Attack sounds smeared: raise PreDelay. 0 ms puts the wet on top of the pick attack. Still fizzy: lower Darkness toward 2.5 kHz. For harshness on the DRY signal chain Dynamic De-Metallizer after this block. Want more chorus-like movement: raise Thickness. 0 = static tank. Too wide / collapsing in mono: Spread 1 is the natural image; drop toward 0 to centre it, push to 2 to exaggerate. Mono sum is unaffected either way.

Reverb.description: multi-machine reverb stereo multi-machine reverb. 8 machines: Room, Hall, Plate, Spring, Chamber, Shimmer, Cloud, Bloom. Allpass-inside-loop architecture with independent L/R tanks (different prime delays), cross-feed, pre-delay, early reflections, output-tap modulation, and RT60-based decay. Freeze (momentary) and Infinite (latched) hold modes via native reverb_tank.h sidecar.
Reverb.name: Strymon BigSky MX

params.desc: RT60 reverb tail. 0.5=tight, 5=hall, 15+=ambient wash. Held by sidecar when Freeze or Infinite is on
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Gap before reverb onset. 0-20=tight, 30-80=hall, 100+=separated
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: 0=fully dry, 0.5=equal blend, 1.0=fully wet
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=dark (feedback LP down, HP up), 5=neutral, 10=bright
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Modulation depth applied to output tap (not feedback ring). L/R use different rates
params.label: Mod

params.desc: Machine-specific. Spring=drive amount, Shimmer=octave-up blend
params.label: Param1

params.desc: 0=Room, 1=Hall, 2=Plate, 3=Spring, 4=Chamber, 5=Shimmer, 6=Cloud, 7=Bloom
params.label: Machine (0-7)

params.desc: 0=normal decay, 1=latched infinite hold via native sidecar. Written by FS13 long-press from Perform / Perform Lite
params.label: Infinite (0/1)

params.desc: 0=live tank, 1=momentary loop-buffer hold (sidecar). FS13 short-press on Perform engages, release disengages
params.label: Freeze (0/1)

params.desc: High-pass filter on reverb wet signal only. Trims sub-bass mud out of the tail without affecting the dry guitar tone.
params.label: Low Cut

params.desc: Low-pass filter on reverb wet signal only. Tames HF shimmer / sizzle without darkening the dry signal.
params.label: High Cut

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

params.desc: Output level in dB (post mix). 0=unity, -24=mute, +12=boost.
params.label: Level

Reverb.usage: Big hall: Machine=Hall, Decay=5s, Mix=0.5, Tone=5. Classic large hall with early reflections. Plate shimmer: Machine=Shimmer, Decay=8s, Param1=6. Octave-up shimmer in the feedback loop. Spring drip: Machine=Spring, Param1=7. Drive into the spring for splashy character. Ambient cloud: Machine=Cloud, Decay=15s, Mod=5, Mix=0.6. Dense, diffuse wash. Tight room: Machine=Room, Decay=1s, PreDelay=10ms. Short, natural room ambience. Infinite pad: Infinite=on, any machine. Native sidecar holds the tail — new notes layer on top. Bloom swell: Machine=Bloom, Decay=6s. Density builds over time — allpass diffusers bloom.

Reverb.description: Physical reverbs: each mode models a real reverberating medium and its electronics -- every mode of the medium at its true frequency and decay -- instead of a feedback delay network. Modes: the EMT 140 steel plate, the Fender 6G15 spring tank, the AKG BX 20E studio spring, two real concert halls (Musikverein, Boston Symphony Hall), the Binson Echorec's swell, a booth whose door your pick slams shut and the decay swings open onto a hall, the EMT plate with loose steel beads that your pick throws into the air, St Paul's Cathedral heard from under its dome, an upright piano whose strings ring in sympathy with your guitar, the Inchindown oil tank, the longest reverberation ever measured, a long desert wire on posts whose chirps race along the line, a chain of rooms whose last one blooms in after the note, and the same bloom behind a shutter that cuts it as the note ends.
Reverb.name: TonePi Physical Reverb

params.desc: The reverberating medium. EMT 140 Plate: all ~21,000 modes of a 2 x 1 m steel plate to 16 kHz, each at its physical frequency and decay, heard through two contact pickups. Fender 6G15 Spring: the Accutronics Type 4 tank's two long springs, every mode from the helix physics (the drip and chirp are not shaped by hand), driven by the 6G15's 6K6GT. AKG BX 20E: the studio spring -- two 1.2 m torsional lines, etched and bent for diffusion, read by anti-phase pickups that cancel the direct echoes (no boing, no flutter). Musikverein / Boston: the real halls, simulated from their geometry and materials (image sources, ray tracing, seat dip) and checked against Bradley's measurements of them. Binson Echorec Swell: the magnetic drum -- one record head, four playback heads (74/148/222/296 ms), all four fed back through the 12AX7 record amp and the steel wire, so the swell darkens and compresses as it builds. Booth Door to Hall: two coupled rooms -- a small hard-walled booth (the amp and you) whose door opens onto the Musikverein's stage. Your playing works the door: a hard pick shuts it (tight, bright booth), and as the note decays it opens and the booth's sound drains into the big, dark hall. The energy that leaves the booth is what fills the hall (coupled-room physics, checked against the coupled-room energy balance); nothing is pitch-shifted. EMT 140 + Loose Beads: the EMT plate laid flat with small steel beads on it. A hard pick shakes the plate past 1 g, so the beads are thrown, bounce and click into the plate (a sparkle on the attack); as the plate decays below 1 g they settle, and the plate rings on as the body. Nothing detects the pick: only an attack strong enough throws the beads. St Paul's Cathedral: you play in the choir, you listen under the dome. The choir and the main volume are modelled as two coupled spaces (fitted to, and tested against, the cathedral's measured responses); under the dome the response is the measured one (OpenAIR, University of York, CC BY). The choir drains through its great arch into the 120,000 m3 nave and dome, so the sound builds before its ~11 s decay, and the air's slow drift keeps the long tail alive without any pitch wobble. Sympathetic Piano: an upright piano with the sustain pedal down and a transducer on its soundboard. Your guitar shakes the board, and every string whose partials it finds rings in sympathy -- both strings of an octave, the fifths, the unisons beating -- heard by two microphones behind the open back. The soundboard is modelled from a measured upright (its ribs, bridges and wood), the 236 strings from a maker's stringing scale, all coupled through the board; struck notes sustain like a real upright's. Inchindown Oil Tank: the amp plays into an entrance pipe of a Second World War oil tank dug into a Scottish hillside -- 237 m of sealed concrete, the longest reverberation ever measured (112 s at 125 Hz, Cox & Kilpatrick 2015). The walls absorb almost nothing (near the limit of a perfectly rigid wall), so the air sets the decay: the highs die in seconds, the bass rings for two minutes. Checked against the measured decay in every octave. Desert Wire: a long steel wire strung on posts -- a farm fence to a telegraph line -- with a transducer clamped near the first post and two contact microphones a few spans down (as Alan Lamb recorded his outback telegraph wires). Bending makes the wire dispersive: the highs outrun the lows, so every arrival is a falling chirp (the pew), and each post passes some on to the next span. The wire's exact response, from its physics. Bloom Chamber: you play in a stone room that opens, through a chain of rooms, into a big concrete chamber where you listen. Each room has to fill before it passes the sound on, so the chamber's sound is not there at the pick: it swells in, peaks up to ~1.7 s later, then rings long. Checked against the physics of coupled rooms. Bloom Bubble: the same bloom, heard from a small dead control room through a window with a shutter your playing works: it opens while the note sounds and shuts as it falls away, so the bloom swells and then drops steeply (fixed rooms cannot do that: their release is always the slowest part). Shut, the chamber still leaks through faintly.
params.label: Mode

params.desc: Dry/wet. The dry signal is never processed.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Decay time (to -60 dB). Plate: at 500 Hz, the damping pad (a real EMT 140: 1-5 s). Spring: at 1 kHz (the 4AB3C1B long tank: 2.75-4 s; 3.2 is typical). BX 20E: at 500 Hz (the real unit: 2-4.5 s). Halls: their own (Occupancy changes it). Echorec: LENGTH OF SWELL -- how long the swell takes to die (at 1 kHz); 10 s is near runaway. Booth Door to Hall: the hall's (1.5-6 s; the booth is ~1.3 s with the door shut). Loose Beads: the plate's, as the EMT 140 mode (the beads' clicks re-render: ~3 s). St Paul's: shortens the cathedral's own ~11 s (at 500 Hz) as if it were more absorbent; 10 = the cathedral as it is. Sympathetic Piano: shortens the piano's own decay (its bass strings ring for tens of seconds) as if every string lost more; 10 = the piano as it is. Inchindown: 10 = the tank as measured (43 s at 500 Hz, 112 s at 125 Hz); lower scales it down (5 = half). Desert Wire: 10 = the wire as modelled (it rings ~90 s: steel barely loses energy, and the posts' damping is assumed); lower scales it down. Bloom Chamber and Bubble: 10 = the chamber as it is (~17 s at 500 Hz); lower scales it down. A change keeps the tail ringing.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Delay before the reverb. The engine itself starts the wet 13 ms late (its filterbank); this adds to that.
params.label: Predelay

params.desc: High cut on the reverb.
params.label: Tone

params.desc: High-pass into the driver, as the EMT's V54 amplifier had: a real plate rings long at 100-250 Hz, which muddies guitar chords.
params.label: Low Cut

params.desc: How hard the driver stage is pushed: up = a little tube compression and grit into the medium.
params.label: Drive

params.desc: Mode-specific. Plate: Brightness -- how long the plate's highs ring (0.5 = the real EMT 140; lower = darker, less metallic). Spring: Dwell -- how hard the 6K6GT drives the tank (+-15 dB around noon); up = more drip and splash. BX 20E: Width -- 0.5 = the real unit (line I left, line II right), 0 = mono, 1 = wider. Halls: Seat -- where you sit in the stalls, front (0) to rear (1). Echorec: Swell Shape -- the four heads' levels (the TSW trimmers): 0 = ramp down (the first head loudest), 0.5 = even, 1 = ramp up. Booth Door to Hall: Relax -- how long the door takes to open as the note fades, 0.05 s (0) to 2 s (1). Loose Beads: Throw -- how hard the driver pushes the plate (30 mN to 3 N): up = softer picks throw the beads too, and they bounce longer. St Paul's: Depth -- where in the choir you stand, 6 m (0) to 46 m (1) from the arch: deeper = more bloom (the sound takes longer to reach the dome). Sympathetic Piano: Pedal -- 0 = up (the dampers stop every string but the top 20 notes, which have none), 0.5 and above = fully down (every string free); between = half-pedalling. Changing it keeps the tail ringing (lifting the dampers lets the strings ring on). Inchindown: Pipe -- the length of the pipe the amp plays into, 0.1 m (0) to 60 m (1); 0.5 = the tank's real 2.5 m, 45 cm entrance pipe. Longer = more of the pipe's own resonances and a later arrival. Desert Wire: Wire -- 0 = a farm fence (2.5 mm high-tensile wire, a post every 6 m, 300 m), 1 = a telegraph line (4 mm wire, 70 m spans between poles, a kilometre); between, everything scales together. Fence: quick bright pews and a flutter of post echoes; telegraph: long sliding chirps arriving from far away. Bloom Chamber: Bloom -- two, three, then four rooms in the chain, across each the stone room's drapes drawn back (draped to bare); up = a deeper, slower swell (at 1: the chamber 15 dB down at 0.2 s, peaking ~1.7 s). The very first use builds the rooms' parts once (~10 s); after that a change takes a fraction of a second. Bloom Bubble: Bloom -- as the Bloom Chamber.
params.label: Param 1

params.desc: Mode-specific. Plate: Size -- 0.7x to 1.2x the EMT 140's 2 x 1 m (0.6 = the real plate). Bigger = denser, lower. Spring: Tension -- a tighter (faster, brighter chirp) or slacker tank, +-15 %. Changing it rebuilds the medium (the tail restarts). BX 20E: Compensation -- 0.6-1 = AKG's anti-phase pickups (the reverb starts 20-50 ms late, no echoes); lower lets the direct transit and the flutter echoes back in (0 = in phase). Halls: Occupancy -- 0 = the empty hall (as measured), 1 = full; 0.6 = 60 %. Fuller = shorter, clearer. Echorec: Drum Speed -- 0.6 = nominal (71 rpm), 0 / 1 = -20 / +20 % (longer / shorter echoes). Booth Door to Hall: Door -- how wide it opens: 0 = a slot (the booth alone), 1 = the whole wall (11.6 m2: the booth drains in ~0.4 s and the hall takes over). Loose Beads: Bead Size -- 0.5 to 3 mm steel balls: bigger = louder, slightly darker clicks. St Paul's: Drift -- the air's slow movement through the space: 0 = a frozen tail, 0.6 = typical, 1 = restless; the late highs wander, nothing pitch-shifts. Sympathetic Piano: Driver -- where the transducer sits on the soundboard: 0 = beside the bass bridge (the wound strings answer most), 1 = the treble end of the treble bridge (the short strings); between, the drive is shared as two transducers would. Inchindown: Air -- the air in the tank: 0 = dry (20 % humidity: the highs die faster), 0.6 = as measured (saturated, 10 C), 1 = warmer (20 C, saturated: longer highs). Desert Wire: Grip -- how hard the posts hold the wire: 0 = loose staples (the wire slides through; the low twang travels the whole line), 1 = tied hard (only the chirping highs leak past each post). Bloom Chamber: Depth -- how far into the chamber you stand, 3 m (0) to 40 m (1) from its doorway. Bloom Bubble: Release -- how fast the shutter shuts once the note falls away, 10 ms (0) to 2 s (1): low = a bubble that pops.
params.label: Param 2

params.desc: Mode-specific. Plate: Pickup Spread -- how far apart the two contact pickups sit (stereo width). Spring: Spring Balance -- the short (58 ms) spring vs the long (72 ms) one; 0.5 = both, as in the tank. BX 20E: Damping -- the foam dampers' pressure (0.5 = factory): up = shorter lows. Halls: Width -- the omni microphone pair's spacing, 0.2 m to 2 m. Echorec: Heads -- 0 = the early T5E's wide-gap heads (to ~5 kHz), 0.5 = the T7E (~11 kHz), 1 = new heads (~15 kHz). Booth Door to Hall: Sensitivity -- how hard a pick must be to shut the door: shut at -6 dBFS (0) to -42 dBFS (1), and fully open 24 dB below that. Loose Beads: Beads -- how many, 4 (0) to 32 (1), in four spots on the plate. St Paul's: Width -- 0 = mono, 0.5 = as measured (a Mid-Side pair under the dome), 1 = wider. Sympathetic Piano: Width -- 0 = mono, 0.5 = the two microphones as placed (0.5 m apart, 0.4 m behind the board), 1 = wider. Inchindown: Echo -- how smooth the concrete is, in five steps: up = smoother walls, the sound running the 237 m end to end as distinct echoes every 1.4 s; down = rougher, a seamless roar; 0.5 = the tank as measured. The first time a step is used it takes ~15 s to build (then it is remembered). Desert Wire: Pickup -- how far down the line the contact microphones are clamped, 1 (0) to 8 (1) spans from the transducer (the right one a span further): further = later, more dispersed chirps, more post echoes in between. Bloom Chamber: Width -- 0 = mono, 0.5 = the pair as placed (two omnis 2 m apart), 1 = wider. Bloom Bubble: Sensitivity -- how quiet the note must get before the shutter shuts: -30 dBFS (0: shuts early) to -78 dBFS (1: only in silence); 0.5 = -54.
params.label: Param 3

params.desc: Reverb level.
params.label: Level

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Reverb.usage: Placement: after the amp and cab (stereo). Classic plate: Decay 2.5, Mix 0.25, Low Cut 80-120 Hz, Tone 8-10 kHz. Darker plate: Brightness down to 0.2-0.3. Lush, wide: Pickup Spread 0.8-1, Size 0.8. Mud on chords? raise Low Cut -- it acts before the plate, like the real V54. Surf spring: 6G15 mode, Dwell 0.7-0.8, Mix 0.4, Decay 3.2. Subtle amp spring: 6G15 mode, Dwell 0.4, Mix 0.15-0.2. Studio spring (no boing): BX 20E, Decay 2.5-3.5, Mix 0.2-0.3. Lo-fi spring: BX 20E, Compensation 0-0.2 -- the echoes AKG cancelled. Floyd swell: Echorec, Decay 4-6, Mix 0.3, Swell Shape 0.5, Heads 0.5; Drive up for more compression. Tight attack, hall bloom: Booth Door to Hall, Decay 3, Mix 0.3, Relax 0.5, Door 0.6-0.8; Sensitivity so hard picks shut the door and held notes open it. Sparkle on the attack: EMT 140 + Loose Beads, Decay 2.5, Mix 0.25; Throw so only your hard picks rattle the beads (watch your input level: louder = more). Ambient, huge: St Paul's Cathedral, Mix 0.2-0.3, Decay 10, Depth 0.5, Drift 0.6; Low Cut 150+ Hz keeps chords from piling up in 11 s of stone. Piano halo: Sympathetic Piano, Mix 0.2-0.3, Decay 10, Pedal 0.5+, Driver 0.6; long held notes bloom as the strings pick them up. Pedal 0 for just the top strings' shimmer. Endless drone: Inchindown Oil Tank, Mix 0.15-0.25, Decay 10, Low Cut 120+ Hz (the bass rings for two minutes); Decay 3-5 for a playable huge space. Laser pews, outback: Desert Wire, Mix 0.2-0.35, Decay 2-4, Wire 0.2 (fence) for quick pews or 1 (telegraph) for long sliding chirps; Grip down for more low twang, up for thin chirps; Pickup up for more distance. Swell after the note: Bloom Chamber, Mix 0.25-0.4, Decay 4-8, Bloom 0.8-1 (the deepest swell), Depth 0.5. Bubble swells: Bloom Bubble, Mix 0.3-0.5, Bloom 0.8-1, Release 0.2-0.4, Sensitivity so the shutter shuts as your notes end. Hall for leads/ambient: Musikverein, Mix 0.2-0.3, Seat 0.4, Occupancy 0.6. Low Cut 120+ keeps chords clear.

params.desc: Delay time in milliseconds
params.label: Time

params.desc: Echo repeats. 0=single, 0.5=moderate, 0.85=near infinite

Reverb.usage: Tape echo: Time=375, Feedback=0.4, Age=0.3, Mix=0.3. Classic tape delay character. Degraded tape: Age=0.7. More wow, flutter, darker, more saturated repeats. Pristine: Age=0.0. Clean delay with minimal tape character.

Reverb.description: Short-tail room/ambience reverb (Helix Ambience parity). 16 ER taps + 4-line short FDN with EarlyLateBlend giving the perceptual "size" axis. No Decay knob — for long tails use Cloud / BigSky.
Reverb.name: Ambient

params.desc: Pre-delay before the ER taps (0..100 ms). Maps to Helix Ambience PreDelay.
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: Equal-power dry/wet crossfade.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: HF damping of the late taps (1.2 kHz → 8 kHz log scale). Maps to Helix Ambience Damping.
params.label: Damping

params.desc: 0 = only ER taps audible (close room), 10 = only the diffused tank tail audible (distant). Maps to Helix Ambience EarlyLateBlend.
params.label: EarlyLateBlend

params.desc: Allpass diffuser coefficient on the wet output (0 = discrete ER bounces, 10 = smooth wash). Maps to Helix Ambience Diffusion.
params.label: Diffusion

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

Reverb.usage: Studio room: PreDelay=5, EarlyLateBlend=3, Diffusion=4. Tight room around the dry signal. Stage ambience: PreDelay=10, EarlyLateBlend=5, Diffusion=7. Open hall feel without the tail. Distant: PreDelay=25, EarlyLateBlend=8, Diffusion=10. Mostly late wash, sense of distance.

Reverb.description: Slowly-building "bloom" reverb (BigSky manual page 13). Trigger-detect + linear-ramp accumulator drives gain from 0 → peak over the Length time, then slow release. Length knob = rise-to-peak duration 280..1000 ms (matches Helix Bloom RiseTime knob).
Reverb.name: Strymon BigSky Bloom

params.desc:
RT60 target for the Hall tank that holds the bloom output — how long the tank itself rings after energy stops arriving. Per-line feedback gains computed from this.

Decay is the TANK ring time. `Release` (below) is the wet-bus fade after you stop playing. The audible tail = min(Decay, Release ×~4). Long decay values need a long Release to be heard.
params.label: Decay

params.desc:
Exponential release tau of the wet-bus gain once you stop playing. -60 dB at ~4.6 × this value. At Release=3 s the wet fades over ~14 s; at 6 s ~28 s; at 30 s the tank RT60 dominates the audible tail.

Prior to this param the release was hardcoded at 1.2 s (~5 s to -60 dB), which capped the audible tail even when Decay was set to 15+ s. Now Decay and Release are independent.
params.label: Release

params.desc: Pre-delay before the bloom-generator. L/R offset by 3 ms for natural stereo decorrelation.
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: Equal-power dry/wet crossfade. 0=dry, 1=fully wet.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Per-line HF damping cutoff (1.2 kHz → 8 kHz, log scale). Lower = darker tail, higher = airier.
params.label: Tone

params.desc: Bloom-generator loop feedback (0.30..0.92). High feedback + long Length produces tails much longer than the displayed Decay.
params.label: Feedback

params.desc: Rise-to-peak duration: 280 ms (0) → 1000 ms (10). Linear ramp; matches Helix Bloom RiseTime 0..2 landing at 280/450/627 ms.
params.label: Length

params.desc: Mute new input and hold tail. Releases on bypass / next chain swap.
params.label: Freeze

params.desc: Like Freeze but with 30% input bleed so new playing layers on top.
params.label: Infinite

params.desc: Wet-side HPF (one-pole). Keeps mud out of long tails without affecting dry.
params.label: LoCut

params.desc: Wet-side LPF on the summed wet bus.
params.label: HiCut

params.desc: Wet-side dB trim applied before the dry/wet mix.
params.label: Level

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

Reverb.usage: Soft swell pad: Decay=4, Mix=0.4, Length=5 (450 ms rise). Plucked notes blossom into pads. Slow ambient: Decay=8, Mix=0.45, Length=10 (1 s rise), Feedback=7. Lush, slow-attack drone. Quick bloom: Length=0 (280 ms rise). Bloom audible but doesn't dominate the dry tone. Long tail: Decay=15, Feedback=8, Length=8. Tail keeps growing well past the displayed decay (manual "Tips & Tricks").

Reverb.description: Cloud reverb (BigSky manual page 14) — 8-stage cascaded modulated allpass diffuser builds an "ensemble" texture before the Hall tank. par1 controls diffusion intensity (0=grainy transient passthrough, 10=full smear).
Reverb.name: Strymon BigSky Cloud

params.desc: 0=grainy transient passthrough, 10=maximum smear / full ensemble character.
params.label: Diffusion

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

Reverb.usage: Dreamy pad: Decay=8, Mix=0.45, Diffusion=8, Tone=5. Diffuse wash with no transient definition. Subtle ensemble: Decay=4, Mix=0.30, Diffusion=4. Diffused texture without losing pluck attack. Wide ambience: Decay=3, Mix=0.50, Diffusion=10. Pillowy stereo cloud.

Reverb.description: Transient-triggered envelope-shaped reverb (BigSky manual page 18). Shape generator drives the wet output through one of 6 profiles: Gate / Swoosh / Reverse / Ramp / Gauss-bell / Bounce. Decay knob = window length (0.3..5 s).
Reverb.name: Strymon BigSky Nonlinear

params.desc: Shape window length. Peak time tracks the shape peak (window end for Reverse, centre for Gauss, ~95% for Gate).
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Pre-delay before the tank. L/R offset by 3 ms.
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: Equal-power dry/wet crossfade.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: Per-line HF damping cutoff. Lower = darker.
params.label: Tone

params.desc: FDN line LFO modulation depth (decorrelation).
params.label: Mod

params.desc: 6 shape buckets: 0-1.6 Gate, 1.6-3.3 Swoosh, 3.3-5 Reverse, 5-6.6 Ramp, 6.6-8.3 Gauss-bell, 8.3-10 Bounce (anti-bell).
params.label: Shape

params.desc: Mute input and hold tail.

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.

Reverb.usage: Reverse: Shape=Reverse (par1=3.5), Decay=1.5. Tail builds up backward into the note. Gated 80s: Shape=Gate (par1=0), Decay=0.6. Abrupt cut-off at the end of the window. Swoosh pad: Shape=Swoosh (par1=2), Decay=3. Slow attack tail. Bell: Shape=Gauss (par1=7), Decay=2. Centre-peaked envelope.

Reverb.description: Shimmer reverb (BigSky manual page 16). Two pitch-shifted voices (octave up + octave-and-fifth) feed the Hall tank — adds an unearthly halo above the dry note. par1 = Amount of pitched content in the wet path.
Reverb.name: Strymon BigSky Shimmer

params.desc: Amount of pitched-voice content in the wet path (0=dry tank, 10=full shimmer).
params.label: Amount

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.

Reverb.usage: Halo over chords: Decay=6, Mix=0.40, Amount=5. Subtle pitched sheen above the tail. Full shimmer wash: Decay=10, Mix=0.50, Amount=10, Tone=7. Bright soaring pad. Subdued sparkle: Decay=4, Mix=0.30, Amount=2. Hints of octave-up without dominating.

Reverb.description: Space Reverb v2 — Eventide Blackhole / Gravity-inspired diffuser tank. Six modulated allpass stages with resonant low/high shelves inside the feedback loop. Bipolar Gravity control: positive = forward smear, negative = reverse swell. High Q on the shelves produces the signature Blackhole whistle at the corner frequencies.
Reverb.name: Space Reverb

params.desc: Bipolar. >0 = forward decay (smoother as g rises). <0 = reverse swell (8-tap rising-envelope shaper into the AP chain).
params.label: Gravity

params.desc: Scales every allpass base delay 0.5×..1.5×. Bigger = longer initial smear and tank time.
params.label: Size

params.desc: Feedback gain. 0 ≈ 0.5 s tail, 1 ≈ 10 s tail. Combine with high Gravity for runaway smears.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Per-stage LFO depth (also scaled by positive Gravity). Breaks metallic AP-cascade ringing.
params.label: Mod

params.desc: Gap between dry and wet onset.
params.label: PreDelay

params.desc: Low shelf corner frequency (in the feedback loop).
params.label: LoFreq

params.desc: Low shelf resonance. >1 puts a peak at the corner — Blackhole whistle.
params.label: LoQ

params.desc: Low shelf boost/cut.
params.label: LoGain

params.desc: High shelf corner frequency (in the feedback loop).
params.label: HiFreq

params.desc: High shelf resonance. >1 produces the upper Blackhole shimmer/whistle.
params.label: HiQ

params.desc: High shelf boost/cut.
params.label: HiGain

params.desc: Hold the tank at 99.9 % feedback (sub-runaway).
params.label: Freeze

params.desc: 0 = fully dry, 1 = fully wet.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: How much the wet ducks under upstream delay taps. 0 = off (default — safe for existing presets); 0.5 = ~6 dB dip on tap peaks; 1.0 = wet fully cuts on tap peaks. Multiple upstream delays are MAXed — loudest tap wins.
params.label: Duck Amt

params.desc: Output level in dB (post mix). 0=unity, -24=mute, +12=boost.
params.label: Level

Reverb.usage: Cosmic wash: Gravity=0.7, Decay=0.7, Size=0.7, Mod=0.4. Long, evolving smear. Reverse swell: Gravity=-0.7, Decay=0.6, Mod=0.3. Build-up envelope on every input event. Whistle pad: Gravity=0.5, Decay=0.6, LoQ=2.5, HiQ=2.5. Resonant shelves sing at the corners. Dark cathedral: Gravity=0.6, Decay=0.8, HiGain=-9, LoGain=+3. Big and warm. Frozen drone: Engage Freeze. Tank holds at 99.9 % feedback through the shelves.

Reverb.description: Vital's own reverb: a 16-line feedback network with a band-pass pre-filter, shelf damping and chorus. Same parameters as Vital, and presets taken from Vital patches.
Reverb.name: Vital Reverb

params.label: Pre Low Cutoff

params.desc: Low-pass into the reverb, as a MIDI note (110 = 4.7 kHz, 128 = off).
params.label: Pre High Cutoff

params.desc: Damping in the loop: the low shelf's frequency.
params.label: Low Shelf Cutoff

params.desc: How much the lows lose each pass.
params.label: Low Shelf Gain

params.desc: Damping in the loop: the high shelf's frequency (90 = 1.5 kHz).

params.desc: Modulation of the delay lines (smooths the tail).

Reverb.usage: From a Vital patch: pick the patch from Presets; its reverb settings load as they are. Decay Time is Vital's log2 seconds. Cutoffs are MIDI notes, as in Vital (69 = 440 Hz). All wet, short decay (common in Vital patches): the pre-filter then shapes the whole sound -- keep it at 1 to match the patch.

Synth.description: Gives every partial of your guitar its own harmonics, phase-locked to it, with no distortion: a chord gets each note's harmonics and none of the intermodulation a drive adds. Enhancer mode adds them under your guitar; Voice mode turns the guitar into a polyphonic synth voice with no pitch tracking.
Synth.name: Harmonic Generator

params.desc: Enhancer = your guitar plus generated harmonics. Voice = a synth voice made from the guitar (feed it to a Surge block in Audio In mode).
params.label: Mode

params.desc: How late the harmonics bloom behind the pick (the dry is never late). 27 ms is the cleanest; the shorter settings add a faint noise.
params.label: Latency

params.desc: Ignore weak spectral peaks that sit on a stronger one's skirt. Quieter on the short latency settings; can thin out low notes.
params.label: Peak Reject

params.desc: Enhancer: level of the harmonics relative to your guitar.
params.label: Amount

params.desc: The waveform each note is built as. All = saw, Odd = square, Even = octave-heavy; Sine = the fundamental only; Triangle = soft odd harmonics; Pulse = a pulse wave (set Pulse Width, sweep it with PWM); Drawbars = an organ, set with the nine drawbars; Bell, Bar (glockenspiel / celesta), Marimba and Xylophone = the inharmonic partials of struck instruments (pair them with Harmonic Decay). Sine and below switch Merge, One Series and Pure Saw on.
params.label: Harmonics

params.desc: Highest harmonic generated. Lower = darker and cheaper.
params.label: Ceiling

params.desc: Playing harder than recently makes the harmonics disproportionately brighter, softer makes them cleaner, as a tube stage would. 0 = linear.
params.label: Touch

params.desc: Voice mode: mix your guitar back in.
params.label: Dry

params.desc: Voice mode: output level relative to your guitar.
params.label: Voice Level

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

params.desc: Sends your picks to a Surge block in Audio In mode set to the same bus, so its envelopes retrigger on every pick. Off if nothing listens.
params.label: Pick Bus

params.desc: One oscillator per harmonic: every pick gets the same steady harmonic balance (Voice). Off = each partial keeps its own harmonics, the richer ensemble sound that suits Enhancer.
params.label: Merge

params.desc: A partial that is already a harmonic of a lower one stops adding harmonics of its own, so a note makes ONE saw instead of a saw plus an octave-up saw (the even harmonics no longer stand out). Best with Merge in Voice mode. A chord note an octave above another keeps most of its own.
params.label: One Series

params.desc: Steadies each partial's pitch across a few milliseconds. Close partials in a chord beat, and the beat reads as a fast pitch wobble that the high harmonics multiply. 0.75 is a good start; 0 = off.
params.label: Pitch Smooth

params.desc: Low chord notes closer than about 47 Hz (a low E chord) are read with a longer window so their harmonics are in tune. Keep Ringing also holds on to a low note that is still ringing when a louder one nearby is picked (A then D on the next string), instead of losing it, and splits two chord notes the analysis heard as one off-key note between them (G and A# in a G minor barre). No extra latency; a little more CPU.
params.label: Low Resolve

params.desc: Voice mode: each note gets its own volume envelope, started by its pick. Shape = your note's own decay times the envelope. Sustain = the envelope replaces the string's decay, so notes hold like a keyboard (up to +18 dB of make-up). Off = your playing's own dynamics.
params.label: Amp Env

params.desc: Amp Env: fade-in after the pick.
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Amp Env: time constant from full to the sustain level.
params.label: Decay

params.desc: Amp Env: level held after the decay (1 = full).
params.label: Sustain

params.desc: Amp Env: how long a note rings on after the string stops or you mute it.
params.label: Release

params.desc: Voice mode: a filter per note, so a new pick sweeps open while the notes still ringing do not. It shapes each harmonic and does not ring or self-oscillate; for resonant squelch put a Synth Filter after this block.
params.label: Voice Filter

params.desc: Voice Filter: cutoff before the envelope.
params.label: Cutoff

params.desc: Voice Filter: peak at the cutoff.
params.label: Resonance

params.desc: Voice Filter: how far each pick sweeps the cutoff, in octaves (negative sweeps down).
params.label: Env Amount

params.desc: Voice Filter envelope: rise after the pick.
params.label: Filter Attack

params.desc: Voice Filter envelope: time constant back to the sustain level.
params.label: Filter Decay

params.desc: Voice Filter envelope: share of the sweep held while the note rings.
params.label: Filter Sustain

params.desc: Voice Filter: how much harder picks sweep further (0 = every pick the same).
params.label: Filter Velocity

params.desc: With One Series on: each note becomes a clean synth waveform built from its lowest partial, instead of keeping your string's own harmonic balance (where you pick along the string). Needed for brass and classic synth tones; Off keeps the guitar's character.
params.label: Pure Saw

params.desc: Voice Filter: the cutoff follows each note, so high and low notes keep the same tone colour. 1 = full tracking (Cutoff is then the value at middle C); 0 = the same cutoff for every note.
params.label: Filter Key Track

params.desc: Keeps chord notes that sit close to a louder note (a third or fourth apart in the low and middle register), which are otherwise lost and leave chords without their third or fifth.
params.label: Chord Detail

params.desc: Adds a sine one octave below each note. Switches Merge on.
params.label: Sub Octave

params.desc: Harmonics = Pulse: 0.5 is a square; smaller is thinner and more nasal.
params.label: Pulse Width

params.desc: Harmonics = Pulse: how far an LFO sweeps the pulse width (the classic Juno/Prophet chorusing movement).
params.label: PWM Depth

params.desc: Harmonics = Pulse: the PWM LFO rate.
params.label: PWM Rate

params.desc: Harmonics = Drawbars: the 16' footage, 0 off to 8 full (3 dB a step).
params.label: Drawbar 16'

params.desc: Harmonics = Drawbars: the 5 1/3' footage, 0 off to 8 full (3 dB a step).
params.label: Drawbar 5 1/3'

params.desc: Harmonics = Drawbars: the 8' footage, 0 off to 8 full (3 dB a step).
params.label: Drawbar 8'

params.desc: Harmonics = Drawbars: the 4' footage, 0 off to 8 full (3 dB a step).
params.label: Drawbar 4'

Synth.usage: Start here (Enhancer): Amount -12 dB, Harmonics All, Latency 27 ms. Clean tones and chords gain sparkle without grit. Synth (Voice): Mode Voice, then a Surge block after it in Audio In mode. Harmonics All = saw-like, Odd = square-like. Latency: only the harmonics are late; your pick attack is not. The shorter settings bloom sooner but add a faint noise; Peak Reject quietens it at some cost to low notes. Touch: 0.5 makes digging in brighter, like a tube stage. Ceiling: lower it to darken the layer.

Everything else (oscillators, unison, filters, envelopes, FX) is the patch's own.

params.desc: How many note decisions the block makes. Full: each pick reads its note (key tracking follows it) and a pitch move without a pick changes the note. Picks: picks still re-attack the envelopes, but the key stays at Key -- no wrong-note or octave ghosts. Off: no note decisions -- the voice opens when you play and ends when the playing dies away; only a new phrase re-attacks. The Generator follows your pitch and dynamics in every mode; key-tracked filters stay at Key when not Full.

params.desc: End a note when your guitar drops this many dB within about 0.1 s -- a mute or a lifted finger -- even if a faint ring remains (an open string ringing in sympathy keeps a muted D4 or E4 going). Synth.usage:
Preset: the sound -- its synth (Vital or Surge), patch and waveform.
Drive: how hard the waveform hits the patch (its filter drive, distortion).
Key: the note the patch thinks it plays: set it near where you play when the patch's filter follows the keyboard (C4 = 60).
Osc 2: the preset's second waveform -- level, tune, detune.

Synth.description: The real Surge XT hybrid synthesizer — surge-synthesizer/surge's own DSP engine compiled headless for the Pi 5. Loads any .fxp patch (dual scenes, 3 osc/scene across ~9 algorithms — Classic, Wavetable, Window, FM2/FM3, String, Twist, Alias, S&H — two multi-mode filter blocks, deep mod matrix, 12 LFOs, built-in FX) and plays it polyphonically from Fishman Tripleplay / MIDI. Mono DI in (ignored), stereo out.
Synth.name: Surge XT

Synth.description: The real Vital wavetable synthesizer — mtytel/vital's own DSP engine compiled bit-exact for the Pi 5. Loads any .vital preset (3 wavetable oscillators, unison, dual filters, mod matrix, 6 envelopes, 8 LFOs, built-in effects) and plays it polyphonically from Fishman Tripleplay / MIDI. Mono DI in (ignored), stereo out.

Synth.description: Native wavetable synthesizer. Six voices — one per Fishman Tripleplay string when MIDI is present, or a monophonic sigmund-tracked voice on the raw DI when it isn't. Serum/Vital-style scan: a bank selects a set of single-cycle tables and the Position knob morphs across them with 4-point Hermite interpolation. Per-voice TPT state-variable filter, dual ADSR (amp + filter), two LFOs, soft drive, and constant-power stereo spread. 433 factory banks shipped under /var/lib/tonepi/wavetables. Mono DI in, stereo out.

Each step plays (root + offset) from the same sample bank, so pattern notes follow the played octave. Offset = 0 is the root; SKIP slots produce silence.

Telemetry.description: Detects digital clipping (samples at or above threshold). Passthrough — does not modify audio. Reports clip count and headroom via bargraphs.
Telemetry.name: Clip Detector

params.desc: Amplitude above which a sample is considered clipping
params.label: Threshold

Telemetry.usage: After drive/amp: Check if your gain staging is causing clipping. Threshold: Default 0.95 catches near-clips. Set to 1.0 for true digital full-scale only.

Telemetry.description: Detects DC offset in the signal. Passthrough — does not modify audio. Reports the average (DC) component and AC RMS via bargraphs. Non-zero DC means something upstream is adding a constant offset.
Telemetry.name: DC Offset Detector
Telemetry.usage: After effects: Some effects (especially asymmetric clipping) can introduce DC offset. Reading: DC value near 0 is healthy. Values above 0.01 indicate a problem — add a DC Blocker block.

Telemetry.description: Professional audio meter via C ffunction. True RMS (sliding window), ballistic peak with decay, 4x oversampled true peak (EBU R128), and VU-style 300ms integration. Passthrough — does not modify audio. Writes directly to shared memory for lowest-latency telemetry. Stereo: independent L/R metering.
Telemetry.name: Jack Meter

params.desc: RMS averaging window. 50ms=responsive, 300ms=stable, 500ms=smooth
params.label: RMS Window

Telemetry.usage: After drive: Check actual peak levels and true peak (inter-sample) for clipping. Before/after amp: Compare RMS levels to verify gain staging. Stereo: L and R metered independently — check balance and stereo spread. VU meter: Shows VU-ballistic level matching analog VU meter behavior (300ms integration). True peak: 4x oversampled — catches inter-sample peaks that digital peak meters miss.

Telemetry.description: Signal level meter. Passthrough — does not modify audio. Reports RMS and peak levels via FAUST bargraph metadata. Use to monitor signal levels at any point in the chain.
Telemetry.name: Level Meter

params.desc: RMS averaging window in milliseconds
params.label: Window

Telemetry.usage: After drive: Check if your drive is clipping the output. Before amp: Verify input level is in the right range for the amp model. End of chain: Monitor final output level.

Telemetry.description: Peak level detector with configurable hold time. Passthrough — does not modify audio. Reports the highest peak seen within the hold window.
Telemetry.name: Peak Hold

params.desc: How long to hold the peak value before decaying
params.label: Hold Time

Telemetry.usage: Clipping check: Set hold to 2000ms. If peak exceeds 0dB, you have clipping. Dynamic range: Watch the peak over time to gauge your signal dynamics.

Telemetry.description: Debug signal probe. Passthrough — does not modify audio. Reports current sample value, min, max, and RMS via bargraphs. Use to inspect signal characteristics at any point in the chain.
Telemetry.name: Signal Probe
Telemetry.usage: Between blocks: Insert to see what levels are flowing between processing stages. Debug NaN/clip: If min/max show extreme values, something upstream is broken. Signal presence: RMS near -80dB means no signal is reaching this point.

Telemetry.description: FFT spectrum analyzer. 4096-point Hann-windowed FFT giving 2048 frequency bins (~11.7Hz resolution at 48kHz). Threaded FFT — computation runs in a background thread, audio thread only accumulates samples. Passthrough — does not modify audio. Logic Pro-style frequency curve display.
Telemetry.name: Spectrum Analyzer

params.desc: 0=instant (noisy), 0.7=smooth (default), 0.95=very slow decay
params.label: Smoothing

params.desc: FFT update interval. 50ms=responsive, 100ms=balanced, 200ms=low CPU
params.label: Interval

Telemetry.usage: After EQ: See the spectral effect of your EQ settings. After amp: Visualize harmonic content and distortion character. Before/after: Place two analyzers to compare spectral changes via overlay. Smoothing: Higher values give a calmer display, lower values are more responsive. Interval: How often FFT is computed. 50ms=responsive, 100ms=lower CPU.

Telemetry.description: Chromatic tuner via zero-crossing rate pitch estimation. Passthrough — does not modify audio. Reports estimated frequency via bargraph. Best with single notes, clean signal.
Telemetry.name: Tuner

params.desc: Signal must exceed this threshold for pitch detection to activate
params.label: Gate

Telemetry.usage: Start of chain: Place before any effects for cleanest pitch detection. Reading: Frequency bargraph shows detected Hz. Compare to standard tuning (E2=82Hz, A=440Hz, etc.).

Utility.description: Adaptive Line Enhancer for mains hum. NLMS predictor at one mains-period delay learns the periodic hum component and subtracts it. Adaptation freezes during loud signal so held notes survive. Place after Input Calibration for best results.
Utility.name: Adaptive Hum Killer

params.desc: Mains frequency (50 or 60 Hz).
params.label: Mains

params.desc: NLMS predictor length. 4 is plenty for pure mains; bump for SMPS-rich environments.
params.label: Taps

params.desc: Upper frequency the ALE operates on. Above this, the signal bypasses the predictor — prevents comb-filter coloration of high-frequency content.
params.label: Band Limit

params.desc: NLMS step size. Larger = faster adaptation but more ringing on transients.
params.label: Adapt Rate

params.desc: Adaptation freezes when envelope is above this level (held-note guard).
params.label: Freeze Thresh

params.desc: Wet/dry. 1.0 = full hum subtraction.
params.label: Mix

Utility.usage: Setup: Place after Input Calibration (or wherever the hum first becomes objectionable). Use the bypass to A/B. Mains: 60 Hz for North America/Asia, 50 Hz for EU/UK/AU. Adapt rate: Higher = faster convergence but more transient ringing. 0.001 is a safe default. Freeze threshold: Envelope above this freezes the predictor so held notes don't get learned. -30 dBFS works for most pickups; lower if your noise floor is itself hot, higher if you want adaptation to keep running into quiet sustain. Mix: Wet/dry blend. 1.0 = full subtraction. Pull back if the predictor is taking out too much pickup texture.

Utility.description: Wideband-RMS leveller / loudness normalizer with look-ahead, peak limiter, and tilt EQ. Two modes: Headroom (fast, after high-gain amps) and Mastering (slow, end of chain). Transient hold, noise gate, soft-clip safety.
Utility.name: Auto Gain

params.desc: Target level, read on whichever scale Metric selects: dBFS when Metric=0 (same scale as the jack meter), LUFS when Metric=1. The two are NOT interchangeable - K-weighting reads well below flat on cab output, so a value tuned for one metric must be re-set for the other. Typical LUFS targets: -14 streaming, -16 podcast, -23 EBU R128 broadcast.
params.label: Target

params.desc: Loudness window. 100ms=very-fast/snappy, 500ms=headroom, 3s=phrase, 5s=balanced, 10s=glacial. Below ~200 ms the long-window RMS gets noisy.
params.label: Window

params.desc: Gain reduce speed. 50-200ms = compressor-like (can pump), 500ms = headroom, 2s+ = mastering/slow.
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Gain boost speed. 50-200ms = fast (can pump on quiet -> loud transitions), 500ms = headroom, 2s+ = mastering/slow.
params.label: Release

params.desc: Maximum gain boost/cut. 12=normal, 18=broadcast, 24=extreme range.
params.label: Max Gain

params.desc: Where the playing's peaks may reach. The gain ride stops short of pushing ordinary peaks (the 99th percentile of 10 ms block peaks over the last few seconds) more than Max Squash past this, so Target is reached only when the peaks leave room for it; otherwise the block settles quieter and keeps the dynamics. A 1 ms look-ahead limiter enforces it for the peaks above that. Applies at AG's output only -- downstream chorus/delay/reverb can add peaks, so place AG last for a chain ceiling.
params.label: Peak Ceiling

params.desc: 0=dBFS (flat RMS, matches the jack meter), 1=LUFS (ITU-R BS.1770 K-weighted loudness). K-weighting reads ~10-15 dB below flat on guitar-cab material, so Target must be re-set when you change this — a -14 target means -14 dBFS in one mode and -14 LUFS in the other. Switching restarts the measurement window.
params.label: Metric

params.desc: -1=darker, 0=neutral, +1=brighter. Spectral tilt EQ at 1kHz pivot (±6dB).
params.label: Tilt

params.desc: 0=off (default), 1=on. Remembers the largest BOOST the block has applied and restores it the instant the noise gate re-opens, so a phrase resuming after silence starts at the level the block had already worked out instead of climbing from 0 dB at the Attack/Release rate (seconds, at mastering settings). Boost only — cuts are never remembered. The maximum is all-time: it is not decayed over a long silence and is cleared only when the chain is rebuilt, so one very quiet passage sets the level every later re-entry starts from. Restore is re-clamped to the live Max Gain.
params.label: Gain Memory

params.desc: How much the limiter may cut ORDINARY picking to reach Target. The gain ride never asks for more, so this is the natural-vs-squashed control: 0 = never limit typical peaks (only catch the odd over), 3 = transparent on most material, 6+ = audibly compressed, like the old behaviour when Target sat close to Peak Ceiling.
params.label: Max Squash

Utility.usage: After high-gain amp: Use Post-Amp Headroom preset. Creates headroom for downstream cab/delay/reverb. End of chain: Use Program Normalize. Slow, transparent level matching. Target: measured as wideband RMS on the same dBFS scale as the jack meter. -12 to -18 dBFS is typical for guitar; -24 dBFS is broadcast. Window: 500ms=headroom (faster), 3-5s=mastering (phrase-level), 10s=glacial. Transient hold: Gain freezes during pick attacks (3× RMS, 200ms hold). Peak Ceiling + Max Squash: the gain ride takes the SMALLER of what reaches Target and what keeps ordinary peaks within Ceiling + Max Squash, so a clean tone gets as loud as its peaks allow instead of being limited flat. Raise Max Squash for more level at the cost of dynamics. Place AG last for a chain ceiling. Tilt: +0.3=brighter, -0.3=warmer. ±6dB spectral tilt at 1kHz. Gain Memory: Off by default. On, the block remembers its largest boost and restores it the moment the gate re-opens, so a phrase after a pause starts at the worked-out level instead of climbing from 0 dB. Most useful with slow Attack/Release, where that climb takes seconds. Boost only, all-time, cleared on chain rebuild.

Utility.description: Band-pass filter. Passes frequencies around the center, cuts above and below.
Utility.name: Band Pass

params.desc: Filter cutoff frequency in Hz
params.label: Center

params.desc: Resonance width. Low=wide, high=narrow/resonant
params.label: Q

Utility.usage: Vocal range: Center=1000Hz, Q=2. Isolates the vocal/guitar midrange. Resonant: Center=800Hz, Q=8. Narrow, wah-like fixed filter.

Utility.description: Micro-freeze / hold buffer. Captures the last Size ms of audio into a circular buffer. While Hold=On the buffer loops indefinitely; while Hold=Off the live signal passes through (with Size ms of latency). Hold transitions are crossfaded (Smooth) to avoid clicks. Use Mix to blend the frozen loop against live for parallel pad textures.
Utility.name: Buffer Freeze

params.desc: Off=live signal passes through (Size ms latency). On=loop the captured buffer.
params.label: Hold

params.desc: Capture window length. 100=single note stutter, 500=chord, 1500=full riff
params.label: Size

params.desc: Hold transition crossfade. Fast=2 ms (immediate, can click), Smooth=10 ms (clean)
params.label: Smooth

params.desc: Wet/dry blend. 1=full freeze replaces live, 0.5=loop underneath live, 0=bypass
params.label: Mix

Utility.usage: Chord freeze: Size=500 ms, Smooth=Smooth. Strike a chord, toggle Hold to sustain it forever. Phrase capture: Size=1500 ms. Long enough for a whole riff to loop. Short stab: Size=100 ms. Stuttery loop of a single note attack. Ambient bed: Size=1000 ms, Mix=0.4, Hold=On. Blend a drone underneath live playing. Trigger: Toggle Hold On/Off to capture / release. Assign it to a footswitch via hooks for performance use. Latency note: When Hold=Off the buffer still delays the signal by Size ms — place AFTER cab/NAM so the delay doesn't compound into the tone colour.

Utility.description: DC blocker. Removes DC offset from the signal.
Utility.name: DC Blocker
Utility.usage: Place after any block that might produce DC offset (preamps, saturators). Removes sub-audio drift without affecting audible frequencies.

Utility.description: Finds howling monitor feedback and parks a narrow notch on it. Requires prominence, persistence AND steadiness together, so a sustained sung note with vibrato is left alone.
Utility.name: Feedback Hunter

params.desc: How far a band must stand above its neighbours to be a candidate.
params.label: Sensitivity

params.desc: Maximum depth of each notch.
params.label: Depth

params.desc: Notch narrowness. High = surgical, less audible on the voice.
params.label: Q

params.desc: How long a candidate must persist before a notch is placed. The main defence against notching a held note.
params.label: Hold

params.desc: How little a band may wander and still count as feedback. Vibrato pushes a sung note above this; a feedback loop stays below it.
params.label: Steadiness

params.desc: Stop hunting and keep the current notches.
params.label: Freeze

params.desc: How many notches may be active at once.
params.label: Max Notches

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Utility.usage: Ring out the monitors with this active — it will park notches on the room modes. Then set Freeze so it stops hunting during the show and keeps what it found. Notching your held notes? Raise Hold (it must persist longer) or lower Steadiness (a sung note wanders more than feedback does). Too slow to catch a howl? Lower Hold — at the cost of more false positives.

Utility.description: Plays a WAV or FLAC file through the signal chain. Used by Tone Match for A/B testing — the target recording plays through JACK alongside your live signal. Control: 0=stop, 1=play, 2=pause.
Utility.name: File Player

params.desc: 0=stop, 1=play, 2=pause
params.label: State

params.desc: Output level in dB
params.label: Level

Utility.usage: Tone Match A/B: Added automatically in a parallel lane. Press Target to hear the reference, press Chain to hear your matched rig. Manual use: Add to chain, set the file path in the preset, and control playback via the state parameter.

Utility.name: Gain

params.desc: Negative=cut, 0=unity, positive=boost
params.label: Gain

Utility.usage: Trim: Set to match levels between blocks. Boost: Positive dB to push the next stage harder. Cut: Negative dB to reduce level before a sensitive block.

Utility.description: Hard pan. Routes mono or stereo signal to left or right channel only.
Utility.name: Hard Pan

params.desc: 0=hard left, 1=hard right
params.label: Pan (0=L, 1=R)

Utility.usage: Hard left: Pan=0. Signal goes entirely to left channel. Hard right: Pan=1. Signal goes entirely to right channel. Use in parallel paths to create stereo from mono sources.

Utility.description: High-pass filter. Removes frequencies below the cutoff.
Utility.name: High Pass

params.desc: Filter cutoff frequency in Hz
params.label: Frequency

Utility.usage: Rumble filter: Freq=80Hz. Removes sub-bass rumble and handling noise. Bass cut: Freq=200Hz. Tightens signal before a drive pedal.

Utility.description: Low-pass filter. Removes frequencies above the cutoff.
Utility.name: Low Pass

params.desc: Filter cutoff frequency in Hz
params.label: Frequency

Utility.usage: Treble rolloff: Freq=5000Hz. Smooths harsh signals. Dark filter: Freq=2000Hz. Lo-fi, distant, telephone effect.

Utility.description: 6-band downward expander with per-band noise-floor learning during silence. Targets the band-specific noise (hiss plateau) without coloring guitar body.
Utility.name: Noise Carver (6-band)

params.desc: Global envelope below this counts as silent (eligible for learning).
params.label: Silence Thresh

params.desc: Continuous silence required before per-band noise learning starts.
params.label: Min Silence

params.desc: Max attenuation per band when it sits at its noise floor.
params.label: Depth

params.desc: dB above noise floor at which the band fully opens (linear soft knee).
params.label: Open Margin

params.desc: Per-band gain attack time.
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Per-band gain release time.
params.label: Release

params.desc: Wet/dry blend of carved vs original.
params.label: Mix

Utility.usage: Workflow: Set Silence Threshold just above your noise floor (-50 dBFS is a sane default). Mute the guitar for >= Min Silence (default 500 ms) and the block silently learns the per-band noise floor. Resume playing - each band's gain expands above its own noise floor. Bands: Fixed crossovers at 150 / 500 / 1500 / 3000 / 6000 Hz. The critical band for guitar hiss is the 1.5-3 kHz one. Depth: Max attenuation per band when it sits at its noise floor. -15 dB is gentle; -24 dB is aggressive. Threshold above floor: How many dB the band envelope must exceed its noise floor to fully open. 6 dB = aggressive (small margin), 12 dB = transparent (large margin, less surgical). Attack / Release: Per-band gain smoothing. Short attack catches transients; long release lets sustained notes ring cleanly. Confidence guard: Internal - learning rate decays after several silence windows so a brief 100 ms gap doesn't overwrite a well-learned floor. Pickup switch -> the residual will rise -> confidence is not automatically reset in v1 (toggle bypass briefly to reset). Bypass: Use the block card's standard toggle.

Utility.description: Does nothing. Fills an empty parallel lane so the lane has a node to hold its mix level and bypass.
Utility.name: Passthrough
Utility.usage: Dry lane: Drop it into an empty parallel lane to make that lane an explicit dry path you can level and mute. Placeholder: Reserve a slot you intend to fill later without changing the sound. No parameters: Output is bit-identical to input.

Utility.description: Post-amp residual VCA with three-state pre-arm machine. Suppresses chain noise floor between notes; pre-arms back to OPEN during confirmed silence for zero-latency attack response. MIDI sidecar overrides instantly when notes held.
Utility.name: Sidecar VCA

params.desc: Envelope below this for Hold ms starts the close transition.
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: Envelope below this (deeper) for Confirm ms pre-opens vca.
params.label: Pre-Arm Thresh

params.desc: Attenuation in ATTENUATE state.
params.label: Depth

params.desc: PASSTHRU -> ATTENUATE delay. Long hold protects natural decays from being clipped.
params.label: Hold

params.desc: ATTENUATE -> PRE_ARMED delay (must be in deep silence).
params.label: Confirm

params.desc: Gain smoothing on opening transitions.
params.label: Attack

params.desc: Gain smoothing on closing transition. Longer = less audible attenuation snap.
params.label: Release

params.desc: Envelope follower attack.
params.label: Env Attack

params.desc: Envelope follower release. Longer = slower close, better legato preservation.
params.label: Env Release

params.desc: 1 = MIDI note activity forces vca OPEN. 0 = audio envelope only.
params.label: MIDI Sidecar

params.desc: In ATTENUATE state: 1.0=off, 2-6=musical taper, ≥50=hard gate. Defaults to 4 (3:1) — smooth fade-out of noise tail as notes decay.
params.label: Ratio

Utility.usage: Where to place: AFTER your amp/cab, AFTER any reverb/delay tails you want preserved. Put your noise_gate2 BEFORE the amp (so it sees clean input) and this block AFTER. Between this and the cab/reverb is fine. Threshold: Envelope must drop below this (dBFS) for Hold ms to start closing. Aim 6-10 dB below your typical playing level. -45 dBFS is a sane default. Pre-Arm Thresh: Envelope must drop below THIS deeper threshold for Confirm ms before vca pre-opens. Set 15-25 dB below Threshold (so -70 dBFS for a -45 dB threshold). Only met when the upstream noise gate has truly killed signal. Hold ms: How long signal must stay below Threshold before vca closes. Short (50-150 ms) makes the residue suppression kick in quickly; long (300-500 ms) avoids closing on natural decay tails. Confirm ms: How long signal must stay below Pre-Arm Thresh before vca pre-opens. 200-500 ms. Depth: How much to attenuate in ATTENUATE state. -20 dB is gentle; -36 dB hides the noise floor entirely. Linear in dB. Attack / Release: Smoothing on the vca gain. Attack on opening, release on closing. Keep attack short (5-10 ms) so the vca opens before the first note hits when MIDI sidecar fires. Env Attack / Release: Envelope follower coefficients. Defaults work for guitar (2 ms / 60 ms). MIDI Sidecar: When ON, any Tripleplay note forces vca OPEN immediately (zero detection latency). Turn OFF if you're not using a MIDI controller. Bypass: Use the block card's standard toggle.

Utility.description: FFT-based spectral-subtraction noise reduction. Edge-trigger Learn while only the noise floor is playing - the block captures a 40-frame profile and starts subtracting it from every subsequent frame.
Utility.name: Spectral NR

params.desc: Below this signal level the subtraction is fully active
params.label: Threshold

params.desc: Maximum bin-level attenuation (dB)
params.label: Reduction

params.desc: Oversubtraction factor (1=literal, higher=aggressive)
params.label: Alpha

params.desc: Spectral floor - prevents musical-noise artefacts. Clamped >= 0.05
params.label: Beta

params.desc: Rising-edge: toggle 0->1 while only noise plays to capture a fresh profile. Returning to 0 keeps applying the learned profile.
params.label: Learn (0/1)

Utility.usage: Workflow: Mute the guitar (or pull the patch cable), then toggle Learn 0 -> 1. EDGE-TRIGGERED: a single rising edge captures a 40-frame profile and starts applying it. The slider can be returned to 0 immediately - the learned profile persists. To re-learn (different pickup position, different noise), toggle 1 -> 0 -> 1. Threshold: Below this signal level the subtraction is fully active; above it the signal passes more transparently. For hum-while-playing reduction set near -10 dB. Reduction: Max attenuation per bin. Higher = more cleaning, more chance of artifacts. Alpha: Oversubtraction factor - 1.0 = literal subtract, 2-3 = aggressive. Beta: Spectral floor (post-subtract minimum, prevents musical noise). Clamped >= 0.05. Bypass: Use the block card's standard bypass toggle. There is no inner bypass slider - the per-block one handles it.

Utility.description: Stereo widener with 3 modes. Modern: multi-band mid-side, mono-compatible — bass stays mono, selected band widens. Classic: Haas delay (NOT mono-compatible) — simple delay on right channel. Stereoizer: multiband frequency-selective widening — bass mono, mids moderate, highs full width. Modern and Stereoizer are mono-safe (L+R = 2×dry).
Utility.name: Stereo Enhancer

params.desc: 0=Modern (M-S band), 1=Classic (Haas delay), 2=Stereoizer (multiband)
params.label: Mode

params.desc: Stereo spread. 0=mono, 0.5=moderate, 1=maximum L/R decorrelation
params.label: Width

params.desc: Modern mode: lower bound of widening band. Below = mono bass
params.label: LoCut

params.desc: Modern mode: upper bound of widening band. Above = mono air
params.label: HiCut

params.desc: Classic mode: right channel delay. 5ms=subtle, 15ms=strong. NOT mono-safe
params.label: Delay

params.desc: Stereoizer mode: how far widening extends into lower frequencies
params.label: Depth

params.desc: 0=dry bypass, 0.8=default, 1=full effect
params.label: Mix

Utility.usage: Modern (default): Mode=0, Width=0.5. Mono-compatible widening. LoCut keeps bass central. Classic Haas: Mode=1, Delay=5ms. Simple stereo from delay. NOT mono-safe — live stereo only. Stereoizer: Mode=2, Depth=0.5. Frequency-selective: bass mono, mids moderate, highs wide. Mono compatibility: Modern and Stereoizer cancel perfectly in mono sum. Classic does NOT. Recording: Use Modern or Stereoizer. For live stereo rigs: Classic is fine.

Utility.description: Native-C M-S width control with sub-200 Hz mono-sum. Width=1 leaves the image unchanged; <1 narrows, >1 widens. Bass below 200 Hz is always mono so the result stays mono-compatible (no phase cancellation on a single-speaker playback).
Utility.name: Stereo Width

params.desc: Stereo width. 0=mono sum, 1=unchanged, 2=double-wide
params.label: Width

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass (0/1)

Utility.usage: Width: 1.0 = unchanged, 0.0 = full mono sum, 2.0 = double-wide. Smoothed 5 ms tau. Bass mono: Side channel is HP'd at 200 Hz before the width scale — sub-200 Hz stays mono regardless. Mono-compatible. Mono input: If the chain hasn't gone stereo yet (L=R), the side channel is zero and the width knob has no audible effect. Use it after a parallel split or a stereo widener.

Utility.description: Time-domain noise template subtractor. Snapshots the noise waveform during qualified silence; subtracts the looped template phase-locked to mains during play. Confidence-gated learning protects established templates from short silence bursts; auto-reset on pickup change.
Utility.name: Template Subtractor

params.desc: Envelope must be below this to count as silent. Set just above your real noise floor.
params.label: Silence Thresh

params.desc: Continuous silence required before template learning starts.
params.label: Min Silence

params.desc: Mains frequency (50 EU/UK/AU, 60 NA/Asia).
params.label: Mains

params.desc: Template length in mains periods. 4 is a good default; bump for slower-varying patterns.
params.label: Periods

params.desc: Wet/dry. 1.0 = full subtraction.
params.label: Mix

params.desc: 0=active, 1=bypass
params.label: Bypass

Utility.usage: Place EARLY in the chain (before pre-gain / distortion) so it cancels noise at its lowest level. Silence Thresh: Envelope below this counts as silent for learning. Default -50 dBFS. Set just above your real noise floor (see jack_meter RMS). Min Silence: How long the input must be continuously silent before the template starts updating. Default 500 ms - prevents a brief gap between notes from overwriting a well-learned template. Mains: 50 (EU/UK/AU) or 60 (NA/Asia). Wrong setting means the template won't lock to your noise cycle. Template Periods: Length of the captured waveform = N x mains period. 4 (default) = ~67 ms at 60 Hz - catches fundamental + first few harmonics + slow drift. Higher = catches longer quasi-periodic patterns but converges slower. Mix: 0 = full passthrough, 1 = full subtraction. Pull back if the cancellation is taking out signal texture. Confidence: Auto-managed. Builds up across silence windows. When you switch pickups the residual blows up and confidence resets - template re-learns within a few silence windows.

Utility.description: Stereo to mono converter. Select left, right, or sum.
Utility.name: To Mono

params.desc: 0=left only, 1=right only, 2=sum (L+R)/2
params.label: Mode (0=L, 1=R, 2=Sum)

Utility.usage: Left only: Mode=0. Keeps only the left stereo channel. Right only: Mode=1. Keeps only the right channel. Sum: Mode=2. Mixes L+R to mono (halved to avoid clipping).
